ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ISP provider limits number of sent messages :-(
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Francis, Thanks for raising this issue. I'm not really sure whether this is something that we can easily, or should really fix within Moodle. To be honest, it seems that your host has implemented this rate limiting in a strange way. It is the job of the Mail Transfer Agent (MTA) to transfer the messages you pass it  to the next point in the queue. If the MTA is unable to deliver them immediately, it is *meant* to queue them until such a time that it can send them. Moodle does not handle these kinds of failures well - it has no way of doing so as it was never really designed with this in mind. In the case of forum emails, we have a single flag for each discussion - if you have 100 users subscribed to the same discussion, we only mark that discussion as sent once - not once per user. If you really want to hack Moodle to do this, then you can do so - it is Open Source after all, but this is not a change that I would be keen to support. The easiest way to hack this into Moodle is to edit lib/moodlelib.php - Find this line: https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/v2.9.1/lib/moodlelib.php#L5657 , and just before the "return true;" line, add a sleep(2). As I say, I don't think that Moodle is the best place to perform this kind of rate limiting, and that you should persuade your host to re-consider the way in which they rate limit e-mail. Perhaps they could whitelist certain domains for example. Hope this helps, Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ISP provider limits number of sent messages :-(
ResponsesInList.Text: Andrew, your post made me think about several other alternatives, in addition to what I mentioned above. 1) On my small Moodle, I stagger due dates for discussions among courses.  I could easily make all discussions for (let's say, 5) courses due on Friday evening.  However, many of the students like to wait until the last moment to make posts, which can then overwhelm my server 's email limits.  Instead, I make posts for one or two courses due Friday night, then for another course Thursday night, then for another course Sunday night, etc.  I think you get the idea. 2) You can encourage students to switch their "email digest type" to "daily emails".  This will consolidate all of the daily posts into one email.  I am unsure if this can be made the default within Moodle, but many students often prefer this setting (although I do not).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ISP provider limits number of sent messages :-(
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rick, Thanks for those suggestions - also good options. It's a shame when it's one point in the chain which makes things difficult like this. Your post has however reminded me why this cannot be done in Moodle, even with the best will in the world. Sometimes we do send e-mails based on a direct user interaction (and not cron). One example of this is when sending messages to multiple users using the participants listing. This will be affected by the suggested change - perfect, that's what we want. However, if your site is more active, and five of your teachers send messages at the same time, then they may still hit that rate limit and have messages rejected. Web applications are not a single thread. There may be 1 connection, but just as easily there may be 1,000. If each of those connections sends an e-mail at the same time, that sleep hack won't work. Andrew

ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for your understanding Francis, I agree, adding a two-second sleep does have the potential to cause other problems. I imagine that it will also increase the load on the server unnecessarily. With regards your question about cron, this should not matter. Most of the mailing in Moodle is written with this in mind. For example, with regards forum e-mails, we mark a forum post as having been mailed out before we mail out. This means that if cron fails during the send, then some users may not receive messages, but at the same time it means that others do not receive duplicates. In some cases, if a failure is repeatable (e.g. something wrong with a user account causes an exception to be thrown), this loop may never end. Hope that this helps, and good luck with your SMTP service, Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 'Mail now' does not immediately sent notifications to forum subscribers
ResponsesInList.Text: I think that "mail now" is a bit of misnomer... As far as I know, this means that instead of respecting the forum-specific delay for mailing a given post, it is added to the mail queue right away. The mail queue will be processed at the next cron run, whenever that occurs. That means that there can still be a delay until the mail actually goes out. For example, if your forum is set to allow editing of posts for 20 mins and cron runs every 5 mins, "mail now" means that your mail will go out within 5 mins instead of within 25 mins. Caveat: there were some substantial changes with regards to cron in the recent versions of Moodle, which may affect this, but probably not or not significantly. If the understanding is not the issue, there may be a technical problem with the scheduling of mail-now mails on your site. There have been a few threads about different technical issues. Search the forum.

With forum subscription set to Optional subscription, Moodle *should* check back with the participant's User profile preferences.  If the preference is not to be subscribed, the participant should not be subscribed to any forum threads.  If the preference is to be subscribed, then participants should start out being subscribed to all discussion threads, and can opt-out if they want.  Except that the behaviour I'm seeing on my Moodle 2.8.3+ (Build: 20150212) site is that regardless of preference, participants start out subscribed to all threads, and can opt-out.  Making optional subscription mode no different to auto-subscription mode. Is this intentional?  Have I misunderstood something? All the best, Lindy (@moodlechick)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum discussion thread subscription behaviour - just checkin
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Lindy, So with auto-subscription, yes. Students start out subscribed to all discussions but can opt-out of either forum subscription, or per-discussion subscription as the choose. With optional subscription, Moodle does not subscribe them by default at all. This has never been the case. The profile setting determines the default setting when a user replies to a discussion. That's to say that when a forum is in Optional subscription, and replies to a discussion they have not taken part in before, this is where the profile preference comes in. It either defaults to subscribing them to the discussion, or remaining unsubscribed. So there should be a difference between Optional and Automatic subscription. However , if you take an existing forum and change it from Automatic to Optional then the existing subscriptions will remain in place until a user unsubscribes. Any new user will not be subscribed. Just to be clear, when you create and Automatic forum, under the hood it subscribes every user in the course to that forum and they gain a subscription setting. Hope that clarifies things, Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Need help configuring forum's "Reply to post" feature.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Willem, So everything looks like it's correctly configured. I don't suppose you have access to the cron logs? Moodle uses a scheduled task to make the connection to your IMAP server , to fetch the mail, process it, and post it. If there's a problem retrieving the message, then you will see it in the cron logs. Sadly we don't (yet) have a way of storing these automatically in Moodle, and you will need to setup your own cron logging if you don't have it already. Hopefully this should give an idea as to what's going wrong and where. Incidentally, the mail checker will only fetch messages from the inbox , which have not been read , and have not been flagged/starred . The act of reading the messages in your mail client will mean that they are not picked up by the mail fetcher. This is something that you may encounter during testing and should be aware of. The reason that Moodle asks you to remove the original message when replying is because it doesn't (yet) remove the original content. There is an issue open to do this, but it's extremely hard to get right - I could go into detail if you like, but suffice to say that Apple and Google have closed patents on how they do this for a reason. Let me know what your cron output looks like and we can continue the diagnosis from there. Best wishes, Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Need help configuring forum's "Reply to post" feature.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Willem, We do make an attempt to capture these. Chances are you have a client which is not defining various headers. Are you able to grab the headers from such a reply and to provide more information on the client? Perhaps you could open an issue with this information? When we send messages from Moodle, we add certain headers to tell clients and MTAs not to reply because it's an automated message (see them at https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/master/mod/forum/lib.php#L744 ) . When we receive messages back, we have a look for certain headers which common clients set in an attempt to ignore them (see those at https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/master/admin/tool/messageinbound/classes/manager.php#L751 ). Unfortunately there is no fixed standard for either the outbound or the inbound headers. We've catered to all of the cases we could find, but clients which are going off the beaten path will cause issues. We can address them on an individual basis, but there is no perfect cure short of a standard being perfectly implemented by all MTAs and clients... Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Disabling Forum
ResponsesInList.Text: Considering admins can do everything on a site I doubt you can. You could possibly delete the forum and badges and create a modified admin role but that role would be severely limited I would think.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Disabling Forum
ResponsesInList.Text: There is another way, and I think it is likely to be more successful, and cleaner... In Permissions go through all the Roles and ensure that the capabilities to create, delete, view, edit, post, save and reply are all set to Deny, or Prohibit. Start with Administrator and then work downward. I seem to recall that that capability is "Inherited", so if Admins role has it on Prohibit, that should apply all the way through..but don't take my word for it. You can also deactivate the forum plugin. If you want specific people to be able to access a forum, then create a new Role, and give that Role to those people.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Disabling Forum
ResponsesInList.Text: You can't deactivate the forum module. It's the only module you can't delete or hide because of the major role it plays in the social constructionist approach to learning upon which Moodle is based.  Look at Site administration>Plugins>Activity modules>Manage activities and you will see what I mean. You can deny the permission of teachers to add a forum and other users to access it, as has been mentioned above, but admins can by default "do anything" so if you mean the site admin, they will still be able to add forums if they want.  (I don't know what happens if you try to remove the forum module from your server ; I;m not going to try )

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hide a quiz once completed
ResponsesInList.Text: MyMoodle can be a bit clumsy for this. Sometimes a better way is In each course that should be counted, turn on completion tracking and set a completion criterion For each credential that is composed of multiple courses, create a course to hold the overview, turn on completion tracking, and add completion criteria including completion of each pre-requisite course. The advantage of this approach is that you can enrol each student for any number of credentials, and get separate completion lists for each. You may choose to give recognition for prior learning this way. You can regulate enrolment in the credential separately from enrolment in the component courses, or you can use meta-courses/child-courses to automatically enrol students. Completion tracking is described here - http://kb.moodlerooms.com/article/27/administrator

ResponsesInList.Title: Subscribing a Group to a Forum
ResponsesInList.Text: We are trying to figure out how to force subscribe a group to a forum without subscribing all of the other users in the course (instructors, content assistants, etc.).  We have the forum set to group mode and assigned only the group that we want to have the email notifications, but it still subscribes and notifies all users. ResponsesInList.Title: Svar: Subscribing a Group to a Forum
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Frances, we have the same problem and I wrote an issue about that in the Moodle Tracker . https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-41677 We resolved it as follows: a general forum for each group settings: "available for group members only"; separate groups choose the forum choose "show/edit current subscribers" turn editing on add the users you want to be subscribers there is an old thread about the issue https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=26282 including: " Let me clarify confusion about Force subscription. Subscription is the feature that sends ALL posts from a forum to ALL course users. It does not recognize groups. ALL posts in a forum go to ALL course users, always. There is NO way for a group to receive via email ONLY the posts of others in his/her group. This means that forums must be checked manually be students, since they will not be receiving email notification of a new forum post. So, if you are using Separate Groups in a Forum, set Force everyone to be subscribed to 'Subscriptions not allowed'. In my opinion it should work in another way as I discribed in the tracker/simon

ResponsesInList.Title: Email account for "Reply to forum via email" feature
ResponsesInList.Text: We are currently looking into setting up the forthcoming Moodle 2.8 installations with 'Reply to forum via email' feature. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Email account for "Reply to forum via email" feature
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Chris, It does need to be a unique e-mail account for each Moodle instance. Each e-mail address should be pretty unique, but we can't tell whether the address belongs to this Moodle or another. When the pickup task runs, it reads each e-mail in the Inbox. It marks it as read, stars it, an then processes it. If it does not validate (wrong address, wrong token, unknown id, etc.) then it is moved to a different mailbox and the user may be informed. This process will render each message unavailable for another site. There is no way around this limitation. Hope this helps, Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Manager can't change forum subscription settings in 2.8
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, having upgraded to 2.8 I'm finding that a manager can't adjust his/her subscription prefs in a forum, am i missing something here? It's very important for me that they can subscribe to forums. Lal

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Manager can't change forum subscription settings in 2.8
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Lal, I've just tested this out on one of my own sites, and the Manager role is able to change their subscription settings on an individual thread, or across a whole forum, where the forum is in optional or auto-subscription mode.  Obviously, if subscription is disabled, no one can subscribe.  If subscription is forced, it should not impact the manager role, as by default the capability for allowing a user to be force subscribed is "Not set" for the manager role - see here: https://docs.moodle.org/28/en/Capabilities/mod/forum:allowforcesubscribe My suggestion would be check the subscription setting on the forum, and the permissions of the manager role on your site.  You'll want the "Manage subscriptions" capability set to "Allow".  Remember too that permissions for roles can be adjusted at site, course category, and individual activity level. Hope this helps! All the best, Lindy (@moodlechick)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Email to forum | Position of message
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Derek, This was changed in core in MDL-48227 and to change the location of the message you would need to modify code I'm afraid. We made the change because many email clients (mobile in particular) were showing the "--If replying..." text as the preview of the message, thus making the preview particularly useless. At around the same time, Ankit also designed a new way of adding this kind of information to outbound messages. Sadly this is master-only, but it may be of interest to you for 2.9. You can see it in action at https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/master/mod/forum/lib.php#L789 When 2.9 comes out, you will be able to move the text from the footer to the header by changing that 'footer' key to read 'header'. If you feel it worthwhile to add the ability to swap them at will, perhaps you could add an issue to the tracker? Best wishes, Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Philosophising | email posts to forums
ResponsesInList.Text: Just curious.  Now we have had this function "Email to a forum" for a while: how are people finding it? Originally I was not in favour of this. Joseph's thoughts: http://www.moodlenews.com/2014/initial-thoughts-on-the-reply-to-forums-by-email-feature-for-moodle-its-awesome/ From the tracker: Christy Mattingly added a comment - 30/Jul/14 2:53 AM To address Derek Chirnside's question of "Why are we doing this?" there are a couple of benefits for users. A. For students or faculty who are commuters, they can use a smartphone to easily respond to a forum post via email. To this from a computer would require Internet connectivity and navigating Moodle from a SmartPhone is not as easy as sending email (which also happens to be the one software interface nearly all computer technology users are familiar with). B. Using email is easier to navigate than Moodle for those requiring screen readers due to sight impairments. C. When composing email messages, the post is automatically saved as a draft if connectivity is lost or the user gets distracted. In Moodle, the timeout setting can cause a post to be lost (although users can compose their post in a locally stored text processing program to avoid this issue, it is an extra insurance step many of them do not think to do plus it is less convenient). [This is seriously hidden in the tracker item here: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-3714 This post is an example of how teachers and geeks can survive on the same page, but teachers can have diffitulty. - this post is also a classic case of they wornderful synergy that is here for these projects, the attention do detail and robust thinking. IMO ] Email to forums: Where I am at: In response to Christy's thoughtful and courteous post above I changed my opinion. Yesterday I enabled this functionality on one of the big servers I work with.  [Easy to do, although I do have a question: is there any other way besides using the evil gmail? ] There was some negative response from some staff.  I'm surmising that the students AND tutors have got used to treating forum notifications like emails, and just click reply as opposed to Notification to go somewhere else and engage.  There is some sort of resistance to using the forums as a forum.  Unsubstantiated assertions, based on no scientific data. I wonder how people are using this.  I wonder how our students will like this. I wonder if we could benefit from a link "Reply direct to sender" but that is huge feature creep. So we shall see. -Derek

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Incoming mail reply-to forums not working with @gmail
ResponsesInList.Text: UPDATE: After a bit of reviewing the code in /mod/forum/lib.php and testing stuff out, I have a few findings below: Question for Andrew: Why did we move the reply-to email at the bottom of email body and not in the header? After spending 6 hours of troubleshooting time, I just couldn't figure out why the reply-to email was not coming through. I did a couple of things: Hardcoded $replyaddress variable on line: https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/MOODLE_28_STABLE/mod/forum/lib.php#L762 It seemed to work. I added a dummy plus address format email and it seems to work fine too. The reply to was coming through in the notifications. But the moment I remove the hard-coded email, the reply-to is complete missing in the notifications. Then i realized, according to some specs online, the reply-to should be present in the header. I added this line: $userfrom->customheaders[] = 'Reply-To: ' . $replyaddress; (immediately after line 763) and it all seems to work just fine! The reply-to is coming through the way it is supposed to. The reply by email is working. The posts are being posted correclty.(Tested using 4 different users and 4 different email addresses by different providers). I wonder why this is happening and what could be the reason behind this bizarre issue. Is it postfix? Do I need to configure it to pickup reply-to from the body of the email and not within the header? Remember, Postfix is what is sending these emails. I have gmail configured for IMAP in Incoming Mail Configuration. HELP! Even though what I did works perfectly for me, I don't want to modify the core code? Kind Regards, Mukarram

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Incoming mail reply-to forums not working with @gmail
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Mukarram We have only moved the text to the bottom of the email. The text does not perform any function other than information to the user. The reply-to address is indeed in the header. See https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/MOODLE_28_STABLE/mod/forum/lib.php#L788 - that sets the Reply-To in the userfrom field of the eventdata. The eventdata->replyto is eventually passed to message/output/email/message_output_email.php where it's then picked up and passed to email_to_user() as a parameter.  It's then added to the headers. If you have some charset conversion issues, it could be being nullified in https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/MOODLE_28_STABLE/lib/moodlelib.php#L5961 but I find that unlikely. This could be going wrong in two possible places that I can think of: The replyaddress is not being generated; and/or The message API is not adding the reply address to the headers. To check 1, add some form of debugging call (print_object / var_dump) of $replyaddress to just after the address has been generated. I'd recommend line 764 in the 2.8 link you sent. To check 2 is much harder, so let's see what we're getting from 1 first. If 1 is still null, then I suspect that the reply address is not being generated for some reason.  That could be: The user cannot post to this discussion (check group memberships, capabilities, forum type, etc); The data key for the message handler has not been set. To check 2, looking at https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/MOODLE_28_STABLE/mod/forum/lib.php#L549 , ensure that the data key was generated by adding debugging there: 
```text
mtrace("Generating data key for {$pid}: {$messageinbounderhandlers[$pid]}");
```
 If you aren't getting a data key for this post, then there's some kind of issue in the data key generation and we need to look there. I think that's probably enough to get things started. Once we work out where things are failing, we can work out where to look next. Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Where do i change the default setting for Forum Tracking?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, It depends on your moodle version. Later moodle versions have an option to change the default settings for user profile fields (until most recent 2.7/2.8 (I think) have settings built in to do this). In Moodle 2.3 latest and probably other versions upto 2.6 you can do something similar to the below..... Change Default user profile setting to Yes Track Forum Posts Find this file: www.yourmoodle.com/user/editlib.php Edit around this line number: 210 1. Find this code: $mform->setDefault('trackforums', 0 ); 2. Replace it with this code: $mform->setDefault('trackforums', 1 ); 3. Save your changes Notice the change from default value of Zero , to One . All user accounts created will now be set to Track Forums = Yes Change existing users 4. If you also want to change all existing users to this setting, then run the below MySQL command on your database : UPDATE mdl_user SET trackforums=1 ; Hope that helps Steve http://sheilds-elearning.com

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Messages from Moodle rejected by email provider
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Sue - we encountered this issue last year (2014). It was a change in policy by Yahoo that triggered the rejections from all providers. It is because Moodle issues emails using the student's email address, and in the case of Yahoo they are flagging any emails not generated from their servers as being a security risk. We opted to do this rather than prevent Moodle using student email addresses as our lecturers find it very useful to be able to reply to emails and have them go straight back to the student. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How do I hide an assignment until a given date?
ResponsesInList.Text: Are the questions part of the assignment's "Description field"? If so, then on the Assignment settings page, under "Availability" you can "Allow submissions from" a certain date and uncheck the box "Always show description." Done this way, students will see the assignment name on the course page, but they will not be able to see the description until submissions are allowed. This approach should generally work without changes to admin settings. In addition, though, Moodle also has something called "restricted" or "conditional" access. This feature needs to be enabled at the site level under Site administration > Advanced features > Enable conditional access. When enabled, Assignments and other activities should have a section in their settings called "Restrict access". Restricted access will allow you to hide an activity (not only an assignment) completely until a specified time or to show it grayed out with notes about the restrictions. Restricted access is nice because of the way it works across activities and resources. In the case of Assignments it just happens to overlap somewhat with the activity-specific Availability settings.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Grading participants's posts and level of participation
ResponsesInList.Text: You ask a question about "level of attendance" that always generates some good discussion. First, the simple thing to do is to use ratings, giving 1 point per post, and using "count of ratings" to contribute towards a students grade.  Right? Simple? Well, not so.  What will you define as a perfect ("A") score?  10 posts, 100 posts, 1000 posts?  Also, once students catch on to this, they might start making many simple posts.  For example, instead of providing a paragraph of ideas, they might instead provide sentences of ideas.  One ends up with essentially the same problem when teachers try to use "number of words" as a criteria for grading papers... students can easily increase the number of words without any more intellectual content. So consider what you really want from discussions, and try to configure your forums to encourage what you want.  For example, you can set up a forum using ratings, where you expect a minimum of 5 quality posts, and then rating each post on a 1-4 scale based upon quality.  If a student makes 5 excellent posts, they earn 20 rating points, which can be a perfect 100% (an "A+).  The burden is on the instructor to read every post, and have some form of idea of what a "1" is versus a "2", versus a "3", etc.  If a student makes 5 posts, let's say: 1 excellent, 3 good, and 1 fair, they have earned 15 points, and the student can decide if they want to make more posts in order to reach the 20 maximum points. Well, this is one idea.  It attempts to encourage "quality" instead of "quantity."  Maybe others will suggest other ideas.

ResponsesInList.Title: Database Error
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi There, I am Erin Steward from Dallas. I am working in Aschere
Energy Dallas as an engineer. I have installed some computers in my company and I am using
Ubuntu server . But I am facing problem to install Moodle in the server. Its showing
some database error. I am not able to get this error, Please suggest.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Database Error
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Erin, from Dallas, welcome to the Moodle community. You can get all sorts of information about Moodle, all sorts of help, but there are a couple of things you need to know. One is that for help on installation errors, go to the Installation forum, for help on the database activity, go to the database forum, for help on the choice activity, go to the choice forum. Most plugins, activities and resources have their own forums, so you really got to pick the right one sometimes. If you are not sure, just go to the General Help forum, which is probably the best place to start, and put your questions there. The second thing, and this is really important, you need to define the error or problem, clearly, and if you are getting an actual error message, include that as well. Give as much information as you can about the error or problem. The more information the better the opportunity the community gets to finding the right solution quickly. Having said that, let's take a stab in the dark. I am assuming this is an error you are getting while still installing. The Database is telling you that it is not being created or you do not have access or similar. There are several possibilities, main one being Ubuntu has not properly installed the database. For most Moodles, the default has been MySQL , so you have to make sure you have My SQL installed and properly configured. With V2.x, I am sure, you do not have to create the database first, Moodle should do that for you. However, you need to make sure that the database is properly named, eg Moodle281 for the version you are installing. Second you need to make sure the root password you have given when installing MySQL is the same password you are giving the Moodle installer. Without the right password, it can't access MySQL or create the database. These are the most common ones, for this stage of installation. There are others, but if you have gotten past this point, then there is something else going on. Without any information though, it is hard to help.

ResponsesInList.Title: Change default setting for "Subscription mode" for forums
ResponsesInList.Text:
By default forum subscription mode is set to "optional" when a new forum is created. In my experience trainers often create a forum without changing this
mode to "auto subscription " or "forced subscription". They then write a
post and expect this to be sent by e-mail to all course
participants, which does not happen as subscription is still set
to"optional". So as an Admin I would like to be able to set the default for forum
subscription to "auto subscription " or "forced subscription". You might also want the default setting to be "subscription disabled". I have just created the following Tracker-Issue: https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-47907 You can vote for this.

They can then still decide to unsubscribe individually. There are several discussions on how to set the default to "no subscription" too. https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=238241 https://moodle.org/mod/forum/discuss.php?d=268308

ResponsesInList.Title: Forum Shared between Multiple Courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Apologies if this has been covered in another forum post - I have searched what I figured to be the most obvious terms and haven't come across anything. Just wondering if it is possible in Moodle to have a Forum which is accessible by users enrolled in Multiple Courses. Optimally, this would be a 'Course Category' Forum where any user enrolled in a course in that specific category would be able to access it. Thank you for your help, Stephen

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum Shared between Multiple Courses
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Stephen, I don't think that's possible. You can create a forum only within a course. As far as I know, the only other place where a forum can be created is on the site front page ("site news" forum). One option is to create a new course in the "social format" with only the forum and add a link to this forum in your other courses. You can allow students to self-enrol themselves in this social course without an enrolment key if that makes it easier. Another option, but possibly not relevant for you, is to use the Groups feature within a single course to separate different groups of participants and yet have a common forum for everyone. Ravi

ResponsesInList.Title: See/grade all posts by user in forum?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all! I have my course set up so that there are 3 forums (discussion) posts required throughout the semester.  The students are to create an original post as well as reply to at least one other post.  They get credit for their original post and the 1 response, but can respond to as many as they want.  Is there a way I can set it so it shows me the posts by users so I can see how many responses each person posted?  Clicking on it by original post, I can give them a rating if they have responded, but I have no way of knowing if they've already received a rating for responding or if its their first response? This is my first semester using Moodle, in previous semesters I've used blackboard and I"m used to "grading forum" and it shows me all post by user, not by thread.  Any ideas?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: See/grade all posts by user in forum?
ResponsesInList.Text: Megan, The course logs might help you with this.  In the course administration block, click on "Reports" and then "Logs."  You can filter by student, activity, and date.  Choose "All Days" for the date.  Click on "Add" for the activity type so that you can view all of the posts that the student added to the forum.  If you click on any of the logs, it will show you the post.  The logs will be listed in chronological order from the time that they were made, so you can rate the first one if you'd like. Alternatively, you can rate them all and take an average of the posts and make that the students' grade.  This can be done on the settings page for the forum.  In the ratings section, you can choose to take an average of ratings for the grade. The thing that I don't like about ratings is that a student could meet the requirements and post high quality posts, but if he/she makes additional posts and they are graded then the grade on those can actually lower his overall grade.  So, you might want to just rate the first post that's made and not the others.  Or you could always go back to the manual grading method.  Either way, referring to the logs should make things easier and more efficient for you as the teacher. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Send message to students
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm not sure exactly what you are asking, but maybe this information will help: To receive an email when a student makes a post on a forum, you must be subscribed to the forum.  Click on the forum and then in the forum administration look for the link called "Subscription Mode." Typically, a user has time to edit their post.  The post is not delivered to your email until that time expires.  However, if the user clicks on the "Mail Now" check box, the message will be delivered within about five to ten minutes. If you go to your profile and clicking on "Messaging" you can choose which types of notifications to receive and the method by which you'd like to receive them. ResponsesInList.Title: Preventing access for instructor role at the activity level
ResponsesInList.Text: I would like to create a forum that is strictly for students to chat with other students without the monitoring of the instructor.  Is there a way to close off instructor access to a particular activity inside of a course?  When looking at the role permissions, it does not seem that access can be prevented at the activity level.  When looking at the particular forum, it does not seem that there is a setting to block access for a particular user.  I thought about creating groups for the forum and putting everyone but the instructor in the group, but I think the instructor will have access regardless of whether or not he/she is in the group due to his/her role.  Plus, creating groups for every course just for that one forum is very clunky and will cause confusion.  I am wondering if there is a simple way to accomplish hiding one activity from the instructor role but not from the student role.  Thanks, in advance, for your input.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Preventing access for instructor role at the activity level
ResponsesInList.Text: In the forum, go to Forum administration -> Permissions, then remove most of the permissions from Teachers. It may be enough to just remove mod/forum:view. You may need to experiment to get the details right.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Preventing access for instructor role at the activity level

ResponsesInList.Text: Bump. Probably a dumb idea to post this on a Sunday. -Derek

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum Development for 2.8.  Any news?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Derek, Thank you for raising this in the forums. During our planning period, we started to scope out the various changes required within the forums and the amount of work required for each. Unfortunately when we looked at both ForumNG (mod_forumng), and Advanced forums (mod_hsuforum), we felt that they were not quite the right fit for Moodle. This was in part because we felt that some of the features included in these solutions did not fit outside of the specific requirements for which they were written for. As an example, both solutions include an anonymity feature, but implement them differently. mod_forumng only allows tutors to post anonymously, whilst mod_hsuforum only allows all users to post under the name 'Anonymous'. Both were written for the HE market, but clearly there are major differences in the perceived requirements. Neither of these implementations allowed for use-cases such as role-playing which are an important pedagogical tool. In any case, if we had decided to migrate to either mod_forumng, or mod_hsuforum, we would have needed to either rewrite within the existing mod_forum plugin, or to provide an upgrade path from mod_forum to the chosen module. In migrating from mod_assignment to mod_assign we learnt many lessons about renaming modules and refactors of this kind... although this was largely a successful migration, it took us many releases to get things into the right state to be able to finally remove the old module. Instead, we have opted to look at each feature in turn and look to improve the existing forum to add the desired functionality. The aim is to improve the forum for the largest number of users and support as many pedagogical approaches as possible. The encompassing issue for all of the forum changes that we've been looking at is MDL-39707 . MDL-1626 is one of the components of this overarching issue and is one of the most requested features of all time within Moodle. I'm hoping that the feature will be integrated this afternoon and will be rolled in weeklies on Thursday. The next forum-related task we aim to look at is likely to be the layout and UI refactor ( MDL-41773 ) with the key aims of this task being to make the user interface more accessible, and clearer. It's likely that this will incorporate a couple of the other issues (e.g. MDL-8501 , and MDL-33692 ). I can't give a timescale on these, but the intention is to have these in place for the Moodle 2.8 release. With regards the roadmap, Martin updated the roadmap recently to give more consistency and to list each project that we are working on. Hope that this helps, Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum Development for 2.8.  Any news?

At a cursory glance you have all the issues I think are generally regarded as important here: edit in place, private reply, accessibility , reporting, anon posts, role playing (I'd love to be able to do De Bono's hats!!) etc. As to the roadmap.  It may be more consistent, but deleting all the links to discussion pages and tracker items has made the it much much less helpful and useful. -Derek

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Export Discussion - Single Simple Discussion
ResponsesInList.Text: The explanation of the URL is that the Single Simple Discussion is a special forum type that is only one discussion thread started by the teacher - it can only ever have replies (not other threads) added to it.  Other forum types can have multiple individual discussion threads.  The single simple discussion has no 'parent forum' if you like to think of it like that. The missing export whole discussion button has been reported as a bug - see & vote for https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-41918 . The button appears when you click 'Show parent' too as the .../ forum/discuss.php ... URL is used for that so that is a work around. Another workaround is to change the forum type to Standard Forum then alter the permissions to prevent students from creating new threads via the Start new discussions [mod/forum:startdiscussion] capability - effectively having one thread. I hope this helps Cheers Teresa

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Like buttom
ResponsesInList.Text: Maybe this issue has been debated already, so forgive me if it has. But I'm not sure if I would vote for a "Like" button in forums. There's a running joke in our house, and among our friends who have kids, that our kids won't read our e-mails unless we supply them with a "Like" button ("Mom, I can't be bothered to type actual words to reply to your e-mail and can barely muster the motivation to read it, but I'd be more willing if I could just click 'Like.'") Seems to me that one of the things we strive for in education - something that discussion forums excel at, actually - is forcing learners to "use their words" to explain, describe, and otherwise say what they mean. If we give them a "Like" button, have we given them a way to avoid this kind of effort that might lead to learning? I'm not sure, but I know that English teachers (I was one) constantly struggle to get their students to articulate fully their thoughts and ideas and questions, which is again something that the forums have always allowed them to do (required them to do). I suppose this issue raises the question of how Facebook and other social media might have goals that differ from those of online classes or online training. In FB the accumulation of "Likes" is a way of registering togetherness and popularity - a way of saying, "I saw your posting / photo / video, and I acknowledge your efforts in the spirit of friendship and togetherness." Do we want discussion forums to do *only* that? Or do we want to facilitate another kind of interaction? "The evidence you have presented seems sound" or "Your posting made me think of a related idea" or (horrors!) "I disagree with you in this one area." Note that FB doesn't provide you a "Dislike" button: it's not about thoughtful evaluation of a posting; it's about popularity ("Dad, I got 251 likes of my cat video!"). I remember what Martin said years ago at a Moodle Moot: "People learn best by asking and answering questions, so we've set up Moodle to enable asking and answering questions." Now there's a thoughtful approach to using technology to enable learning, I thought - and I still think so. I think I'd want the ability to turn the "Like" button on and off, so that I could accomplish more in a Moodle forum than I can currently accomplish in a FB posting. Thanks.  -  Peter

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Roger, You should find them under the moodledata directory (its location is defined in the $CFG-> dataroot directive at the config.php file): http://docs.moodle.org/19/en/Moodledata_directory

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Where are forum attachments stored?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Roger, Sorry for stating the obvious, but it isn't when it isn't. Are we then talking about a Moodle 2.x installation? Because you never mentioned that. If you're working with 1.9, then the directory structure uses the course ids (e.g. everything under directory 123 belongs to course 123). If you're working with 2.x, then you need to access the mdl_course table, look for the original file name of the attachment and use the content hash value to locate both the directory and the file. So, if the original file was named "somefile.pdf" and its content hash is something like " d7 89 ab34...", you would then use the leftmost first four characters to determine the location, like so: moodledata/filedir/ d7 / 89 and there you would find file "d789ab34...". Files are not encrypted. --- Reference http://docs.moodle.org/dev/File_API_internals#File_API_internals

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Restrict Students From Posting At Social Format
ResponsesInList.Text: We were able to do this in Standard Forum for General Use, and this may work also in the Social Format. Let us know! To allow students to reply to the instructor’s post, but not allow them to create new posts, from within the forum, go to “Forum administration > permissions” From the “Advanced role override” drop-down menu choose “Student” Scroll down to the 25th item, “Start new discussions” and select the “Prevent” radio button Select “Save changes” at the bottom left of the screen. Now students will not see the "Add a new discussion topic" button.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Presets in a Forum
ResponsesInList.Text: Steve, to preset their grades, choose Gradebook > Full view , scroll down to the forum row and type -10 in the Offset column, and save changes. "The offset is a number that is added to every grade for this grade item, after the multiplicator is applied." Sorting and grading forum posts is easier in " Advanced Forum ". If it is an option for you, switch to using that module instead of trying to make first-posts in alphabetic order. Cheers, Russell Edit: Actually, I think a -10 Offset does the opposite of what you want: it invisibly adjusts student grades down after grading, whereas you want to give them a highly visible threat before the activity. It makes me wonder, in your relationship with the students, will that threat be perceived as exciting and satisfying? Would it be equally well served, and sound less aggressive, if you set them a (positive) target?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum Unread posts with Twitter Bootstrap
ResponsesInList.Text: The bootstrap themes in Moodle don't generally add/remove classes for most things that are in core moodle unless its identified in a theme renderer. Simply using a bootstrap swatch will not work on Moodle without some of the adaptations done in the bootstrap based themes (such as Clean) as it does not address all the classes used in Moodle. And applying a bootstrap swatch over the top of something like Clean may well mean that those classes do not change style as they will have been identified by the work done in BootstrapBase and Clean, but are not targeted classes and styles in the core bootstrap swatches. So as a starter - what theme are you actually using (so we can see if there is an issue with a renderer in that theme) and in what way are you applying the 'Twitter Bootstrap template'?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Flag and S icons in Discussion Post
ResponsesInList.Text: Marcia, Are you using advanced forums? If so then this is specific to advanced forums and not part of the Moodle core forums. ResponsesInList.Title: Subscription to a forum marks posts as read when subscription email is sent
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I had the same issue in Moodle 1 , but for anyone interested in this, it's just the same issue in Moodle 2: when a user subscribes to a forum each message that is included in a subscription email (digest or individual) will automatically get marked as read. To me this doesn't make much sense. I use the subscription service in Moodle to get notified that there's some activity in the forums, but it doesn't necessarily mean that I read the new message in my inbox (even more so for digests). Rather, I would find it much more useful if messages that were mailed out would not change their read/unread mark because a lot of users prefer to read posts in the actual forum in Moodle. Well, fortunately there's an easy fix to change this default behaviour, and it's the same as in Moodle 1. Simply look into the file /mod/forum/lib.php and in the forum_cron() function (and ONLY in that function), there comment out the two lines/occurrences with forum_tp_mark_posts_read($userto, $userto->markposts); so simply do this instead: //forum_tp_mark_posts_read($userto, $userto->markposts); forum_tp_mark_posts_read() is responsible to (surprise!) mark posts as read. In the forum_cron() function there's one line for individual post and one line for digest emails. The only thing I don't like about this is that it touches core code, so I need to be aware of these changes on every update. I really think this behaviour of Moodle should be optional and I would appreciate an (official core code) admin setting to decide if subscriptions interfere with tracking in this way. This should be quite easy to implement. The default behaviour is not very popular with our students. Cheers! Anatol

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forums in Moodle 2.7
ResponsesInList.Text: This news is rather disappointing, but not perhaps too surprising. Some light trawling though the Tracker reveals that discussion and code patches around revamping the Forum have gone on since at least spring 09 -- that's 5 years. It's disappointing that this has not received a higher priority especially for a version that's slated for long term support. 6 months or so ago we were told that changes couldn't be made in 2.6 but to look for 2.7. Is the policy to make version changes based on strict deadlines working well? I wonder whether it might be worthwhile to evaluate this policy in some way to get assessments from managers of moodle sites large and small. It's very disappointing when good solutions are implemented but in versions which managers cannot implement until the next academic year. For example, the fix to control sending feedback on assignment submissions which got 90 votes in the Tracker ( MDL 33600 ) came too late for 2.6 and so was placed in 2.7 -- fortunately it is being backported into v2.6 ( MDL-43985 -- which took 77 votes). In both of these Tracker conversations there are references to institutions having to upgrade to a version one point less than the newly released one -- thus 2.6 in summer 2014 rather than 2.7. On another tack, though related, there seems to have been little progress on implementing Wiki and Survey upgrades. Both of these have high interest levels in the Tracker but there seems no mechanism to vote on priorities for the next release and so both of these are left on the shelf. It seems to me that a new version or point update that rolls out a major feature upgrade might allow a sharper focus on improving these basic features of Moodle. Just some thoughts.

ResponsesInList.Title: Forum URL Construction
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello All I am new to moodle development and hence I am seeking your help. I was looking at how moodle constructs the url for forums. The general url structure is:- https://yoursite.com/moodle/mod/forum/view.php?id=XXX How does moodle determine the id of the forum? I checked the moodle forum table, mdl_forum. Even though the id of the forum is stored as 3 in the database , the id in the url is 111(it sums up to 3). http://54.201.160.26/moodle/mod/forum/view.php?id=111 Similarly for a forum with id=4 in the database, the id in the url is 112. However, for the auto generated news forum for the course, the id in the url and the database is 1. I wanted to understand the logic behind the id numbers. Thanks!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum URL Construction
ResponsesInList.Text: The id comes from the course_modules table. For this forum, the course_module.id will be 112, and the forum.id will be 4. The link is via course_modules.instance, but you also need to check course_modules.module to make sure you forum.id 4, and not something like quiz.id 4.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum URL Construction
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks! I understood now.

ResponsesInList.Title: Email from forum not displaying correctly
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, When posts are submitted to course forums in my Moodle site, an equals sign replaces several letters throughout the resulting automatically generated email (see attached). Also, the photo of the person posting the mesage fails to appear in the email. Any suggestions on how to fix this would be most appreciated. Thanks, Ronan.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Email from forum not displaying correctly
ResponsesInList.Text: I too had this problem. I then found this bug in the moodle bug database , which describes the problem in depth. Basically, to enable compatibility with most mail servers, it uses an old method of encoding 8bit characters to fit into a 7bit SMTP stream. This has a 78 character limit, so = are inserted to split the message up. The image and links do not work because they also have characters replaced with = signs. I managed to fix it on our mail server by changing the $mail->encoding line in moodlelib from 'quoted-printable' to '8bit'. Other than this, you can change to plain text encoding (which we did while i investigated) Maybe in a later version of moodle, this should be an option in the admin variables page to go alongside the SMTP options.

ResponsesInList.Title: Per-discussion subscription - request for feedback
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, I'm hoping to get some feedback for some work I'm currently planning relating to forums. This is work intended for Moodle 2.7 and at this stage is research-based to determine the possible requirements and scope of the work. One of the longest requested features in Moodle has been the ability to subscribe to a single discussion rather than a whole forum, and this is something that I'm looking to implement. This was originally requested in MDL-1626 . My request for feedback is initially to assess how the discussion subscriptions should work in combination with existing forum subscriptions and related features. When a user is subscribed to a whole forum, I see two potential options for this feature: you are not presented with the option of subscribing to an individual discussion if you are already subscribed to the forum as a whole; or you have the option of subscribing to a discussion, even if you are already subscribed to the whole forum . Although 1) seems initially appealing because it reduces the complexity of the interface and reduces what initially seem like redundant options (that is to say that it seems pointless to subscribe to a discussion that you're already subscribed to), I suspect that 2) may actually be the better option as I'll explain below. We've supported the ability to have an e-mailed forum 'Daily Digest' for a very long time in Moodle, which means that from their profile setting a user can select whether they want to receive: one e-mail per forum message; a single e-mail containing the subject of all forum posts made during a day; or a single e-mail containing the full content of all messages sent during a day. These latter two options are the Daily Digests, and are currently sent once per day. Since Moodle 2.6, we have additionally supported the ability to have a different digest setting for each specific forum. This means that you can choose to receive an e-mail per forum message as your default setting for most forums, but have a daily digest option for some forums which aren't as relevant to you. We could extend these existing subscription states to allow a user to receive a range of interaction levels depending on their interest and requirements. So if their profile digest option is to receive an Subject-only daily digest a user can override this for a specific forum, or a specific discussion within a forum. As an example, we'll take Jeff. Jeff is a Humanities lecturer at the University of Life. His department is very large; he has many students and teaches on ten to twenty modules per year. Jeff teaches some of these courses as the main tutor and wants to receive every forum post as soon as possible because he takes an active interest in his specific subject matter and wants to interact with his students. He is also a guest lecturer on a couple of other introductory courses which cover many aspects of the subject. Since he only takes part in the occasional lecture for these courses, he doesn't really follow the discussions as actively. He'd like to receive a daily digest with the subject of each message so that he can skim them in case there are questions relating to his lectures or his research areas. When he spots these posts, he wants to be able to take part in the conversation more actively. He doesn't want to wait until the daily digest arrives and look for the specific subject, but to receive each message as soon as possible. In order to do so, he subscribes to the individual discussions. He now receives one e-mail per post on the discussion, but for all other posts on the forum he still gets a daily digest. He's also on a faculty noticeboard in another course which he must read, but rarely has to reply to. For this forum, he wishes to recieve a daily digest with the complete content. This way, he can read the entire discussion at a time convenient to him. In addition to the above argument, and arguably more importantly for students, since forum subscriptions can be forced upon a user I feel that it's important to give users the ability to determine the level of their personal involvement whilst still receiving e-mail notifications. Having a granular level of digest and subscription states would cater for both of the above. In terms of the User Interface, I've attached some very brief mockups for areas we might change initially. There will be other areas to consider, including the e-mail footer, and discussion views. In summary though, we will need to update interfaces: when creating a post (either a reply, or a new discussion topic): add the ability to subscribe to the discussion; and remove the ability to subscribe to the whole forum; and add a status view with toggle capability to the discussion list. I'd love to hear any views others may have in this area - both positive and negative. If you have any other considerations you think we need to take on board, or have an alternative proposal for example. Thank you in advance, Andrew Nicols

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Per-discussion subscription - request for feedback
ResponsesInList.Text: Please note, the above is just looking at how we interact with existing forum subscriptions. It doesn't take into account subscribing to a forum which you are not subscribed to at all (this should be fairly obvious anyway). I will also be posting at some point on the possibility of unsubscribing from a forum, but I need to consider how this will work with all of our existing forum settings and how this fits into pedagogy.

ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for posting this Andrew. Overall this sounds great, but one item stood out when I read your post: when creating a post (either a reply, or a new discussion topic): add the ability to subscribe to the discussion; and remove the ability to subscribe to the whole forum ; and add a status view with toggle capability to the discussion list. Why would you not want to allow a user to subscribe to the entire forum when creating a new discussion? Imagine that the forum is a Q&A forum for instance, and the user is Sam Student: Sam wants wants to ask a question - ie start a new discussion. She'll want to be subscribed to that discussion as "one email per message", so she'll know right away when someone replies. But Sam also wants to subscribe to the Q&A forum as a whole, to receive a digest of questions that her classmates have asked. The interface could have two drop-down selections (or maybe a nicer ui element): Discussion subscription: Subscribe me to this discussion as individual emails for each new reply/post Subscribe me to this discussion as a daily digest of full posts Subscribe me to this discussion as a daily digest of subjects only (actually, this last one might be of little use) Do not subscribe me to this discussion beyond the Discussion subscription [default] Forum subscription: Subscribe me to all posts in this forum as individual emails Subscribe me to all posts in this forum as daily digest of full text Subscribe me to all posts in this forum as daily digest of subjects only Do not subscribe me to this forum aside from individual discussions specifically subscribed to The interface when reading a forum or discussion should, in the place where it currently has a link to the subscription settings, have two indicators, such that it can show messages such as: "Current subscription: You will receive each new post in this discussion as an individual email, but you will not be notified of new posts in other discussions in this forum". I'll think this through a bit more, there might be some flaws in my thinking. Cheers, Minh-Tam

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Per-discussion subscription - request for feedback
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Minh-Tam, My thinking for removing this option from the new discussion/post interface is that a whole-forum setting is not contextually appropriate for a the post screen. If a user wants to subscribe to a forum as a whole, they should be able to do so from the forum view page rather than when posting a message which is contextually relevant. This would also help us to keep clutter to a minimum and detract less from the key task - writing a forum post. Andrew

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Per-discussion subscription - request for feedback
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Andrew, that makes sense. As long as the forum subscription setting is implemented in a way to not add too many clicks. Right now, going form "my Home" to a changing the subscription in a forum takes three clicks: > course > forum > admin block/subscription Clicking on "Unsubscribe from this forum" or "Subscribe to this forum" has immediate effect, no settings page is needed because there are only two possible options to toggle between: Subscribe as per preferences defined in profile, or unsubscribe. Once we allow a per forum (and per discussion) choice of four subscription levels [one email per post | full digest | subjects digest | no subscription], this won't be just a toggle any more. We might be tempted to send a user to a settings page ("Choose your level of subscription for this forum"), which adds another two clicks: > course > forum > admin block/subscription > click selected subscription level > click OK

You already gave a couple in your email (Jeff's use cases). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum permissions 2.4
ResponsesInList.Text: You are one the right track with the question I suspect, permissions. Go into Site Administration, and look at Permissions on Accounts. Check the Student account and it is likely that permission to start a new discussion has been set at "Inherit" and somewhere, someone has switched it off. If you change it to "Allow", at the Site level, it will affect ALL forums in the site, which should work. If you only want it on that one forum, then go into the Forum, then select "Permissions" from the menu and make sure that Student are listed everywhere they need to be. These are the four main permissions for Students to do what they need to do: Delete own posts (within deadline) Reply to posts Start new discussions View discussions Change the Rate permissions if you want students be able to rate posts. Make sure Students can access the forum via those permissions and it should be Ok. If Students are not listed, then they can be added with the plus sign or button at the end of the row. (Not individual Students, but as enrollees.) If students are already listed, but cannot access what they need, then there is another problem, probably in the site wide permissions. If this does not work then there is another issue altogether, which will probably need some hack of the code to make it work.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enrolment, guest vs authenticated user, and forum permissions
ResponsesInList.Text: The Roles system in Moodle is designed to categorize access to the various parts of Moodle, to provide a limit to the capabilities of Users in each of the contexts of the entire Moodle. It is the division of capabilities inherent within the Roles that provides a basic internal security for the Moodle. You can give Authenticated Users the right to access a forum by changing the Forums permissions of the Authenticated User.  You need to change the permissions Reply to Posts, Start New Discussions and View Discussion . You can do that via the Front Page , go to Administration ► Users ► Permissions ► Define roles and there to Authenticated User, then Edit Permissions and Capabilities. There is only one the public area that you can place your forum in and have it accessible to Authenticated Users and that is from the Front Page. You can create a forum that displays on the Front Page or you can place your forum in the Main Menu Block on the Front Page. Courses are not considered part of the public area of a Moodle. AFAIK you cannot grant access to a Forum within a course without that User being enrolled in the course. To hack the code to change that could open a rather large security hole within all your courses.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enrolment, guest vs authenticated user, and forum permissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Just an update, in case people find this thread in a search. I keep finding it myself as I look for solutions! Here's where we're at. This is informational-- I'm not sure it's all kosher. We have several distinct public areas of the moodle site; we're using it as a student portal as well as for courses. Public areas are setup as distinct courses -- for clarity of navigation and it allows us to give different people update privileges for different areas. These courses allow guest access, and auto-login guests is set. Each area has its own forum, for posting questions/feedback etc. We want to require that someone is logged in to moodle before posting,  but we don't want people to have to "enrol" in the course to post. The capabilities system suggests that this should be a simple matter of giving extra permissions (forum view/reply/post) to authenticated users in the given forums. This doesn't work-- for whatever reasons (I suspect some legacy code), reply still requires enrollment, and the start discussions button didn't show up. There are some comments in the docs like "There are certain things, such as posting in a forum, that guests are never allowed to do, despite the permissions interface suggesting otherwise ." Fair enough. The code (forum/lib.php) shows that in addition to testing for the capabilities, the forum_user_can_post is also checking for enrollment. Oddly, the forum_user_can_post_discussion doesn't. Our current plan is as follows create a Participant role based on authenticated user, and set that to be the default for logged in users. Make it available at category level. Put all the public area courses into a single category. Override permissions at the category level to give our new participant role the extra priveleges we want. (And maybe more later, like the choice activity). Comment out the annoying checks for course enrollment where the capability check should be enough. (this is the possibly foolish part -- but really, if capabilities work, they'll work here. It's not like we're overriding at the site level. Search the tracker for other evidence of this, and post the requirement for course enrollment to post in forums as a bug; at least in versions of Moodle with the nice roles/capabilties system. If anybody thinks this is madness, it would be great to hear why. Perhaps there's dependencies in activity logging or something that isn't obvious? Why not just auto-enroll everyone into the public courses? We're a large institution; it would be 20,000 users or so, and I don't know the system well enough to know that huge enrollments wouldn't be a drag on performance. It just seems a waste. We certainly don't need user-level activity reports for the public areas.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Enrolment, guest vs authenticated user, and forum permissions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello All: We are running Moodle 2.4, and were *very* happy to find this thread, because we've been walking down the exact same road that Gregor describes above.  No need to repeat any details, because it's exactly the same.  Seeing as how there were no replies to his last post, and we can't find any additional documentation on the topic, we went ahead and modified the code in /mod/forum/lib.php as well.  Specifically, we commented out this code: if (!is_viewing($ context , $user->id) and !is_enrolled($context, $user->id, '', true)) { return false; } This solved the problem for us. As best as I can see from this code, and the definitions of is_viewing and is_enrolled, it seems to have been a safe move - given that we've got our permissions properly set, which we do. So, I'll echo Gregor's question by saying, "Does anyone see anything particularly poor about doing this?"  Feedback is most welcome.  If not, then I'm inclined to agree with Gregor in calling this a bug that ought to be fixed. Thanks Joe

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Hyperlinking forum to an image gives mixed results per users
ResponsesInList.Text: Hidden resources are not generally accessible to students, although they are to teachers/admins/etc. This means that the links you provide should not work for students, for any of the resources. ResponsesInList.Title: A suggested change to the forum settings
ResponsesInList.Text: I use Moodle in the classroom and until Moodle 2.0 I found the Q&A style forum very useful. I would set various questions and the students would post answers. They would not see any other students answers until they had posted their own. Then in March 2011 MDL-9376 broke this for me by  preventing students seeing other people posts until the maxediting time had elapsed (i.e. a typical 30 minute delay before students could see other peoples posts) https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-9376 This made the Q&A forum unusable in the classroom setting for me. ResponsesInList.Title: Remove "Forum Posts" from Navigation Menu
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm using the Fusion theme with a new installation of Moodle 2.0.2. I'm wondering if there's a way to remove the "Forum Posts" link (and the "Posts" and "Discussions" sublinks) from the Navigation menu. I've disabled the Forums as best I can and I feel having the links there will be confusing to students.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Remove "Forum Posts" from Navigation Menu
ResponsesInList.Text: I agree that the links are confusing and results in multiple questions from students and guests asking how to use the forums. Disabling "See all user posts" (moodle/user:readuserposts) and "View discussions" (mod/forum:viewdiscussion) under "Site administration->Users->Permissions->Define roles->[Role]" should remove these options from the navigation block. Here is a patch that does that for 2.X: Find the following code within "/lib/navigationlib.php": // Add nodes for forum posts and discussions if the user can view either or both // There are no capability checks here as the content of the page is based // purely on the forums the current user has access too. $forumtab = $usernode->add(get_string('forumposts', 'forum')); $forumtab->add(get_string('posts', 'forum'), new moodle_url('/mod/forum/user.php', $baseargs)); $forumtab->add(get_string('discussions', 'forum'), new moodle_url('/mod/forum/user.php', array_merge($baseargs, array('mode'=>'discussions')))); P.S. Added to Tracker: MDL-27058

ResponsesInList.Text: There are two answers to that. 1. a. The forum is one of the oldest parts of Moodle, and over the years, lots of different features have been added one at a time so there is a lot of mess. b. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Subscription at the discussion (Thread) level revisited.
ResponsesInList.Text: In Moodle, Students get a limited amount time to edit their own posts, and then they can't edit any more. This is a reasonable compromise. It gives you time to notice and correct most errors, or to delete a post you made in anger if you reconsider a few minutes later. But it does not destroy the fact that a forum is an asynchronous discussion that builds up over time. The ability for anyone, at any time, to go back and change anything, would let them destroy the history of the conversation. By default, the editing time is 30 minutes, but this can be changed by the admin in the site-wide forum settings. ForumNG has this feature. ForumNG also has the option to export all or some as a thread as a word document or to an email.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Subscription at the discussion (Thread) level revisited.
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, right now everyone, particularly at Moodle HQ, is focussed on getting Moodle 2.0 finished, so really very little thought has been given to what happens in Moodle 2.1. Before ForumNG could go into Moodle 2.1, at least all of the following would have to happen: 1. The ForumNG code has to be updated to be compatible with Moodle 2.0. 2. The developers at Moodel HQ have to review the code, and decide whether it is good enough technically to go into Moodle core. 3. The community need to have a discussion about whether replacing the existing forum with ForumNG is the right thing for Moodle. None of that has happened yet. What has happened is we at the OU have kept Martin and the rest of the Moodle community informed about what we are doing (Including: * Posting the original specification in the General Developer Forum some months before sam started writing the code. * sam posting regular updates in his blog during development. sam's blog is aggregated with others at http://planet.moodle.org/ . * Releasing the code so people can try it. And, from discussions with Martin, I know he has not ruled out the idea of adding ForumNG to Moodle 2.1, but, as I said above, he is spending most of his time thinking about Moodle 2.0 right now, so the real decision will be made in the future. 'It is possible that ...' was my attempt to reduce all that to one sentence. To subscribe to a thread, view that thread, and at the bottom there is a button to subscribe, next to the text: "Subscription "You do not currently receive messages from this discussion by email. If you would like to, please click Subscribe to discussion." Of course, if you are already subscribed to the whole forum, that does not show up.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Subscription at the discussion (Thread) level revisited.
ResponsesInList.Text: Do bear in mind that the spec sheet was written nearly 2 years ago, and since then we have gone through implementation, piloting and release, with lots of feedback from our users, so what you see today will not be exactly what was in the original plan. The benefit for the OU if FormNG becomes a standard part of Moodle is clear. If that happens, then more people will contribute to the on-going maintenance, and contribute new features. We won't have to do all the work. Therefore, we have a significant incentive to do the work required to get this into Moodle core, in addition to the fact that the OU like to be a good contributing member of the Moodle community. However, we also realise that it is for the Moodle community to decide what is the best way forwards for Moodle. For example, there was a question of which wiki to include in Moodle 2.0, nwiki or ouwiki. The community chose nwiki, and we accepted that, even though it was not the decision we were hoping for.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: See all posts for students
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Curt, One way to accomplish this is by using the Participation Report in the Navigation block. Go to the Navigation block, select your course -> Reports -> Participation report. Now you need to select the “Activity module” (e.g., Forum week 1), the time frame (e.g, 4 weeks), then select “Students” and “Post.” This should give you a summary of what the students did in a particular activity. Another way  to accomplish this is by using Logs . Go to the Navigation block, select your course -> Reports -> Logs). If you want to get an overview what all participants in this course did in a particular activity, you need to change the date to “All days” and select the particular activity in the next drop down menu (e.g., forum week 1). Change “All actions” to “Add.” In case you are looking for a particular student in a particular activity, just change “All participants” and select the student’s name. With kind regards, Hartmut

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: See all posts for students
ResponsesInList.Text: (You know you've got it pretty bad when you start replying to yourself in forums.) That twisty path in my last posting is a lot of clickity-click-clicking. If you're willing to do a little pre-work, I've got a way to save you a little time as you're reviewing student postings. Background: Every course has an internal Moodle id number. Every student also has an internal Moodle id number. You can use this information to adjust the URL to jump straight to the forum postings view, bypassing the clicking. Trouble is, you need to know those id numbers. Go to a view that lists all your students (e.g. Gradebook, Participants list, or Enrolled users). Move your cursor to hover over a student name (don't click, just hover). In the very bottom left-hand corner of the browser, a URL will be displayed. It will look something like this: https://your.moodle.site/user/view.php? id=1857 & course=17 id=1857 the student's Moodle id course=17 the course Moodle id Work your way down the list of students, making a note of each student's Moodle id number. The URL for the posts view is: https://your.moodle.site/mod/forum/user.php? id=1857 & course=17 Paste this URL into your web browser (replacing your.moodle.site with your actual site URL), but don't hit <Return/Enter> just yet. Notice the id=1857 and course=17. If you modify those to match your course's Moodle id number and the student you want to view and hit <Return/Enter>, you'll be taken directly to the list of that student's forum postings. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assigning grades to forums when posts aren't made
ResponsesInList.Text: The way I take care of this problem is through the Grade Administration screen.  From the main course screen, click on Grades in the Settings menu.  Mine defaults to the Grader Report , but you can change it to Full View .  On that screen you should see a list of all the assignments and some other details about them.  Under the column header that says Aggregate only non-empty grades there is a checkbox, which if left unchecked will calculate a zero for any activities where the student has not submitted.
