ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assigning grades to forums when posts aren't made
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm not sure how your grading is set up.  We have assigned maximum point values to each forum/activity.  The maximum activity values cumulatively total 100.  In the sample user report below, see the grade column.  It has the total points accrued at the top and the total number of points earned for each activity.  There is also the percentage column which shows how well a student did on each activity and their overall grade at the top. To achieve this, first the rating for each activity's aggregate type must be set to maximum rating . Second, assigned point values must be set so that all activities' maximum points possible when added together for the whole course total 100. Third, back in Settings ⟩ Grades ⟩ Categories and items ⟩ Full view , the aggregation must be set to Sum of Grades and Aggregate only non-empty grades must be unchecked. This may require a change in the way you calculate grades, and therefore not be feasible for any active courses, so I offer it for your consideration in grading future courses.

ResponsesInList.Title: Reply to forum by email
ResponsesInList.Text: Is there any plans to include 'Reply by email' functionality to the forum module? We are hoping to move to Moodle communities soon, however many of our users are on Email distribution lists and would prefer to continue communicating this way.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Reply to forum by email
ResponsesInList.Text: I know of no way to truly "link" email lists to Moodle forums. NOTE: simply sending out emails per forum posts and being able to reply to said forum post via email does NOT link an email list to a forum. There's more to it then that. Among other things, email list subscribers need to see forum posts as emails and for forum readers to see emails as forum posts, all in a "transparent" fashion. A little more background (which may be a bit off-topic here, please forgive me if so)... I believe that the "linking" of email lists to forums (particularly *existing* email list communities that have been running for a long time) will be an increasingly-important capability for communications systems for a long time to come. I have been participating in the ongoing development of Mail2Forum, aka M2F, at http://m2f.sourceforge.net . This project "links" (synchronizes, mirrors, etc) phpBB (see http://phpbb.com ) forums to any external email list (much like GNUMailman can link its email lists to Usenet newsgroups). However, since Moodle has its own, native, "proprietary" forum module, it can not leverage this development from the phpBB community (or any of the vbulletin.com community, the other "other big forum software" provider). While I do find it powerful how nicely-integrated the Moodle forums are with the rest of Moodle, I think they lack in features, and they also have the problem of not leveraging the forum-communities development as per above. In short, if there's one area where I wish Moodle would "break out" it's module to have it rely on other software it is forums. I would be particularly interested in the API stuff being developed in phpBB 2.2.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Reply to forum by email
ResponsesInList.Text: Sure we can leverage email-to-forum technology, especially if it's in PHP. The hard bit is piping/parsing the email, not inserting it into a forum. Moodle mail already has headers now that include course/forum/post information which should help. Just show me something that actually exists and works with all mail clients and all users!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Reply to forum by email
ResponsesInList.Text: Another point is that some users will not realise that they are sending an answer to a public forum instead of to a privat person who sends an email. (It happens already with the current forum-reminder.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Reply to forum by email
ResponsesInList.Text: The headers seem to carry through pretty well in a quick test I did today, so determining the place to insert the mail should not be too hard assuming all emailers retain the headers like Mozilla does. The main issue remaining is this: how can incoming email be authenticated? Email addresses are easy to forge ... I'd be interested to see how this m2f solves that one.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Reply to forum by email
ResponsesInList.Text: Ger Tielemans writes: Another point is that some users will not realise that they are sending an answer to a public forum instead of to a privat person who sends an email. (It happens already with the current forum-reminder.) Assuming I understand your point correctly (please correct me if I do not), I have found this to be handled well with email list managers like GNU Mailman. Each email list has an option to format the headers such that a reply to a broadcast email message is addressed to the single author of the original email, to the entire email list, or maybe even something else. The main idea: if one "modularly" links an email list with a web forum, then let the email list handle the emails, the forum handle the posts, and synchronize the data msgs from the 2 delivery mechanisms on the "backend" separate from the user. This (theoretically, at least) leverages the power and strengths of each mechanism in its focus area (email for email lists, forum posts for web forums). Martin writes: The main issue remaining is this: how can incoming email be authenticated? Email addresses are easy to forge ... I'd be interested to see how this m2f solves that one. I'm interested to see what kind of "email authentication" you mean here, and maybe go through a few scenarios. For example, my Moodle profile's email address is moodle.org@mengland.net (anything going to @mengland.net gets sent to me) as a convenient email-filtering mechanism in my MUA (mail user agent like Outlook or Eudora). However, most of my From: and Reply-To: headers still get sent out with a different address (something-else@mengland.net...I don't put the real address here for fear of web-crawling spam miners). Do we want to "authenticate" that any emails/posts sent/made to the Moodle "conversational space" (be it email lists, web forums, newsgroups, etc...because they can all theoretically be linked) have an author that reads moodle.org@mengland.net instead of something-else@mengland.net? This part is probably relatively easy to do. Email lists already do it. And/or, do we want to verify that emails with From: and Reply-To:'s (or any similar headers) are truly coming from me, a la PGP security or something of that nature that will verify my authenticity via some sort of key...or some other implementation? This seems rather difficult, given that I suspect this would require client-side (as in MUA) configuration changes for authentication not to mention a lot of hand-shaking between server and client mechanisms (if I understand things correctly, which I may very well not--I have not developed these kinds of software systems before, I'm simply guessing as to what would be needed). And/or some other scenario(s)? Maybe I do not have a firm understanding on this point? -Matt

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Way to see if student has completed required forum posts or replies in gradebook?
ResponsesInList.Text: Can a student post a response such as "orem ipsum dolor sit amet, consetetur sadipscing elitr, sed diam nonumy eirmod tempor invidunt"?  If so, and if no one cares to actually read these posts, then you might have a problem getting Moodle to count these. However, if someone really is reading student posts, then I can suggest that you use ratings, set the criteria to "count of ratings", and make the scale be "1".  Whoever is reading the posts can then simply rate each post with a score of "1". I am one who believes that if students are being asked to say something, then someone should take the care to read what they are saying.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Way to see if student has completed required forum posts or replies in gradebook?
ResponsesInList.Text: Bonnie, based upon what you have said, I now highly recommend that you use the "rating" system.  After reading a post, it only involves two clicks (one to drop the possible scores, and one to then pick a score."  You can easily set it up to do a simple count, or you can even decide to score students (even something as simple a 1, 2, or 3 points) if you really want to give them more credit for better posts. Just try this rating thing right here on moodle.  Don't you see that you can rate my post?  It's as simple as that. (Of course, you still have to configure your forum grading method.) I think once you try this, you will see that it is the ideal solution for you. When I do this, I let students know that their grades for posts will be seen after I read them.  This allows me to read them at any time, and then because I rate them, I easily see which post I have already read.  Moodle's way of handling posts, and grading, is far superior to products like Blackboard.

ResponsesInList.Title: Can you restrict/remove the rich text editor in 2.4?
ResponsesInList.Text: We have students that are getting around the attachment limitations in the forums on 2.4.3 by using the insert image function in the rich text editor of their message.  Is there a way to remove the editor or restrict the uploads via the insert image button on specific forums?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can you restrict/remove the rich text editor in 2.4?
ResponsesInList.Text: Why does it matter? Your post reads like "Oh no! students are communicating more effectively than the teacher has allowed. We can't possibly allow that!" There must be more to it than that, but I don't understand.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can you restrict/remove the rich text editor in 2.4?
ResponsesInList.Text: It matters more in the size limitation than in the number of attachments, the goal is to keep posted images to a size/resolution that is reasonable for viewing on a monitor and/or having to download on a slow Internet connection.  In this example, students uploaded raw images from their camera that are 4000x3000 and over 2MB in size, much larger than the attachment limit. This does not make more for more effective communication than the teacher has allowed, as you can't even view them without resizing them or zooming way out, which then makes the related text unreadable.  And zooming doesn't help with the bandwidth issue.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can you restrict/remove the rich text editor in 2.4?
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, there are two approaches to this: One is the technical view-point that this thread started with. Moodle should make it impossible to do 'bad' things. The other approach is to view this as a learning opportunity. Now, digital literacy may not be the primarly learning outcome of your course, but this is an opportunity to briefly explain to students about appropriate sizing of images for online discourse, the tools available to do that, and how their actions online affect everyone's learning. There are even ways you could handle this were you don't have to do all the work. This is a topic where students can help and police each other's behaviour.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can you restrict/remove the rich text editor in 2.4?
ResponsesInList.Text: The instructor of this class has posted instructions describing how to post the images, and was expecting the attachment size limitation to back up his instructions by not allowing the large images.  It is an earth science class, so no, digital literacy is not a primary outcome, and I wouldn't expect it to be, but he also doesn't just leave the students in the dark to figure it out completely on their own. I don't expect Moodle to prevent all "bad things", and I didn't present my question in that way.  I merely pointed out that Moodle provides a way to circumvent a desired setting by our instructor, and am looking for a technical solution to his request as a Moodle administrator.  If there is one, I will implement it, if not, then I will move on to the next request.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can you restrict/remove the rich text editor in 2.4?
ResponsesInList.Text: I agree with Benjamin here: removing the rich-text editor selectively is not just a "technical" solution. It would we very useful to have in lots of places in Moodle. In forums, for example, it would allow / encourage light-weight, short-form conversations, which may be pedagogically useful.

ResponsesInList.Title: Forum grades not visible to students
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, we use a forum for students to post text on a specific topic. Teacher then grades to posts. The forum has a time limitation - it can be used only on one certain day. After the forum is closed a teacher grades the posts, but student can not see the grades, since the forum is closed (Allow acces until). How to enable studetns to see the grades but disable them to make new posts or replies? Thank you

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum grades not visible to students
ResponsesInList.Text: A way to do this would be to change the permissions for the specific forum.  You can go to the forum in question, then on your settings menu go to: Settings > Forum administration > Permissions Go down to the Permission called "Reply to posts" and remove the Student role. Doing it this way you can allow the forum to remain visible but students can no longer make new posts.  Depending on the type of forum and existing permissions, you might also need to remove the Student role from "Start new discussions. " One last step: you will now need to disable the end date for restricted access in your forum settings.  This will make the forum visible again, but since you have changed the aforementioned permissions students will not be able to make any new posts. HTH !

ResponsesInList.Text: Danny, There are several variables to consider and since you're new to Moodle, perhaps the terminology is being confused. Let's try this: Enter your course and turn editing on. Choose to add a new Forum (forget about the one you already created for now) Provide a name and introduction for the forum, and leave the Forum type set to Standard forum for general use (the default) Leave all other settings/options at their defaults Click Save and display at the bottom of the page. You'll see something similar to the image below (hopefully). At this point, since there are not posts yet, there is nothing to reply to. Click Add a new discussion topic Provide a name and message , then click Post to forum. In the image below, the initial post now appears for users to read (they have to click to enter the thread and read the post). From the student's perspective, they will be able to enter the post and see the reply option (see below): So, if you've been following those steps and students still cannot reply, I'm not sure what to suggest as a solution. But, you mentioned you allowed "a student user" to try to reply to your post. Did you enroll the student with a student role, or as a guest ? I don't believe that users with the "guest" role can participate in forums (they can't reply or post). Remember, too, that the News forum is unique, in that it does not allow for students to reply (it's a one-way push of information, so "forum" is a bit of a misnomer). Other factors that may prohibit posts and/or replies include permissions , blocking , groups , and access restriction settings. I hope this is helpful to you, but feel free to ask more questions and provide us with more details so that we may better understand your predicament. Screen shots (captures) can be very helpful, too. Good luck! -Mike

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Block forum for a single user
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tiffany, There are a number of things that might be applicable, but I have found it useful to create a series of Roles using Student as the parent Role with different capabilities granted. Trying to work with single students was not easy but when using Roles, it is so much simpler. I keep an extensive description of what Role does what and what students have been assigned to those Roles. They revert to normal Student Role when they no longer need that capabiltiy. I have never considered denying a capability as if anyone had done something to attract my attention, that student is denied access until the matter is sorted. (Usually this has been around harassment issues but very occasonally not.) However, there is no reason to suspect that you could not have a Role that denies capabilities, in this case, the capabiity of replying to a forum, or access to the forum. Create the Role, change the permissions, assign the student to it. That should do the trick.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Block forum for a single user
ResponsesInList.Text: This is rather brief, but it is correct: http://docs.moodle.org/19/en/Useful_things_a_teacher_can_do_with_roles#Provide_temporary_read-only_access_to_a_naughty_student The steps are: Admin creates a new role called 'Naughy student' (or something more politically correct). When setting up that role, set the permission for relevant capabilities, like the forum ones, to PROHIBIT. Assign that role to the student you want to block.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Changing the message sent out for board subscribers
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Axel The format of forum subscription emails are set in the 'Email Digest' setting of an individual's profile .  The default is to receive a single email with the entire message when it is posted (or 30mins + the next cron).  Other options include receiving a daily digest with either subjects only or the full messages of each post. You could prevent subscription to your forums to force users to read everything in Moodle however this will stop any notification that there is a new message. Users should also be encouraged to visit Moodle to reply and not respond by replying to an email notification, you might want to have a look at changing the ' Use email address in reply' setting to prevent user's email in the forum subscription email (Site administration ▶ Plugins ▶ Activity modules ▶ Forum). I hope this helps Cheers Teresa

ResponsesInList.Text: Jose, I pretty much use the Seperate Group mode for most on my courses.  It comes in really for a variety of  reasons, but the best is the ability to have a private forum for each of my students, or faculty peers who teach different sections of the same course using the same course site.   I hope what follows is helpful to you...  Note that creating a seperate course is not necessary here. One way you can create a private forum for you and each parent, or in my case each student is as follows: Start by creating a single group for each parent. I name my private groups " Student name, Talk to Me... " Choose a name that makes sense to all Be sure you add the parent (student) and yourself to the group. Repeat this process as needed. I use, "Talk to Me" Create the "Talk to Me" forum (pick a name that makes sense for you. Adjust the settings as needed. Be sure the visibility setting is "Show." Save & Display the forum Verify forum Subscriptions See top left side of forum window: This forum allows everyone to choose whether to subscribe or not Force everyone to be subscribed Show/edit current subscribers Subscribe to this forum Don't track unread posts CLICK "Show/edit current subscribers" Depending on your SEPERARTE Groups selection,  you may or may not see any subscribers! Change the Groups selection by using the drop down menu to select each parent group one at a time. When you do this, you should see a list of subscribers or potential subscribers...namely you and the parent. Add each as necessary. Then select the next parent group, and repeat. Securing the privacy of the forum UPDATE this Forum Adjust the ﻿"Force everyone to be subscribed? " setting to Subscriptions not allowed." TEST the forum ...select one parent group and make a post, requesting an reply post.  Email another parent and ask if they received the post. Their responses should let you know if it works as intended. One final note.  You can use this forum to blast all subscribers to the  Talk To Me forum.  Their responses will be seen only by you. Good luck. +Allen Tvvvvv Add your Parent Use your preferred forum settings, but be sure to select "Show" groups.

ResponsesInList.Title: Locking Forum Posts
ResponsesInList.Text: Is there a way to lock forum posts so that no one else can reply to them? Thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Locking Forum Posts
ResponsesInList.Text: Here's what I do: 1) Add a forum 2) While in the forum, click Permissions from the Settings block 3) Scroll down (or use "find") to locate the "Reply to posts" and "Start new discussions" permissions (see image below). Click the plus sign (+) to add a role to the "prohibited" column. 4) Here's what is looks like after clicking the plus sign - just use the drop-down menu to select "student" as the role, and then click the "Prohibit" button as shown. 5) With those steps done for both permissions, you should see that the role of "student" now appears in the "Prohibit" column. When you want to allow posting and such, just re-enter the Permissions and delete the role from the Prohibit column by clicking the "X" next to the role(s). If there's a better way, I'm eager to hear of one. The benefit to this method is that students can prepare for an upcoming discussion, but cannot participate until everyone is "in the same room". Likewise, after a discussion has passed, students can revisit the forums to review and study for an exam, for instance, but again cannot participate or modify the posts. This, in my opinion, is far better than simply hiding a forum.

ResponsesInList.Text: (This post continues a conversation started in the tracker here: http://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-36797 ) Hi, Charles: Attached is a screenshot of what my Settings > Forum Admin > Permissions page looks like. I am logged in as an Editing Teacher (default role settings) in a forum and course I created. Looks like your Moodle admin may have adjusted the default settings for the Editing Teacher role, assuming you have that role in this course (you're not in a Non-Editing Teacher role are you?). Ask your Moodle admin about giving the Editing Teacher role in this course these forum capabilities to archive a forum. It should be a safe thing to do (it's one of the role permission defaults after all). Letting the teachers do the work of changing student forum permissions means the admin doesn't have to do it. Good luck!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Using permissions to archive a forum
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Charles, My guess from looking at your screenshot you posted a link to in the tracker issue is that your teacher role lacks the moodle/role:safeoverride capability. Here are some instructions for your admin: Go to Settings > Site Administration > Users > Permissions > Define roles Edit the teacher role and change the capability moodle/role:safeoverride to allow Click the button "Save changes" Click the tab "Allow role overrides" (in Settings > Site administration > Users > Permissions > Define roles) Check the appropriate box(s) in the teacher row to set which role(s) they can override. Most likely it will just be the student role, so check the box where the teacher row intersects with the student column Click the button "Save changes" (Steps adapted from the section 'Enabling non-editing teachers to override safe permissions' in Override permissions .) You can check out how it is for your admin by trying things out on our demo site demo.moodle.net . I obtained a permissions page just like your screenshot by logging into the demo site as an admin, editing the teacher role and removing the moodle/role:safeoverride capability (which is actually allowed by default), then logging in as a teacher and going to a forum permissions page.

ResponsesInList.Text: If anyone finds this thread from a search in the future, just posting to say I have added to the (rather sparse) FAQ number 11 here http://docs.moodle.org/en/Forum_FAQ on how to archive a forum, using Stephen's screenshot (thanks Stephen) and Helen's admin advice (thanks Helen)

So, although as an administrator, you can submit posts that are not tied to a group (when selecting the "All participants" element in the droplist), students in groups actually do not have access to these posts. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: is there a way to rate a forum and make it unread at the same time?
ResponsesInList.Text: Have you (or your campus Moodle Admin) applied the "Manual message read marking" option? When this is used, it requires the user to mark any post as "read" when they view it (just click the "Mark read" link that appears in the same area of the post as the "Reply" link does). So, even though viewing a post won't mark it as "read" (remove highlighting) automatically, I find it less of an inconvenience than trying to find one or two posts (among many) that I wanted to return to. For instance, as I read over the unfolding discussion and contributions from students, I can manually mark those as "read" that I don't necessarily want to revisit. For those that I do want to return to, I leave them as "unread". The other element is that I can change my mind and mark a post as "unread" after I manually marked it "read" initially. I do think this is quite backwards, however. The more efficient work-flow for an instructor is to have things automatically marked as read when we read them, with the option to mark them as unread as desired - not the other way around. But, I can live with this for now. Maybe version beyond 2.3 will see such a change toward efficiency and increased user-friendliness.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle 2 Read tracking: Bug or feature?
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle allows teachers to set Read tracking options within a forum and allows users to set their Forum tracking options in their profile. For the teacher setting up a forum there are three options for this setting: Optional (default) - students can turn tracking on or off for the forum at their discretion On - tracking is always on in this forum for all members Off - tracking is always off in this forum for all members If the forum setting is set to Optional, then it is dependant on the users profile setting whether read tracking is enabled. Works as expected. If the forum setting is set to Off, then there is no read tracking enabled on that forum regardless of the user setting. Works as expected. If the forum setting is set to On, then the user must have read tracking enabled in their profile settings for unread posts to be marked as such. That does not seem correct to me. I would expect that Read tracking would be enabled regardless of the user setting. Have tested this in Moodle 2.0.2, 2.0.4 and at http://demo.moodle.net/ Is this a bug or is it a feature? I guess it comes down to whether the course setting should override the users preferences? If it does for Off then I think it should also apply for On. Comments?

ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, it implies that Read tracking will always be On. This is not the case. Unless the user also has Forum tracking enabled in their profile then forum posts are not tracked. See attachment for setting.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle 2 Read tracking: Bug or feature?
ResponsesInList.Text: OK.  I think I have figured it out. There are two different settings for Forum tracking of read/unread posts and the effects of these settings are not documented.  So here goes: 1. User profile: This is a global or site wide setting.   The user must turn on read tracking in their profile or else * NO * forum read tracking settings set by the teacher come into play. 2. Forum settings: The teacher can then choose the option for the Forum Read tracking (On, Optional, Off).  This setting is for the individual forum. If On is chosen, then the student cannot disable Read tracking for this forum, except if they disable it in their User profile.  If they disable it in their profile then it is disabled for all forums throughout the site. If Optional is chosen and the student has read tracking enabled in their profile, then the student can choose to turn off Read tracking for that individual forum in the Forum settings block If Off is chosen then there is no read tracking regardless of the users profile setting A help symbol on the User profile page explaining this behaviour (e.g. Global v Individual forum settings) and better instructions within the help in the forum settings would be good.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Embedded YouTube Video not appearing in Single Simple Forum
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm using 1.9.11 but I believe everything I describe is in the same general areas. There are a couple things you will want to check if you are trying to embed videos using the Embed code. Check the role permissions to see if that role has ALLOW set for the permission TRUST SUBMITTED CONTENT. Further discussion on topic . In Site Admin > Security > Site Policies, check to see what you have for the Allow EMBED and OBJECT tags and Enabled Trusted Content settings. Read the descriptions and switch to enabled if you are sure you want to do so. Further discussion on topic . That should get you all set if you are trying to use the embed codes. The way I read the settings (someone correct me if I am wrong) is that forums work differently than other places that you will see the HTML editor. For example, a label can be created by teacher or higher role by default. So in essence, they have control of the course so they are to be trusted. The forums though have other people posting with lower permissions who may post objectable videos. So with the above settings set to No , it is stripping out the code which may contain objectable content for your own safety. A better option in my opinion is using the YouTube filter (Site Admin > Modules > Filters > Multimedia Plugins). If you have that the YouTube filter enabled, you don't have to change the above settings. To embed a video, you simply enter the URL of the video.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moving a Forum Thread to Another Forum / Course
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a thread / discussion in a forum of one class and I want to move it to the forum of another class. Can I do this?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving a Forum Thread to Another Forum / Course
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Sam You have to be careful here with your terminology - because moving a Forum thread from one Course to another is a completely different task to moving a Forum thread from one Forum to another (within the same Course).  And it's best to use the correct term.  Note that Class is difficult to interpret because Class has no specific meaning in Moodle, and could be interpreted in different ways. As a Teacher, you can easily move a thread from one Forum to another - using the "Move this discussion to..." dropdown menu that it shown when viewing a Forum thread You can move a thread to a different Course by using the Import function in the target Course (you need to be a Teacher in both).  You could then use the first technique to move the thread to an existing Forum within the target Course if you wish. Stu

ResponsesInList.Text: http://docs.moodle.org/23/en/Course_meta_link You may have to enable Course MetaLinks in your site - Settings > Site administration > Plugins > Enrolments > Manage enrol plugins But then, set up your main courses first, then set up a separate course containing just the forum - or any other resources which may be shared across the main courses [I'm using 'courses' in the moodle sense here - I think from what you have posted this equates to your 'modules'?] Then in Settings > Course administration > Users > Enrolment methods choose Course Meta Links and then choose each of your main courses in turn. You will need to set up a link for each of the courses IF you have different students on each one - IF, on the other hand,  all the same students are on all the courses then there is only a need to enrol them once via the first module they will be enroled on and you could use the same method to automatically enrol them on each of the following ones! eg Use whatever enrolment system you have to enrol the students on Course A - and automagically onto the separate CourseForum, then using course metalinks again, automagically enrol them onto CourseB, CourseC and so on - this of course depends on how exactly you organise the modules, whether they are paid for or a load of other factors! HTH Richard

ResponsesInList.Text: (I'm sharing this here in case it will be useful to someone else -- life is too short to reinvent the same wheels) I am organising optional sessions to provide students with an orientation to Adobe Connect before they are expected to use Connect in their courses or for assessment. I have found an easy way to provide a booking system is to use a forum to adertise the session and then use the Rate menu to let them register. To do this you need to setup a SCALE, then use that SCALE in the forum rating.  An advantage is that once you setup it up once it makes it very easy to add other sessions, students get to see who else has booked into the session (and when) and also if the session is full. Below is the text I in the forum description (I have also attached a screen grab). I hope this saves someone else a little bit of time. Peter Evans http://eMarkingAssistant.com Helping teachers grade papers and mark assignments electronically ---- cut here 8<--- This forum is used to book into an Adobe Connect orientation session to sort out any technical issues with your microphone, computer or internet connection before you attend a Connect session in your course. Orientation sessions are held at specific times and more sessions will be added if there is sufficient demand. The sessions start on the hour and last about 30 minutes. You should enter the room 10 minutes before the session and follow the onscreen prompts to indicate that your microphone is working or to request assistance. To attend a 30 minute orientation you should: go to the ... site which is currently located at: ... scroll down below the images to the heading that says GDLP Adobe Connect orientation sessions and click Book into an Adobe Connect orientation session select the message for the time and date you want to attend use the Rate menu at the bottom of the message to select Yes, I will attend this session , then click send in my ratings click the link next Rate menu and confirm that your name is registered at least one day before your orientation click Prep your computer or enter the 30 minute orientation session and after you enter the Adobe Connect room follow the prompts in the guided setup to ensure that your headset microphone and computer are setup correctly 10 minutes before the start of the orientation click Prep your computer or enter the 30 minute orientation session and follow the prompts to put a tick next to your name when you know that your headset is setup correctly and other people can hear you Welcome to your online meeting room. Please do NOT add your name to a session if the maximum number of people has been exceeded (your booking is stored with the date and time of the booking) CANCELLED will be added to the subject line if the session is cancelled (all other sessions will go ahead)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum Not Sending Emails
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi William, To answer the CRON question.  CRON is a Unix system daemon that can call other programs to do repetitive tasks. If you OS is a BSD then as root execute the following; crontab - u root -e On a Linux system execute sudo crontab -u root -e A editor will pop up into which you add the following; For BSD add 0/15 * * * * /usr/bin/fetch -q http://your.domain.org/moodle/admin/cron.php For Linux add 0/15 * * * * wget http://your.domain.org/moodle/admin/cron.php Save and all should work. Cron .php is the Moodle house keeper. In the example the cron job is executed every 15 minutes, change to suit you needs. I hope that translates OK for you.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: UTF-8 character set
ResponsesInList.Text: The installer can reset the charset, but it may not be the right one. For example, some cPanel installations have set to a utf-8_swedish_ci and another reported a latin_swedish_ci charset. While I do not think I have seen one of these for a while, they can still happen. You may want to look at the database and see what charset it is set up as with phpMyAdmin for My SQL , or phpPGadmin for postgres . Your host should provide you with an appropriate tool. BTW , it should be utf-8_general_ci.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Avoid student new post in question and answer forum
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Eduardo, You can accomplish this with a change of permissions for the student role. Open the forum activity and move your cursor to Forum administration (in the Settings block) -> Permissions -> Choose Students (in Advanced role override at the top). Search for “Start new discussions” and check “prevent.” Scroll down to save. Now students can only reply to your forum posts. With kind regards, Hartmut

ResponsesInList.Text: Good Day All, Iam seeing the reason behind why it work for some and not others. It seems that the change was not recorded in the database table itself.  The database table is called mdl_user. There is a heading in it called maildisplay with range 0-2..Some users are on 0 and other 1,2. To hide users's email address you would select 0. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forcing mails to be sent from the system mail(Urgent)
ResponsesInList.Text: Good Day All, I have resolved the issue. To force users to hide their email addresses in moodle 1.9.7 you need to do two thing: 1) Edit editlib.php and comment the following Comment lines… //  $choices['1'] = get_string('emaildisplayyes'); //  $choices['2'] = get_string('emaildisplaycourse');" 2) Set maildisplay column in mdl_user table to "0". To do this, the easier way is to write an SQL Query. Iam using mysql and my db so i would write " UPDATE `mdl_user` SET `maildisplay`=0." This command updates all users to 0. Thanks again for your help. Much appreciated Brian Hall

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Merging Discussion Threads
ResponsesInList.Text: I think I have found a way to do this, but please don't try this if you are unsure. It's highly experimental for me and I wouldn't want to be responsible for breaking anyone's Moodle. You need to get into the underlying database for this method, although someone (not me) may be able to create a nice comfy tool/module to do it. You can access the Moodle database structures using the MySQL Admin 2.11.9.3 plugin (http://moodle.org/mod/data/view.php?d=13&rid=448&filter=1). You would need administrator privileges for this. Look in the table mdl_forum_posts and check out the table headings. The first column is the post ID, the second is the discussion ID and the third is the parent ID. Back in Moodle, you need to find the post IDs of the post that you are trying to move and the post that you want to become its (new) parent, which you can get from the end of their URLs. Back in the database table, edit the row of the post ID that you want to move, and change the number in the third (parent ID) column to that of the (new) parent. Press go to run the SQL command to actually make the change. Go back to Moodle and observe (refresh your browser if necessary) the change in forum structure. I haven't noticed any problems so far in doing this, but I'd appreciate any expert's opinions on this method.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Merging Discussion Threads
ResponsesInList.Text: I wanted to do something like this but as I don't have access to the underlying database I did it by backing up the forum then editing the moodle. xml file I found inside. It's a similar issue - you have to alter the parent id of the post. However, you ALSO need to remove bits of the code that surround each discussion - look for the <discussion></discussion> tags, compare with previous posts and work out what needs to be there and what doesn't. Replace the original moodle.xml file with your new version and reupload the zip file. Then of course, I discovered when I restored it, that there was an error - which turned out to be that the id of the removed discussion was still present in the read tracking for the forum, so re-edit, remove all those references, and voila! Worked perfectly. I don't know yet how to write over the original forum, perhaps I can't, so I resolved it by deleting the original. Tricky first time round, but very doable. However, new question: I now have a broken forum which I don't seem to be able to delete. Solution at present is to hide it, but how can I remove it completely?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Single Simple Discussion Forum + Separate Groups - Workaround
ResponsesInList.Text: If I understand correctly what everyone here is asking for, the objective is to have only one topic (discussion) thread that only members of that group and yourself can see and reply to. Your course settings -- at course level, not forum settings -- should be set to Groups: Separate groups, Force: No. As teacher, go into your course and create a new forum with these settings: Forum type: standard forum for general use Can participants post...? No discussions, but replies are allowed. Force everyone to be subscribed? Subscriptions are not allowed. Group mode: separate groups Visible: show As teacher, you WILL have to start a new thread ("Add a new discussion topic") for EACH group. Since they are separate groups, each student will see ONLY the thread for his/her group. Students can reply to your (teacher) posts and to posts of others in their group. They can not start a new discussion. **This effectively maintains the 'single discussion' forum idea.** Since it's a 'single discussion' thread, you'll only need to do this once, so no big deal (unless you have oodles of groups). So, as teacher, click on the name of your forum, and choose the first group from the drop-down menu. Write up your post and submit it. (You may want to copy your post so that you can just paste it in to the new topic threads for the other groups.) Do this for each group. Voila! When students login, they see only 1 topic (assuming each student belongs to only one group), and they can reply to it. You as teacher can see them all and reply to all the students' replies. Yes, if you need to tell something to all groups, you will need to post that in each topic. Or use the 'all participants' if you don't want/need them to reply to that post. Remember, they can still respond to what you post in their group topic thread, they just can't directly reply to your 'all participants' post. Let me clarify confusion about force groups. In the course settings, all that 'force groups' means is that whatever you've selected--none, separate, or visible-- will be the default that shows up in all activities you add to your course. If your course settings are Groups: Separate, Force: Yes, then you can not change an activity's (such as a forum) settings to Groups: Visible. If your course settings are Groups: Separate, Force: No, then you can change an activity's settings to Groups: Visible, if you like. Let me clarify confusion about Force subscription. Subscription is the feature that sends ALL posts from a forum to ALL course users. It does not recognize groups. ALL posts in a forum go to ALL course users, always. There is NO way for a group to receive via email ONLY the posts of others in his/her group. This means that forums must be checked manually be students, since they will not be receiving email notification of a new forum post. So, if you are using Separate Groups in a Forum, set Force everyone to be subscribed to 'Subscriptions not allowed'.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: any way to list students without any posting?
ResponsesInList.Text: You are getting some good ideas from others, and I will add my two cents. Here's what I would do.  I would use the assignment method and tell all students that they must upload their files.  Then, I would use a forum, I would make the initial post, and instruct students that they are required to make at least one post commenting about their experience(s) doing the assignment, whether they liked it, had problems, any things that others should consider, any improvements to the assignment to make it more educations, etc.  So, upload a file and make one post. I think you will be very satisfied with this method, and you will learn more about the assignment than expected. Make the forum Aggregation Type = "count of ratings", and make the grade = 1.  Let students know that they will get their one point after you read their post.  Monitor the forum, and give them their points.  (By the way, you can make the points be anything that is proper for this assignment, I am only suggesting 1 as a minimum.)  Remember, you can provide a point score for their file too.  In this way, you can grade the quality of their file along with grading their quality of their posts. Once again, I think you will really enjoy reading students comments. You might want to award points for their posts immediately after reading them, so that students know that you are on top of the discussions.  You can even jump in with your own ideas.  However, depending upon the file, you might want to wait grading these until after the due date, otherwise students might start sharing their files.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: any way to list students without any posting?
ResponsesInList.Text: Wouldn't it be great to do all that in one activity? As a student, upload a file and comment on your work, possibly a few short comments targeting different aspects (which you can then group by aspect to get a better view on students perception of those aspects), all in one entry. Then the instructor can view a list of all students with their submissions and comments and grade, all in one page.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: any way to list students without any posting?
ResponsesInList.Text: The advanced uploading of files Assignment allows students to upload 1 or more files and comment on the file(s) uploaded.  The number of files (up to 20) and whether or not comments are allowed are settings that the instructor determines when the assignment is set up.  The instructor sees the file(s) and comments as a unified submission through the standard Assignment grading interface.  Advanced uploading of files also allows the instructor to send back a response file (eg, the student's file with editorial comments).

ResponsesInList.Title: Report to list Student's Activity
ResponsesInList.Text: You could run a report:- My Courses > [Course Name] > Navigation > Reports > Course Participation > The following selections will appear.  Just choose the forum name, the days back you wish to search, select "student" and "select all" for show actions. You can then see which students have and haven't posted to the forum. This report will show you the number of postings each student has posted. The good thing about this report is that you can then select the students who haven't posted by clicking the box on the right hand side and you can send a message to these by using the option below the report (that is of course if you are using the message option). Also if you have the completion tracking option chosen for your course then you could track them that way too. You would be able to run an activity report for this as well. If the student has fulfilled the set criteria (i.e. forum posting) then the activity will be marked complete.

Edit (Add): I created a forum with 'Auto subscription' in a course with 8 users (just to be sure the user's profiles didn't have any effect I tested this with three users who had ''No: don't automatically subscribe me to forums' as the auto-subscribe profile field with the others having 'Yes: when I post, subscribe me to that forum in their profile).  ALL users were subscribed to the forum immediately after I created it Therefore Derek I suggest you use 'Auto subscription' as your Yes initially option Edit: Has anyone else had issues with Auto subscription not subscribing everyone initially? ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Suprising Forum Subscription options: 'Yes Initially' missing - now 'Auto subscription'???
ResponsesInList.Text: More testing!!  I have found an issue was related to changing a forum with 'Optional subscription' to 'Auto subscription'... and the subscribers not being updated. Here are my findings: Forum created with Who is subscribed Is this expected? Optional subscription Nobody Yes - they can 'opt-in' Auto subscription Everyone Yes - they can 'opt-out' Forced subscription Everyone Yes - obviously! Disabled Nobody Yes - obviously! But... create an Optional subscription forum then change the mode, this is what happens: Forum created with Who is NOW subscribed Is this expected? Auto subscription Nobody No!! - you are even told 'Everyone is now subscribed to this forum' Forced subscription Everyone Yes - you are told 'Everyone is now subscribed to this forum' and they are Disabled Nobody Yes then create a Forced subscription forum then change the mode, this is what happens: Forum created with Who is NOW subscribed Is this expected? Auto subscription Nobody No!! - you are even told 'Everyone is now subscribed to this forum' Optional subscription Nobody Yes - they need to opt-in Disabled Nobody Yes I've created MDL-32125 for this. Cheers Teresa

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Discussion Count
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a similar situation.  In one of my courses, I expect students to make four posts.  Here's what I do. I create a "Standard forum for general use".  I put this into a "Participation" grade category.  Then, in "Ratings", I use an aggregation type of "Count of ratings", and a "Scale" = 4. Whenever students make a post that I read and think is fine, I award 1 point.  (Make sure to turn java support on, so that you can give the one point in- context .) Doing it this way, the total number of points (i.e., the grade for this discussion topic) will show up in the grade book. I am putting a couple pictures in this post that might help.  I hope that I explained my system well.  If not, ask more questions. -------------------------

ResponsesInList.Title: Grading Moodle forum posts in a less traditional way, i.e. "+1" instead of grades from 1-n?
ResponsesInList.Text: We're currently building an eLearning system and up until now Moodle 2.2.1 has been a great choice and was able to do just about everything we wanted it to do. However, one of the desired features for this system is giving me a bit more of a headache than I expected: In order to give students an incentive to post constructive feedback and questions on the forums we want to give them the ability to rate each others posts. This should not be part of their final grade, but we would like to display a public ranking of students with the most helpful post to incentivise others to follow in their footsteps. In order to increase fairness and avoid problems arising from a traditional grading scale, the students should only be able to give positive feedback for posts they liked, but no negative feedback for posts or possibly even students they may dislike. This is somewhat similar to Google's "+1" or Facebook's "Like" approach to rating content - not perfect, but it eliminates several problems of the more traditional public rating system. Sadly, I found no proper, somewhat native way of doing anything like this or even similar with Moodle's grading system. Just using a simple scale of 0 to 1 would be perfectly fine if one could display the total sum of "ones" under the post and create a small, live table of the top ranked students that the students can see. Even when chosing to display the sum of all votes, Moodle naturally caps this at the highest possible grade, one, making the result useless. So in short the features required would be: adding votes/likes/plus or similar to forum entries - this doesn't have to be overly pretty and can make use of the existing dropdown menu showing who liked/graded whom to the teachers and admins internally - this is already possible with the existing system possibly show a list of the highest ranked students to students and teacher alike Ist there any clever way of using Moodle's othwerwise incredibly powerful grading system in the way we want to, did I simply miss an existing function? Any simple hack to allow for it without sacrificing the abiliuty of somewhat painless Moodle updates in the future (tweaking a couple of lines of Moodle code would be fine as long as it can somewhat painlessly be applied to future versions)? How easy would it be to extend Moodle with this feature for someone with php knowledge and a background in php-based CMSs? Is there maybe already a plugin providing something similar? How flexible and well documented is Moodle's plugin system in this area (could one hook into the existing grading system and extend it or would one have to reinvent the wheel)?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Site News not viewable
ResponsesInList.Text: The default role for all users setting can be found in Site Administration > Permissions > User Policies . However, if the default role for all users is set to authenticated user, this will not result in news forum emails being sent. To achieve this, you need to assign all users the front page role of student. (See the Roles FAQ documentation for further details.) A simpler solution can be found in Moodle 1.9 onwards - a default front page role setting in Site Administration > Front Page > Front Page settings .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Daily Warm Up Question
ResponsesInList.Text: This should be achievable with the dataform either already or at some point in the near future. One possible application which should already work is the following. You enter the questions as entries in one dataform activity. This activity is read-only for students. Then you use the dataform view block to populate the questions to the course main page, one per day in order. The block will also display a link to add a new entry in another dataform activity which serves as the students' private file (or journal or dropbox or whatever name you wish to call it). The students' activity is set to seperate students to the effect that each student can see only his/her entries. The activity is also set to accept one entry per day. Etc. After six weeks you can review each student's entries in that entry and mark each entry or all entries as a whole. Or you can export to downloadable files and review the files. While the above scenario should already work, the dataform is not yet complete. But it should be completed by next summer and definitely for the next school year.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What to consider when choosing the moodle forum?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Kat, The first question is really your site. What is it doing? A school site? A specialist training site? Broad commercial, private interest? Who is your audience? Who is going to moderate and how well do they know their areas? These are your first questions. What is the common interest of each target group? Is the moderator respected/known? Usually the moderator is able to determine what makes a good topic, what is on/off topic, appropriate or not and so on.  If you have a group of potential moderators, turn it over to them.Talk to them and let them run with it. Let their interests run it, good moderator's forums will fly, poor moderator's forums will die. If you are on your own, then it is a different structure. How far can you narrow topics and balance work loading issues yet keep large enough sized groups to make for interesting discussions without them becoming unwieldy? You can start with one question then break out significant departures from there, or develop 4 or 5 questions and keep all discussions inside those parameters. Your profile does not give enough information to build any further on this idea, but that is where you really start.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What to consider when choosing the moodle forum?
ResponsesInList.Text: As Rick has put there, "Ask any questions about ... here" is an excellent way of getting people to go to the forum, but once there, you might propose that they look at all the questions asked and suggest they might try answer them.  You can, of course, grade them on their answers, frequency, accuracy, supportive language used/not used, any criteria you might want to apply. If the end goal is to offer life skills then using supportive language and techniques are critical to succeeding in your course.  This is what they have to show so what the forums are actually about becomes less important. I would suggest that some topics of the forums be allowed to develop organically, or holistically if you dare, and others be strictly regimented to the theme of that forum. Many people do not see those features of these forums as most questions are technical, but it is still critical to use the right language. Having a severe hearing difficulty myself, I am often concerned that I come over as too patronizing at times, but even more so here, with the written word. You might be very surprised the impact that our oral development has on our approaches to written responses, but believe me, it is very real. This is why the use of the forum in a lot of areas has benefits beyond what we immediately see.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Embed Youtube in forum
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, In fact Moodle will actively REMOVE any HTML code suitable for exploitation, like <object> and <embed> tags. Letting unknown people to upload arbitrary code with those tags will open your doors to any type of scripting attack. It is a security hole. There is an administration setting to aloow you strip/no strip <object> and <embed> tags from user input. More secure is the "trusted content" option. You can allow a defined set of people, those with "trusted content " capability to used those tags. Messages from any other peoble will be cleaned. And the more secuere option is to use a filter. There is a filter made by Eloy Lafuente (stronk7) to allow ANY user to safelly embed YouTuve or Google videos in ANY content within Moodle: Multimovie filter . There is also a side block.

ResponsesInList.Title: copying forum to a course, maintaining user names in posts, 1.9
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi. The following describes how to copy a forum from one course to another, maintaining the name of posters and the dates of the posts.  I used Moodle 1.9.x (x == 7, I think), and you need to be an Admin (or at least a Teacher with access to the source and target courses, and an empty course). I'd recommend first backing up both courses, and testing with 2 or 3 temporary/test courses. Make a backup of the source course, including all users, but only including the forum and no other modules. Restore this into an empty course (all users, all modules, which'll only be the forum).  I'll call this the copy-course. In the copy-course, unenroll all users.  This is the key for maintaining user names in posts. Backup the copy-course, including all users and user info. Restore into the target course Select the 'adding data to it' option. Keep all user data and files selected Ensure the start date is the same as the start date in the source course ... this'll ensure the forum posts' dates are the same (I believe this or something similar was mentioned somewhere at moodle.org) Post if I need to describe the above better. Other notes This can be extended to multiple forums. I tried Import, but it didn't work at all ... nothing was copied over, save for an empty forum. A simple backup/restore didn't work, as it copied over the users as well, which was not wanted (i.e., it enrolled all extra users from the source course into the target course). It is likely possible at the db level to do something similar, but this is obviously a worse way to go; if you can do something reasonably easily via the Moodle GUI, it's safer to avoid manipulating the db directly. I have no idea if it works or is needed in 2.x (e.g., Import or simpler alternatives may work in 2.x) I couldn't find at moodle.org, after extensive searching around Oct. or Nov. 2011, any instructions in the forums or docs on how to do this, which is why I'm posting it. Cheers

ResponsesInList.Title: Is Q & A forum  working in Moodle 2.0.3
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I use the  Q &A forum in our installation of Moodle 2.0.3 The time that users have to modify a post is 45 minutes, which is high but, until now, it was affecting any of the tools. When I tested the Q&A forum as a mock students, I noticed that they can view other partipant's answers before posting their own, despite the red warming of "you need to post something before browsing other people's posts" I read that there were several bugs with regard to that forum here http://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-9376 Was it fixed for Moodle 2.0.3? Is it the hight time -45 minutes- which allows users to view other people's responses before start posting something ? Thank you

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is Q & A forum  working in Moodle 2.0.3
ResponsesInList.Text: The Q & A forum restricts users from seeing others post at the discussion level, not the forum level. So if you were to create the forum and then create the first "question", students need to respond to your discussion topic, not create a new discussion topic for it to work as designed. If they just keep creating a new discussion topic, then yes anyone can see this independent of posting first. I believe it was designed this way so that you could have different "questions"/discussion topics all within the same forum. Example forum on World War II. Two separate topics: European Front & Pacific Front. Each would have their own thread and when students reply to each one, they will then be able to see the rest of the responses for that thread. One option to resolve this issue is to take away students capability from starting new discussion topics in that forum. This can be done in the Forum settings > Override permissions tab > student > Set Start new discussions to prevent. You could do this same change at the site or course level but if you did that it would take away their ability to start new discussion topics in other forum types as well (e.g. Standard forum for general use). So you may want to do this just at the forum level. Another option (which I can't verify works as I haven't used it) is to use a patch that when a Q & A forum is created, it changes that permission for you. See this tracker . It lists some code in the description that is suppose to do this. The tracker you linked to is actually a different problem altogether. It is addressing the issue that when a student responds to one of the discussion topics, they can then see everyone else's post right away. They would read everyone else's post and then depending on the editing window that is set, change their post with ideas they got from others. 45 minutes is a little long in my mind to allow for editing because you could run into students posting a dummy post, checking everybody else's and then re-editing their post. But that is my opinion. Most students are honest enough not to do that (or not smart enough to think to do that). My site is set to 30 minutes so that time limit doesn't exactly eliminate the problem either. Happy oodling!

She wanted it to be a little like the amazon reviews, where you could leave your thoughts and ratings. Currently you can have threads, with no ratings. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Book Reviews in a Forum
ResponsesInList.Text: You can allow students to rate forum posts - see the documentation here http://docs.moodle.org/21/en/Forum_FAQ

Afaict, neither the database nor the forum can sort the entries by ratings though.

My colleague needs you to be able to leave a rating for inside your OWN comment, as the ratings are not being used to rate the comment itself, but in fact to leave a score rating for a book that has been mentioned. So for example, I would suggest the book Harry Potter and leave a rating for this book of 5. The next person would leave their comment, and put their own rating in there. Over time, you would have a number of comments per book, each with a rating left by the comment author. I will continue to investigate this matter!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Book Reviews in a Forum
ResponsesInList.Text: My colleague needs you to be able to leave a rating for inside your OWN comment, as the ratings are not being used to rate the comment itself, but in fact to leave a score rating for a book that has been mentioned. Rating the book should be done on the entry/post that introduces the book and you can then view the list of ratings and raters from a link that is automatically added to the entry/post. This also allows for displaying an aggregate (e.g. highest, average). It is true that it would be nice to have the rating and the raters' comment in the same place, as your colleague envisions it, but this may not be easy to implement given the current implementations of the rating and comment components. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Editing Forum Discussions
ResponsesInList.Text:
You could change the line 
```text
        if ($age < $CFG->maxeditingtime) {
```
 to 
```text
        if ($age < $CFG->maxeditingtime or isadmin()) {
```
 in cvs :/moodle/mod/forum/lib.php. Then you as administrator could always change your own post. If you also change the preceeding line from 
```text
    if ($ownpost) {
```
 to 
```text
    if ($ownpost or isadmin()) {
```
 then you can edit anyone's posts.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Editing Forum Discussions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey guys, collaborative writing ideas in Moodle have been discussed at length before. Just search for collaborative and wiki in the search forum. A number of people have "started" projects for collaborative writing, but not finished them. In the meanwhile, if teachers really, really want to edit journals in-line, they can quickly log-in as the student, edit the journal, and use a different font color to include in-line comments. There may be limitations on discussion spaces in Moodle, but to be fair you should consider what values the existing structures impose on a community of writers. The journal is a place to think and rethink privately. The forum, however, is a public space where we respond to each other. To revise the forum is to mess with history. For example: Say I become hot-tempered in a post and flame somebody. Perhaps two other participants respond to that flame with fair criticism. If I can go back and edit out the temper-tantrum, someone will read the forum and think the two responses to my initial post were inappropriately harsh. Now when someone reads the thread, as a whole are they really seeing what transpired? The fact that we error in communication and might need to face criticism, speaks to another really significant element of the writing process: that what we say becomes permanent. I find that there is a great laziness in prose from my students because they are used to writing in instant messenger applications. Their shortcuts, their misspellings, their rants are, for the most part, written on the air. Forums should have a different feel. There should be times in the writing process when we edit and revise (read journals, exercises, assignments, workshops, etc.) but there have to be public moments when things stand as record. If I make the terrible mistake of insulting one of my students in class on a Thursday, there is no way on Friday of taking those words back. In this way, I think the forum should stand as a record and encourage everyone to consider the audience from the start. Likewise, I feel comfortable calling students on specific posts on occasion. Buddy, do you see how you didn't read the preceding posts carefully? Pal, do you see how you said something quickly in haste that has turned into an incredibly complicated debate? I would rather have his NEXT post reveal that he heard my suggestion, rather than have him revise history and make it not stand for anything. Forums are "snapshots in time" of a "public us" that I think reveal our passion, our ideas, and what we have missed. It is usually in the "what we have missed" part that we need the commentary of others in order to grow. (As I am sure that I will be lectured by other Moodlers for whatever blinds me at the moment. -- I'm ready for it!). best, Tom

ResponsesInList.Title: The philosophy underlying "no editing after 30 minutes"
ResponsesInList.Text: Tom, You've written an excellent explanation here of the philosophy underlying the "no editing after 30 minutes" limitation of Moodle.  I vote for it to be included in the FAQ! That said, this thou shalt not edit thy post after 30 minutes limitation, it seems to me, is one of the major drawbacks of Moodle.  Other popular forum software, such as phpBB and BlackBoard, all allow a person to edit his post for as long as he wants... or at least gives the admin the option of turning that  feature on or off. The option to edit one's post for as long as one wants encourages open and more honest / authentic online communication.  I have seen this transpire in my courses on Blackboard.  The reality is that most people do not use the edit feature... they're too busy.  But knowing that it's available should they need to is very comforting and encourages them to post their thoughts anyway, even if it is not perfectly written. It's not that with the "edit anytime" feature, a student would post just anything, without concern for quality-- they know that even if they edit it later, someone may have already read the first version. So they tend to use that feature responsibly, or at their own risk. Forcing a posting to be set in stone after 30 minutes, as it were, is a scary thing, especially for perfectionistic personality types, of which there are quite a few in my classes... it can discourage open and authentic reflection. I am kind of dreading showing Moodle to our students for this very reason. Almost everything else about Moodle is an improvement over BlackBoard.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: The philosophy underlying "no editing after 30 minutes"
ResponsesInList.Text: George, you say you like Tom's description (which is excellent and I totally agree with) but then you carry on as you hadn't read it. This is not just an "at their own risk" issue. Editing posts after they have been mailed out and after people have read them affects everybody. Suddenly things people remember can't be found anymore, history is revised, the fragile web of memories that makes up a community is broken. There needs to be a place where some record of interactions is preserved and forums is that place. The process of discussion is as important as a polished final text, particularly in collaborative learning. Imagine if our most public social forums (such as the mass media) could be rewritten by politicians and celebrities whenever they felt like it! Four solutions for you: Firstly, Moodle has other places for reflective rewriting, such as journals (and soon Blogs), and also places for public collaborative writing (such as Wikis, Glossaries, Exercises etc). I suspect the reason BB and PhpBB have these features is because there are no other place they could put them. Note that the 30 minutes is an admin option (you can set it anywhere from 1 minute up to 60 minutes) Secondly, 30 minutes re- editing does not mean a 30-minute limit on editing ... on your first edit you can take hours if you want. You can take weeks if you want, using a journal or your own word processor, then copy and paste into a forum. Lastly, Moodle is open source. If you truly feel your students can't deal with the change (and I strongly suggest you do real research on this before assuming it's the case) then it's a three-line hack to make it work your way. In mod/forum/lib.php and mod/forum/post.php, change this line: OLD: $adminedit = (isadmin() and !empty($CFG->admineditalways)); NEW: $adminedit = (!empty($CFG->admineditalways)); And add this to your config.php: $CFG->admineditalways = true;

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Editing Forum Discussions
ResponsesInList.Text: I think it's both patronizing and presumptuous to impose an artificial limit on editing time upon Moodle users. If Moodle admins choose to utilize "bad pedagogy" or whatever is being railed against in this thread, what business is it of the developers to impose that viewpoint when it would be trivial to give the option? Like it or not (and I don't), forums are currently the flexible and adaptable method of sharing information on Moodle. The announcements section is a forum -- we have no choice in that matter! We utilize this forum for announcing activity pairings, and these change. It is ridiculous to force us to choose between (a) abandoning the announcements, or (b) posting replies to ourselves correcting the original post, which forces students to read the entire thread before figuring out exactly what's going on. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: HOW WE CAN CHANGE DEFAULT FONT AF ALL   MOODLE  TO TAHOMA ?
ResponsesInList.Text: It can be either Themes can be set for the entire site (as normal) but they can also be set for specific users - in the user profile - and courses - in the course settings - if those settings are enabled (Site Administration> Appearance> Themes> Theme Settings) So you could have one theme for the whole site with a specific adjustment in another theme which is applied for a particular user. ResponsesInList.Text: In v1.9 the default font can be changed, but it needs to be changed in a number of places. In fact, part of the advantage of Moodle 2 themes is an easing of the hugely intricate style coding of v1.9. If you have the capability in your environment, then you may be able to make a modification at one point to affect all the styles in the theme folder. I think, in a Linux environment it will be using grep and sed and a Windows environment now actually has a grep for Windows available as well. The issue is that you have to look and see what strings you need to replace and how. If you are going to go to this bother, why not just make your own theme?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Rename News Forum
ResponsesInList.Text: I suspect that for existing courses, you're getting a cached forum name. Try this - turn editing on in a course, and then hide/show a topic or week. That should trigger a cache rebuild.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Rename News Forum
ResponsesInList.Text: When the news forum is created, the name of the forum is "News forum" (depending of the language, of course). Even if you rename "News forum" in the forum.php file, the existing news forums keep their name "News forum". So, you have to execute the request : UPDATE forum SET name = "NEW_NAME" WHERE type = 'news' and name = 'News forum" But I discovered that it is not enough ! You have to rebuild the cache course as well ! The forum name is also in the field modinfo of the course table. This field is used as cache. Even if you execute the previous request, when you visit a course, the old name still displays. To display the new name, the cache course must be rebuilt. If you edit the forum, the new name will appears in the name field and when you saved the page, the cache course is rebuilt. More information here : - modinfo in the course table (2005) - a problem with modinfo field in mdl_course database table (2008) - courses and modinfo (2007) I think that the best is to call the function rebuild_course_cache($courseid), where $courseid is the id field of the course. Pascal

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Rename News Forum
ResponsesInList.Text: I realised that the script admin/replace.php calls the function rebuild_course_cache. So I wrote the attached script "rebuild_course_cache.php" from replace.php where I only kept the last code lines about rebuilding course cache. I tried it on my test website and it works. You can download it from my post and try it. If there is something wrong with my script, tell me ! Be carefull ! Use this script on a test website before to make sure everything is ok with your moodle ! And anyway make a backup of your database ! To rename all news forum on a moodle website already in use : - rename "News forum" in the forum.php file via Language moodle menu - execute the request in your database : UPDATE forum SET name = "NEW_NAME" WHERE type = 'news' and name = 'News forum" - copy the script attached to the folder /var/www/moodle/admin and execute it by calling : http//yourwebsite.com/admin/rebuild_course_cache.php

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can't get scaled response options to show below forum posts
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Erlyn Seeing the rating for another user makes sense, you cannot rate yourself!! I can suggest you also check the permissions for the student role in this forum (or the current course) to allow students to rate posts and see all ratings rather than just their own. I think you could do this at course level as it sounds like you've got other forums that you'll want this in too!  To override permissions at course level click 'Assign roles' from the course Admin menu, Click the 'Override Permissions' tab then select the role you'd like to override (in this case the Student role).  Find the ' Rate posts mod/forum:rate ', the ' View any ratings mod/forum:viewanyrating ' and the ' View ratings mod/forum:viewrating ' permissions and ensure the student have these set to "Allow".  To do this for the one forum click 'Update this forum' from the forum rather than 'Assign roles' from the course, then follow the above steps With regard to the grade received for the ratings, I believe the numeric values for your scale (Very Average - Try Again!, Very Good - I like it!, Excellent - Let's see more like that!) would be 1/3 for Very Average, 2/3 for Very Good and 3/3 for Excellent - because you are using 'Sum'. Non-Numeric Scales on 1.9 Moodle Docs outlines other scale examples and their respective values which might be helpful! ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Automatically Grading Forums
ResponsesInList.Text: You can set the forum ratings to count of ratings and that will be part of what you want but that means the instructor still has to rate each post. To have the forum automatically award points based on a student posting means a student could post a one letter post and receive credit for an entire post. There has to be some sort of accountability to check for quality. There is a similar discussion in this forum thread where Bruce Long also makes a recommendation. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Automatically Grading Forums
ResponsesInList.Text: By default , the student role does not have permission to rate others on forums but you may want to check how your system has that permission set just to confirm. The count of ratings gives a point for every post that receives a rating. So if a student were to make five posts and the teacher gave a rating to each one, they would receive 5 points. If the teacher determined that one of their posts wasn't of any quality, he could leave it blank and not rate. The student would then not gain that point. Happy oodling!
