ResponsesInList.Title: Point Based Grading
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm hoping someone can help me. I teach a course that is point based, each assignment is worth so many points, with a total at the end of the semester of 300 points. But we ahve them broken up in categories, for example: Journal Assignments = 15 points (One point per assignment) Class Assignments = 90 points (10 points per assignment) Attendance = 85 points (about 14 points per class) Participation = 85 points (about 14 per class) Final Assignment = 25 points with possability for extra credit for a maximum total of 300 Based on their points, is what their grade is: Points                          Grade 285 – 300                    4.0 278 – 284                    3.7 270 – 277                    3.3 255 – 269                    3.0 248 – 254                    2.7 240 – 247                    2.3 225 – 239                    2.0 218 – 224                    1.7 210 – 217                    1.3 195 – 209                    1.0 Less than 195              0.0 I have played around for 3 days trying to set things up right, and I just can't seem to figure it out. Any assistance would be greatly appreciated. Thanks, R.J.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Point Based Grading
ResponsesInList.Text: Think I got it, nevermind.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Point Based Grading
ResponsesInList.Text: RJ, Even though you have it, I would like to offer some thoughts for you and others. I prefer to set up categories, and then think in terms of percent per category.  Then, if Participation and Attendance is worth 50%, I make this worth 50 points in this category.  Well, you might ask why. Once I have set up a category like this, it gives me the flexibility to not have to worry how many attendance items go into this category.  I can have 10, 13, whatever.  I can make each attendane item be worth anything, such as 5 points.  Moodle will then add up the points for all of these items, and calculate a percent of the 50 points in this category.  I don't need to worry about how many items I have.  I use the "simple weight mean of grades" aggregation for these "points" categories. Usually, in at least one category, I use "mean of grades".  This scheme tallies up the pecentages per assignment.  I do this when I use in-class clickers.  You see, some days I might have 9 questions, some days 5, etc. However, I want each day equally weighted just in case a student misses a day when there were 9 questions.  If I used a "points" scheme, this student would be penalized more for this 9-question day than a student who missed a 5-question day. I know this grading gets a little complex, and there are so many ways to do it.  In products like Blackboard and WebCT, you are almost forced to think about how many assignments you will have, and whether you are going to use "points" or "percentages."  But in Moodle, you don't have to do this.  Furthermore, at the beginning of the semester when you have few graded items (like 20 out of the 300), using my method would still accurately produce a proper grade based upon what has so far been graded. Let me know if you need me to better explain this.  You can look at one of my syllabi on my website to see how I communicate these grading categories to my students.  You will notice that I say nothing about how many individual assignments will be in each category (because I never know). Here's another great thing about Moodle.  If you decide to change the points (percentages) in any of the categories, you can!  Maybe you later decide that Attendance should be only 45 points, and exams should be 30 points.  Just make the change and Moodle recalculates everything. Now this is really great! By the way, your extra credit is pretty simple to do.  I try to keep my extra credit in a category that has "Simple weighted mean of grades". If your Participation is really in-class participation, you might consider using (experimenting) with the "mean of grades" for this category.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to change the Default setting in profile for subscribing to forum posts
ResponsesInList.Text: Here is how you can change the default settings: 1. Open File=moodle/user/editlib.php in a html editor (e.g. Dreamweaver) 2. Search for "autosubscribe" and you'll find this line of code: $mform->setDefault('autosubscribe', 1); 3. Alter this text to read as follows: $mform->setDefault('autosubscribe', 0); 4. You might want to use this opportunity to alter the default for tracking forums.  It is currently set to 0=false.  I prefer that new students would have this on since it allows them to easily see what posts they have not read .  To do this, change the code as follows: $mform->setDefault('trackforums', 0); -->  $mform->setDefault('trackforums', 1); 5. Save your changes and PUT the revised editlib.php to your server .  This will allow all future subscribers to have the autosubscribe set as "false" [=0] and, if you used step #4, to have the trackforums set as "true" [=1]. Aaron Rose-Milavec Catherine of Siena Virtual College Moderator@fuse.net

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Emails not going to all enrolled
ResponsesInList.Text: We identified a resolution for our forum email problem.  Here was our scenario and the fix in case this helps others. Scenario: Our course has multiple forums (one per week).  We found that some students were getting emails for some forums, but not everyone was getting emails.  When we investigated further, it became clear that students received emails for forums to which they had previously posted and not to forums to which they had not yet posted. This was due to the combination of these settings: Student profiles included this setting for Forum auto-subscribe: “Yes, when I post, subscribe me to that forum”. Each of the forums in the course was set to “Allow everyone to choose to subscribe”. The combination of these settings resulted in students getting emails for forums only if they have posted to the forum already. To fix this, we did the following: Force subscribed everyone in the class to every forum. De-enrolled all of the students. Re-enrolled all of the students. The force subscription then took effect. Hope this helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum emails - quick question
ResponsesInList.Text: The Mail Now setting decides when the forum post goes out to the cron to then process the email notifications. If a user does not check the Mail Now setting, then that user will have 30 minutes to edit the post before it is sent to cron to then email. If a user does check the Mail Now setting, then the post will be sent to cron and the user does not have the option to edit the post anyway. I believe how you have cron set up and how frequently you have it set up to run decides when the email notifications go out.

ResponsesInList.Title: Q&A Forum Instructions
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, I work at the University of Illinois to create Moodle courses for our instructors and help them understand how to use Moodle. Many of our instructors had questions on how to set up a Q&A Forum on Moodle 1.9.9. When we directed our instructors to moodle.org for help, they still had questions on how to set it up. I want to get your opinion. I posted the instructions that we came up with below. Are these instructions helpful? Is there anywhere else we could direct the instructors for help? Thanks! Q and A Forum Help Article The Q and A Forum is a great instructional tool for instructors to require students to respond to a question or prompt before reading what their peers think. This kind of activity works well to foster original thinking while reducing the “me too” posts that can be common in discussion forums. Unfortunately, the default settings for the Q and A Forum need to be modified for it to function as intended. In most cases when using a Q and A Forum, an instructor should be the only user starting new threads (discussion topics). Students will then respond to the instructor’s threads and then they will be able to view and respond to their peers’ posts. When setting up a Q and A Forum, instructors should not include the discussion questions, and/or prompts to which your students should respond in the Forum introduction. The Forum introduction is the place to inform students that they should respond to each of the discussion threads first before being able to view and respond their peers’ posts. The threads posted by the instructor should be the discussion questions and/or prompts to which the students should respond. A Q and A Forum should always have at least one thread started by the instructor before students access it. To configure the Q and A Forum to work as described above, make the following changes: Create a Q and A Forum and add a general Forum Introduction. Access the Override permissions tab. Select the Student role. Set the Start new discussions permission to prevent. Save the changes. Save the forum. Add a new question or prompt for your students to reply to before seeing their peers’ responses. Add as many new questions or prompts as desired for this Q and A Forum activity.

ResponsesInList.Title: Auto-subscribe all users?
ResponsesInList.Text: I've read some older posts regarding this subject, but wasn't clear on how to do this.  I would like to set all courses on my site so that all students are subscribed to the forums whether they post or not (since some students are "lurkers" and do not post, but want to receive all posts).  Is there a way to do this to make sure all current students in a course receive digest whether they subscribe themselves or not? Thanks, Vikki

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Auto-subscribe all users?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Vikki In your Forum settings page, you should have the option to Force everyone to be subscribed - either No; Yes, initially; or Yes, forever. You will need to set this for each Forum that you want to force their subscription. From the Moodle help pages... "...if you choose to force subscription on a particular forum then all course users will be subscribed automatically, even those that enrol at a later time. "This is especially useful in the News forum and in forums towards the beginning of the course (before everyone has worked out that they can subscribe to these emails themselves). "If you choose the option "Yes, initially" then all current and future course users will be subscribed initially but they can unsubscribe themselves at any time. If you choose "Yes, forever" then they will not be able to unsubscribe themselves. "Note how the "Yes, initially" option behaves when you update an existing forum: Changing from "Yes, initially" to "No" will not unsubscribe existing users, it will only affect future course users. Similarly changing later to "Yes, initially" will not subscribe existing course users but only those enrolling later." But...! This is different to them receiving a daily Email Digest. They will only receive the email posts/daily digest if they're subscribed to the Forums, so you will still need to do the above on each Forum that you want to force their subscription.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Inserting jpegs, gifs, or pngs into Moodle 1.9 Forums
ResponsesInList.Text: My students have been able to do this for awhile.  Might it be that your administrator has set the file size of the attachment to 0MB?  This is a system setting.  Right now, mine is set to 2MB. ResponsesInList.Title: Specify only few users in one of the forum
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I want to create a forum where only selected users are able to view or participate. Preferably, only user with the rights can see it in their page and rest of the users are not able to view the forum in the first place. Thanks in advance.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Specify only few users in one of the forum
ResponsesInList.Text: You should set up groups and then groupings. You can see more information on groupings in the Moodle Doc - Groupings . Make sure you have grouping enabled though first. You can then create a group of users you want to see it and a group of those you don't want to see it. Then create groupings that just mimic your groups. So you will have 2 groups and 2 groupings. Each grouping only has one group in it. Then in the forum settings, select visible or separate groups and select the designated grouping. On the course homepage then, the users in the grouping that can see it will see no change while those not allowed to see it won't see the forum at all.

Average of ratings - The mean of all ratings Count of ratings - The number of rated items becomes the final grade. Note that the total cannot exceed the maximum grade for the activity. Maximum - The highest rating becomes the final grade Minimum - The smallest rating becomes the final grade Sum - All ratings are added together. ResponsesInList.Title: Forum not sorted by date
ResponsesInList.Text: I thought that forums were automatically sorted by the date of the last posting.  I now have a forum where recent postings are not appearing at the top.  Does anyone know if this is a setting or if it might be a bug? thanks in advance. Brian

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum not sorted by date
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Brian, The default view of a forum in Moodle is to "Display replies in nested form." This means that the newest replies are generally at the bottom in order of receipt based on the reply. So each direct reply to a post is nested beneath the original post with the newest at the bottom. If you want to see the newest posts at the top then you need to go to the top of the forum page and select "Display replies flat, with newest first" from the drop down list. Hope this helps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: save discussion threads

From here you can just save the file and resistribute and/or print at will. I have used this numerous times and it works great.

ResponsesInList.Title: ForumNG: advantages and disadvantages
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everyone, I thought it might be useful to have a list of ForumNG pros and cons - you can download it from Google docs: forumng.2.34.zip. (I've put it here because I don't find it easy to locate.) I'm not sure my list is complete - can anyone help? Cheers, Glenys Advantages Advanced DHTML / AJAX (dynamic web page) support in the discussion page, which allows you to reply to, edit, rate, and delete posts without leaving the page. Unique (only) discussion view which combines the benefits of 'nested' and date-related views; it is a nested view, so you can see the discussion structure, but except for unread posts (and their immediate parents), posts are 'collapsed' to a short summary, so you don't have to scroll through mounds of junk to get to the unread posts. Expanding a post is one click away. Thanks to 2), when replying to a post, the whole previous discussion can be visible, not just the previous post. Up to 3 attachments can be added. Ability to merge discussions. Forum locking. Save as draft. "Change subject (optional)" appears when replying as hint to do so if necessary. Permalink: a direct link to a particular posting. Export to Word. Show readers: list of people who have viewed the discussion via the website even if they haven't posted. The rating system has friendly star graphics (this can be modifed to whatever you want) and can be used for grading or without a grade. Sticky discussions - choose to have a discussion stay on top of list. Mark posts as important. Popup message warning you to copy the message before refreshing the page. Popup Warning: You must save any changes to this post before 10:19 AM. After that time you will no longer be allowed to edit the post. Disadvantages Images uploaded as attachments by students form their hard disks do not appear in the body of a message. - they appear as attachments. This was at the request of OU testers. I'd really like to have this as an option in 1.9. In 2.0 students can upload images anywhere directly through the HTML editor. Not integrated with Moodle core features: Does not appear in the 'list of all a user's posts". Not integrated with the Latest Course News block. A post is considerd "empty" and won't post if there is no text, only an image. To include teachers in "Force eveyone to subscribe" the teacher ID "3" has to be manually added by the Admin to the list of Subscriber roles in the ForumNG settings.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: ForumNG: advantages and disadvantages
ResponsesInList.Text: Re advantage 4 and disadvantage 1: In Moodle 2.0, you can attach multiple files to a forum post in the standard forum, and in the Moodle 2.0 version of Forum NG you can embed images using the HTML editor like you can here. Therefore, you can cross those two off your list now. Dis 2.1: This feature would have to be added to Forum NG if it was ever proposed that Forum NG be added to core. Dis 2.2: Arguably, course news is not really a forum, and it might be better to make the course news system entirely independent of forums anyway. That is not my idea. I think I have heard Martin D saying it. Dis 4. may be fixable now considering the new way of handling enrolments in 20, but I am not sure. In terms of what "Refactor of the Forum module" on the roadmap means. Well, we have basically not been talking to HQ about this since the initial vague discussions ages ago that established that ForumNG becoming the standard forum was one possible option. HQ have clearly been busy with 2.0. sam has been working away busily at a 2.0-compatible version of Forum NG. Once there is a finished 2.0 version of Forum NG, it will be easy for HQ to evaluate it for real, rather than hypothetically, so there is no real harm done that the conversation has not started yet. I'm obviously biassed, but I am now using Forum NG  on the OU course I am studying, as well as using the forums here, and Forum NG is definitely nicer to use. The extra slickness in the interface makes things just a little bit easier. The one I particularly use is being able to see all the posts in a thread while writing a reply. (I just had to open Derek's post in a new tab to see something in it.) Also the fact that when you want to reply to two different posts in the same very active thread, you don't lose your place or your unread markers when making the first reply. Not that standard Moodle forums are at all bad. I like them a lot, but the little UI improvements in NG are worth it. I have never had to look very closely at the ForumNG code. I have worked on sam's code in the past and it is generally very good, but before becoming such a critical part of Moodle, the code would have to be scrutinised very closely. In terms of making a decision, I am sure that Martin will find it helpful to hear the opinions from as many different users as possible (I have no doubt that the developers will let him know what they think of the code behind the scenes). I would encourage you all to contribute to this thread.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Emails not going out from any forums - New Moodle 2.0 install
ResponsesInList.Text: We identified a resolution for our forum email problem.  Here was our scenario and the fix in case this helps others. Scenario: Our course has multiple forums (one per week).  We found that some students were getting emails for some forums, but not everyone was getting emails.  When we investigated further, it became clear that students received emails for forums to which they had previously posted and not to forums to which they had not yet posted. This was due to the combination of these settings: Student profiles included this setting for Forum auto-subscribe: “Yes, when I post, subscribe me to that forum”. Each of the forums in the course was set to “Allow everyone to choose to subscribe”. The combination of these settings resulted in students getting emails for forums only if they have posted to the forum already. To fix this, we did the following: Force subscribed everyone in the class to every forum. De-enrolled all of the students. Re-enrolled all of the students. The force subscription then took effect. Hope this helps!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Can i create a course independent forum?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Heinser, As I understand Moodle, everything in the platform is inside a 'course'. For example, the front page of Moodle is usually the course #1. So you cant create a forum outside of a course. But you can create a course only for your forum. For example, you could create a course, like an open one only for teachers, and then insert a forum activity in it. The inscription to this course could be limited for the users that have the login key, and you give that key to your teachers. Then, you create a link in your front page (like in an HTML block). This link can point directly to the forum if you whant, just use the direct URL when you are in the forum front page. When a teacher click on the link from the HTML block in the site front page, he is oriented to the page where he must enter the login key (the first time only). After that, he have access to the forum from the front page of your site. Hope that help! JF

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Approval period?
ResponsesInList.Text: I appreciate that there are circumstances in which having a moderated forum discussion which requires the approval by a teacher can be useful. However as I have continued to think about this issue, I have become less convinced that doing such is a good idea. My concern is that if it is a moderated discussion to what degree does it remain a discussion. I often advocate that in developing policies and handling issues in online courses follow the same types of responses that one would expect in the classroom. So when I read that a parent might be upset because a student made an inappropriate response, I am concerned why the parent is reading the posts of other students. Here in the U.S. the parent has a right to know what their own child writes; however, not those of other students. Further, most parents are not allowed to sit in the traditional classroom. Further, in that classroom the teacher does not ask each student to tell that teacher what they want to say to the class before they say it. There is a general sense of trust that in a discussion, each person is free to say what they feel is appropriate. If a student makes an inappropriate post (or comment in the classroom setting) I have disciplinary measures in place to deal with those situations. I might even go as far as to argue that an inappropriate post might not necessarily be deleted but that it might serve as an opportunity to discuss why it is inappropriate (or even if it is inappropriate). So are censored discussions really discussions? Of course one could also argue that they are forums, places for comments to be stored. So I can see where it may be helpful to have the ability to censor discussions but I am not sure that we should. I would be interested in hearing what folks think. On one side one could say that we could just add it and leave it up to the teachers to use it or not. On the other there is the concern for feature bloat. When we throw in the social constructionist pedagogy that Moodle is influenced by perhaps we get to a point when we say that a certain feature is not pedagogically consistent with how the tool is intended to be used. I think there are several factors to consider here but I am realizing that I need to be careful about just saying any feature we can program in fact ought to be in Moodle. I look forward to reading what others think about this but it is certainly more complicated than I initially thought. Peace - Anthony

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Approval period?
ResponsesInList.Text: As I have mentioned in the tracker, this option is often requested but when asked how it might work in practice unless forums are constantly monitored those who seek this facility are less clear about how they would manage it in practice. I understand the use cases put forward - I hear them frequently enough in my work with clients. Incorporation of this would undoubtedly change the nature of many discussions (if they would still be 'discussions'). It would be a big step for Moodle IMO .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Approval period?
ResponsesInList.Text: What if this feature was setup as a separate module...a Moderated Forum module...that admins could add to their moodle setup (or even replace the un-moderated module for setups that would require it). While your thoughts are good...there is a great deal of difference (especially at the public K-12 School Level) between the immediacy of comments made in a classroom (combined with comments made by the teacher immediately in response) and those comments made online. Afterall, the comments made on a moodle forum are already delayed by 30 minutes by default. That lag in and of itself could cause a great deal of confusion to the ongoing "discussion"...for instance, a student comments on another student's comments. 10 minutes later another student comments on the same comment. When the original student sees the first response and makes their "defense", it is still ten minutes before they see the second student's comments which could either hurt or help their case (in the event of a heated disagreement/debate type setup). If we want a true discussion then maybe we should be moving the other way where we don't have the 30 minute lag time...I still think giving administrators the option of have both available could be a benefit if we don't go the way of allowing individual teachers to setup the modules with the moderation option. With moodle being designed for scholastic uses, it seems logical that the safeguards that would be expected would be included. The reason I use Moodle instead of other more open social networking tools is due to the control that a teacher has the opportunity to maintain over the course and its activities .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Approval period?
ResponsesInList.Text: I understand what you're saying Anthony. However, the reality of many situations is that we need to be able to moderate discussions. In some situations we cannot use discussions that cannot be moderated. How many Web 2.0 tools are blocked in public schools because we have no control over the content. We could have a philosophical discussion about these policies and the social constructionist pedagogy that would be quite interesting. However, that discussion is would get us nowhere if we can't use the tool because of lack of a feature. I know in our current LMS (ANGEL) we can turn moderation on or off for discussions forums. I believe the same capability is in Blackboard. We can moderate YouTube comments (and I wish more people would). We can moderate blog comments. It doesn't seem unreasonable to be able to moderate Moodle discussion furum comments. I know for a practitioners viewpoint, the inability to moderate posts will be a touchy policy area as we move to Moodle. I vote for the availability of forum moderation.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: News Forum Force Everyone to be subscribed does not subscribe any community members
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Laren, We had a similar problem with one of our clients, and the problem turned out to be the Initial subscription (' mod/forum:initialsubscriptions ') capability. Only users who have the ' Allow ' permission for this capability will receive emails from forums that are force-subscribed. For force-subscribed forums, subscribers are not kept in the forum_subscribers table, hence their not showing up in your query results. We only found this out after looking at the code of the forum module. It seems unusual to use that capability to determine who should receive emails for force-subscribed forums, especially as there is a 'View discussions' capability. The way the module currently works, it is impossible for an admin or teacher to prevent users from subscribing themselves while allowing them to view discussions (and receive emails). The natural way to do that would be to use the ' mod/forum:viewdiscussion ' capability to determine people who get to see or view postings in force-subscribe forums. What we did for our client was to set the ' mod/forum:initialsubscriptions ' capability to ' Allow ' for the site default role, but you could obviously set it for the appropriate role and context in your own situation. Hope that helps. Muyi

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sorting Forums
ResponsesInList.Text: Mike, Well, moving forums from one week to another is a simple task: you turn on editing and use the up/down icon next to the forum title, click that and you get box selectors in every week so you can choose where to move this to (or did I entirely misunderstand point 2?). You can move forums from one course to another (and hence between categories) using backup and restore, with some care... Before doing the move check that the forum has a different name from anything in the target course - if only to remove confusion! In the donor course click backup. Untick all resources except the named forum you want to move and its matching 'user data'. Set all the other options to No or None except the Users which stays at 'Course' otherwise the forum is switched to without user data mode, and that will give you an empty forum!. Once the backup is completed you can restore it from where it is to its new location. Click restore beside the filename. It should respond with 'Later in this process you will have a choice of adding this backup to an existing course or creating a completely new course' which is what you want. (If not you would be obliged to move the file first) Click Continue. Check the next panel to see what you are restoring and click Continue.

ResponsesInList.Text: It appears that we resolved this by having the instructor not only create the forum but seed it with the first entry. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Q&A Forum type - students see all posts at outset
ResponsesInList.Text: One problem could be that your students are posting their replies as new threads, which are available for everyone to see. To properly use the Q&A forum in 1.9.x, you should set up the forum with its general introduction, use permissions override to remove the ability for students to start new threads, and have the instructor post the questions that students will respond to as individual threads within the forum. When the students go to the forum to post, they need to go into each of the threads set up by the instructor to post their reply as a reply, not a new thread.  Once they have posted a reply to a specific thread, then they will be able to see replies of other students to that thread.  They still will not be able to see the replies of other students in the other threads, not until they have posted their reply there. It would make more sense if the default setting on the Q&A forum would be that students are not allowed to start new threads.  unfortunately that's not the case.  This issue was the source of lots of confusion and consternation here for some faculty who wanted to use the Q&A forum, until I showed them how to ensure that students were posting within the instructor-created threads.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Configuring Moodle so it sends forum emails out through Google SMTP
ResponsesInList.Text: If you look at the Moodle Docs on the subject " Important warning : When sending emails, Moodle attempts to send them "From" the email address of the user writing the message, this allows the recipient to reply directly to the sender via email. Google, both in their Gmail and Apps for Education product do not allow this - so any emails sent from the system will be from the account you use to authenticate on the SMTP server . To make things more confusing, the name will be the recipients, but the email address will be the SMTP account's email address, for example: "Dr Fred Bloggs" <moodlemail@mycollege.edu>. This does not render the Gmail useless for Moodle, emails all come with a link you can click through and reply on Moodle, but it is important you understand this limitation before continuing with this setup. If you wanted to use Gmail's SMTP regardless, you would be advised to use a dedicated account for the purpose, and have an auto response so that messages to the address bounce back with an instruction to click on the link in the email and reply through Moodle." Google appear like other relay hosts to do masquerading.  There is no way around this except use another relay host . Is there any reason you can not use your ISP as a mail relay? John

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Site News - "No news has been posted yet"
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Ok, it seems the way to fix this issue is to visit your moodle database using something like phpMyAdmin . Find the offending forum (news forum that will not delete) and look for the instance ID (this can be found from the rss feeds). The forum ID number and the instance ID numbers are different. From the mdl_forum table find the Instance ID of the forum. Delete the forum directly from the table. The un-deletable forum is now gone, however there is still reference to it in the mdl_course_sections table and requires removing. To remove the entry find the course number in question, (the news forums are always found in the topic outline (section 0). Find the Forum ID number (not the instance ID) and remove this from the 'sequence' field of the table. Now you have successfully managed to remove the forum we now need to assign the old restore forum to behave as a 'news' forum. It seems that restored forums do not get restored as news and are set as 'general disscussion forums'. So we need to visit the mdl_forum table. Find the ID & Instance ID of the forum to update. When you have located the forum simple alter the field 'type' from general to news and save/update the table. You can then visit the course from within moodle and move the forum to whatever section you want. The 'Recent Activity' side block now works. The 'Recent News' side block now works. I have not noticed any issues, however if you have set rss feeds you may rss also want to remove entries within the mdl_block_rss_client table and delete the rows which apply to any said forums. That should do the trick! Hope this helps someone else. Steve www.vocationaltraining.org.uk

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Login from script outside of moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Anthony, from what Richard is describing it is similar to our (my organization's) need to develop a single login and authentication process for a range of PHP Apps. Martin developed a script to accommodate MediaWiki some time ago, but that was just not robust enough for our need. Some organizations have developed something that may or may not work in limited scenarios, but for me, there should be a single login and authentiction process, a standardised module if you like, that could be easily adaptable to all PHP Apps. For me, this would be much better than trying to integrate lots of different PHP Apps into a single tool, less risky from a coding perspective as well. (I do not have the PHP skills to do this myself, so have no real idea as to how difficult this would actually be.)  Perhaps the tool would be a login script, then a distribution to such Apps as used or a set of adapters in each App that can meet the App's authentication processes that receive data from the login script. Alternatively, a script that builds a single authentication table in a database with each App accessing that database for their authentiction processes would allow a more consistent approach, that all App makers could use, but i am not sure that PHP is either fast enough or flexible enough to use multiple databases at the same time in this manner. I would suggest that if this was possible and was to be done, and a set of Apps say, Moodle, Mahara , MediaWiki, WordPress, phpMyAdmin be bundled as a complete LMS\social tool,  it would be a very popular bundle very quickly. I understand that these are all, in some ways, "competing" products, but reality suggests that "one-size fits all" approaches are doomed to failure. Keeping the options open is a better approach, for me anyway.

ResponsesInList.Text: Not a silly question, Anthony, a very pertinent one. I would suggest it is more revealing of my own lack of knowledge of networking stuff actually. (The only one I have heard mentioned by name is IChain, and I am not sure that is even how it is spelt, and I have no idea how it is done in the Moodles I am an admin for now.) This sort of thing seems to move into realms of networking that most of the people I have worked with do not ordinarily use, do not really understand. I suspect that this is a structural thing that my employers are going to have to make a decision about soon though. Here it is, my employers decided to use Moodle, at the encouragement of a prominent member of the Oz Moodle community, and good for him. His company provide the Moodles, the servers and everything else, at a cost I assume, and we access them. Each school in the State, (which is nearly twice the size of Texas and about 1/20th the population,) has one Moodle, which makes about 400 odd Moodles, not all of which are being used - and few are being used extensively. My argument is that Moodle on its own fills a purpose, but it is not all things, and we should not make it all things. We need to use other PHP Apps, which need to be on the same server as our Moodles, and thusly we need a single login to access all of them. I doubt that LDAP will meet that need, as the Moodles are not on the same servers as each school. In short, it is a bit of a nightmare, but it is getting to the point where others are recognising that Moodle on its own is going to be insufficient to meet all our needs. We need Mahara, we need Mediawiki, and I would suggest we also need WordPress. I have all these set up on my private server and I do not understand enough about PHP to develop my own  single login. But we need it - if not right now, then in a year or two. I am also quite sceptical about the longer term economic health of the world, so delivering cheaper school support services that will last for many years without replacing the computers, the servers or the software, is going to be a high priority. As licensing will become a thing of the past, as most of the existing companies will disappear,  even Microsoft and Adobe, and Apple, and be replaced with who knows, we will need to depend on Open Source, and have people who can run fixits, make patches and so on, just to keep things going - but that is another story.

ResponsesInList.Title: Post Threshold for Blocking -- Teachers vs. Students
ResponsesInList.Text: I am confused about the Post Threshold For Blocking for forums. When I just tested this for a Q&A forum it seems that students were not limited to the post threshold, but the teacher for the course was. This is odd, as it seems contrary to the help for that setting (copied below). I had set the threshold to 2 and the warning to 1. This was applied to the teacher (which I don't think it is supposed to). It warned the teacher at 1 post and did not let them post a third post. It did not warn the student at all and the student was able to make 3 posts. Isn't this the reverse of the way it should be? We are using v1.8.2+ Thank you! The concept of managed postings is very simple. Users will be blocked from posting after a given number of posts in a given period, and as they approach that number, they'll be warned that they are approaching the threshold. Setting either the warn threshold to 0 will disable warnings, and setting the block threshhold to 0 will disable blocking. If blocking is disabled, warnings will automatically be disabled. None of these settings affect teachers posting

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Combining Quiz Results
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Nick I would suggest create separate quiz activities , one for each subject.  The score for these will of course filter through to the gradebook.   If you set the Aggregation of the course to 'Sum of grades' the total of the quiz scores will be the course total.  If you have other graded activities in the same course, you can add a grade category to hold the quizzes.  The category total is then the combined score if you set the aggregation to 'Sum of grades'. I hope this helps Cheers Teresa

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum: Email notification even though suscription is not allowed
ResponsesInList.Text: If you have access to your database through phpmyadmin, then just do the following. 1. Select the mdl_user table 2. Click on the pencil (to edit) beside autosubscribe 3. Change the default value from 1 to 0 The above will change the default value for all new accounts. 1. Select the mdl_user table 2. At the top, click on SQL 3. Erase what is in the query field and enter the following: UPDATE mdl_user SET autosubscribe = 0 4. Press "Go" This will change all existing accounts to "No: don't automatically subscribe me to forums". Note: It's always a good idea to back up your database before doing anything like this. Use at you own risk. Steve

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: looking for suggestions for debugging problem sending emails of forum posts (about 1/3 of people are not receiving it)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Peter, We had a similar problem with Siteground due to limits on the number of e-mails our account could send at one time (they do this to try to prevent SPAM , I think). Siteground provide an amazingly good value service, but this is one area where the limits placed on the account can be a pain. The basic account is to my knowledge only 40 e-mails at a time and the premium is 80 e-mails at a time, so the fact that you are getting more than that means that you may already have a higher level account or you might have some sort of e-mail handler in there to split it into more than one session. This is certainly your best bet, but I don't have the technical knowledge for how that is best done. We ended up either reducing the number of people on a forum to our maximum number of e-mails permitted, or we removed subscriptions altogether and then sent e-mails out in batches referring to the forum post using the messaging system. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Embed Player into Forum Post
ResponsesInList.Text: Unless your system has "Allow EMBED and OBJECT Tags" under Site Policies set to Yes (the default is No), then Moodle will strip out any embed and/or object tags and the code associated with them.  You can ask your system admin to set this system setting to yes, but they may not want to, as it introduces potential security risks. You don't need to use embedding to add your VoiceThreads though.  VoiceThread has developed a Filter that can be added to your system, to allow VTs to be placed wherever anyone is editing text - labels, web pages, discussion forum posts, assignment descriptions, quiz questions, etc, without needing to risk the use of embed codes.  It's like turning on the Multimedia Plugins filter that allows you to embed YouTube clips without using Embed code. You can find the filter at the VoiceThread site: http://voicethread.com/about/blog/2009/20090220/ or here at moodle.org: http://moodle.org/mod/data/view.php?d=13&rid=2176&filter=1 keith landa

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: latest news posts
ResponsesInList.Text: No, it is a news forum and the default for front page news forums is to deny editing rights to all but Admins, as far as I have found it to be. Assuming that all your non-Admin users are logged in as Authenticated Users, you can go to Administration ► Users ► Permissions ► Define roles And search for items in the Forum section of permissions, and there you will find  Add News, Edit Any Post, Reply to News, Reply to Posts, Start New Discussions. Make sure all these permissions are set to Prohibit for all the Roles you assign in the Front Page, except Adminsitrator, of course. This blocks any opportunity to edit any news item as an Authenticated User. Be careful here, make sure you check that Students, Teachers, Course Creators and Adminsitrators have sufficient rights to use general forums in their courses.

ResponsesInList.Title: Signatur in Moodle?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Signatur in Moodle?
ResponsesInList.Text: No. Remember that Moodle is designed for use as part of courses. Most courses involve only a small number of people, who get to know each other, so some standard boiler-plate at the end of everybody's post is just a waste of space and distracts from a focussed discussion of whatever topic the class is about. Also, in Moodle, you have a personal profile page that you can customise with whatever information you wish to share about yourself. Wherever you participate (not just in forum threads), that is, wherever your name appears, it will be a link to your profile. So, if you want to know more about me, the person who replied to you, just click on my name.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Signatur in Moodle?
ResponsesInList.Text: Why would you want to? As I see it, signatures are used in environments where the identity of the author of a post is not always easily identified. In Moodle this is not an issue, but in a mediaWiki-based repository, for example, you have an option of whether you add your signature or not.

ResponsesInList.Title: Evaluation tool for Moodle piloting
ResponsesInList.Text: We have been using Blackboard LMS for a few years now. Currently we are also piloting MOODLE with some selected group of students to understand the challenges and benefits of MOODLE vis-a-vis Blackboard. Is there any evaluation tool available or developed by anyone that we can use rather than re-inventing the wheel Thanks in advance Tom

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Evaluation tool for Moodle piloting
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tom, This is really in the wrong forum, it should be in the Comparisons and Advocacy forum, but no matter... AFAIK there is no specific tool developed and used for the purpose you describe, but there has been a recent study that offers a very comprehensive comparison of Blackboard and Moodle. (This is a large PDF file btw .) It starts out with reservations about swapping from Blackboard, well that is how I see it the tone is not that balanced initially as it contains that typically American suspicion of the concepts inherent within Open Source. As it progresses, the comparison between the two becomes considerably more analytical and balanced then more favourable to Moodle. The recommendations are somewhat wishywashy, preferring to sit on the fence rather than outright acceptance that Moodle is a better option. I thought it obvious that the solution to the problem they pose, that of cost of migration, would be attenuated over time. What they propose is to run both Moodle and Blackboard, but they refrained from taking the next step, that is lay out a planned shift that could take place over two to three years. In three years, Blackboard will be worn out, and as Moodle is in continual improvement and upgrade, will still be fresh, the last courses could be shifted at minimum cost and training costs could be both incurred and amortized over a more reasonable time period two to three years incurring costs, and another year to amortize that cost. The bottom line is that we are finding it increasingly difficult to support the Western price model, so we need to be more analytical and careful in selecting the tools we use. The real problem is that most of those tools are so inflexible that we are often trapped in particular regimes, (just look at MS Office and how that has both had a hugely positive and negative impact on our expectations and practices in such a simple process as word processing.) The additional problem is that we do not see that inflexibility initially and we can be facing huge costs to make changes to our practices as the Authors of that report have noted.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moving a Forum (or discussion) from One Course to Another
ResponsesInList.Text: I had the same issue, and if you have access to your MySQL database , you can use this. First, create a forum in the new course and make a note of its forum id. Then, using php my sql admin and using the SQL box (second tab), paste the following and run the SQL query at your own risk. UPDATE mdl_forum_discussions SET course =1, forum =68 WHERE course =2 AND forum =34 then paste this and run the SQL query, again at your own risk. UPDATE mdl_forum_subscriptions SET forum =68 WHERE forum =34 In this scenario, course =1, forum =68 is the NEW course/forum and course=2 AND forum =34 is the OLD forum. In the first SQL query, the forum discussions are moved from the old forum to the new forum. In the second SQL query, all subscribers to the old forum are automatically subscribed to the new forum.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: No forum post notices (my solution)
ResponsesInList.Text: After much frustration and experimenting this is what I've discovered. Our process We are using courses setup with multiple forums for private one on one coaching. That means one student and one coach per course Inside the course are multiple forums - these are used for discussions between coach and the single client. Forums are arranged by topic. All forums are set to make everyone subscribed all the time. The problem The client could make a post and receive notice of his/her own post but the coach never received a notice, nor did the admin The coach could make a post and receive an email notice but no one else received one. The permissions were as follows System level - admin assigned Course level - coach assigned as "course creator", client assigned as student The solution All those who needed to receive copies of forum posts had to listed as actual students at the course level Even though the coach should have received notices they weren't and same with the admin. It appears the functions are not inherited (as far as the forum notices are concerned) So far this is working I'll post if it doesn't work or something changes Hopefully this will help someone else with the same issue.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: The future of forums in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Some of my thoughts on this: Moodle forum is actually pretty good. Most developers happily use the forums here every day, so if any bugs arise, they tend to be jumped on quickly. By comparison, block and wiki were in a really bad state in 1.9 and before. Dealing with them was much more urgent. Of course, moodle.org is not a typical example of how the forum is supposed to be used. The important use cases relate to use in teaching, and so some of the missing features are important, and better moderation was one of the things we really needed at the OU that lead us to make ForumNG. The Moodle 2.0 release has been mainly focussed on behind the scenes infrastructure improvements. The plan now is to focus on the different activity modules in Moodle 2.1, and in many cases this is long overdue. And more overdue that we had hoped, because it is taking longer to get Moodle 2.0 finished that we expected. Like many things, Moodle development strategy has to be a mixture of planning and opportunism. Although the big picture is infrastructure improvements in 2.0, module improvements in 2.1, we got quiz improvements because the OU and others volunteered to fund or do them. We got a rewrite of the workshop module because David Mudrak came along with a good plan to do it. The wiki happened not just because the situation was critical, but also because there were developers in Spain and at the OU volunteering to do the work. As said above, further improvements to the forum are overdue, so now is a good time to start thinking about what the most important missing requirements are. Actually, in a few months time, once Moodle 2.0 is out of the way might be even better, but it does not really matter. (By the way, useful tip, if you just type the id of a Moodle bug like MDL-3030 , into a forum post, or on Moodle docs , it automatically gets converted into a link for you.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Blocking New Posts to Forums
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi David The appropriate way to stop users from participating is by overriding the permissions for that role on the specific forum. To stop student from posting discussions & replies to a forum follow these steps: Edit/update the specific forum Click the 'Override Permissions' tab Click 'Student' (or other role you would like to alter) Select the 'Prevent' radio button beside the following two capabilities Reply to posts [ mod/forum:replypost] Start new discussions [mod/forum:startdiscussion] Save Changes Note that this only changes the Student role's permissions for this particular forum, you can however following steps 2 - 5 from the Assign Roles page to override the permissions for all forums within the course. I have shown our teaching staff how to do this so they can change the permissions to specific forums when required, rather than asking the administrator to do it every time. Also note that It takes site permissions to be able to override roles. If you are not the Admin and cannot follow these steps your Administrator will need to provide your role with the ' Override Safe Permissions ' capability. Re your PS about CTRL-Right arrow: This also drives some of our users crazy. I find this only happens on some browsers like IE , it doesn't do it for me in Firefox . Sorry for the long post, I hope it helps Cheers Teresa

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Able to categorize posts?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Shane Chris has provided a good alternative, using the database activity with a present ready to be imported - thanks Chris! Do remember the database activity doesn't send email subscriptions. A Forum with visible groups will allow you to use a dropdown to filter the posts. You need to create four groups (eg 9th, 10th, 11th, 12th) then configure the forum to visible groups - it sounds like you've done these two steps. You then ask your teachers to select the relevant group in the 'Visible groups' dropdown (displayed at the top left of the forum screen) before clicking 'Add discussion' button. The selection of this dropdown determines which group the forum thread is associated with and is key to ensuring the dropdown will filter the posts. Note: you cannot alter existing threads to associate them with a group - unless you alter the actual Moodle database (that's the database that runs Moodle not the activity). Let us know how you get on Cheers Teresa

ResponsesInList.Title: FYI: Embedding Flash Video in Forum Post
ResponsesInList.Text: The question has been asked of me recently how one can embed YouTube or other flash-format videos in a forum post. Embeds show up everywhere else (even in the forum description) without any special adjustments, but not in spaces where users can make submissions. NOTE: This is by design, so if you're going to make the changes I suggest below, make your teachers aware that .swf files will now appear, including any animations or videos that kids want to post. If you're sold and would like to make the change, here are the two admin-level settings you'll need to adjust: 1) Admin Block > Plugins > Multimedia Plugins > √ Enable .swf filter, and 2) Admin Block > Security > Site Policies > √ Allow embed and Object tags. One last note: this is a good thing to enable if you'd like participants to be able to post videos, podcasts and other flash content in submission spaces. If, however, you'd just like to post a video for them to discuss in a forum, I'd recommend placing the video embed code in the description. This will show up at the top of the discussion board, then, without opening the flood gates for all .swf content. Enjoy!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Playing RTSP FIles on Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: rtsp is a protocol not a file... rtsp is the protocol for delivering Real Time Streaming files (hence the name rstp!) As such all you can do is either provide a link to the rtsp link or; use a container movie that points at the rtsp file. I believe the container movie is Apple's recommended way of doing it; and I have always found it works well. I also provide the rtsp link under the container movie too with instructions for VLC users to copy the link into their VLC video player to view the video. Jon

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum for teachers ONLY - access settings?
ResponsesInList.Text: A solution we have been finding some success with.. we created a new Role called Staff, based on Authenticated User but can see hidden files. Obviously, all staff are members and Role is assigned at the front page. While I was unhappy with this initially, it actually works well. Everywhere we need to put hidden folders there is no issue with seeing them by any staff members. We have an area where only Admins access that can be seen by staff, but there is no reason for staff to go there, nothing exists there except Admin materials. Staff areas are all well marked. We have found though that more and more materials are going into Staff areas and there is less demand for hidden areas anywhere else. Once Staff were confident that Students could not access their preserves, then it made it much more relaxed and easier for staff to do things. And Lev: "then to access a password-protected "forum course" the second login is required... A bit cumbersome." You misunderstand what Mary means when she says "password protected". A password is placed on the course or forum, to access the course you need to enter the password when asked. You are only ever asked once, and that is when you enroll to use the course or forum, after that, you are already enrolled so it does not ask again. However, anyone without the password cannot enter the course. We had some difficulty with students sharing passwords, so we changed passwords but manually enrolled students. They could get into courses, but their friends could not. No idea why students would want to do that, but they did, and when asked most of them shrugged and said "My friend was in there and it looked interesting" and "better than what we do in this class." or "Mr So-so is so boring, this is much better, more fun.." and so on.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Another question about group forum settings
ResponsesInList.Text: Your forum setting is currently set to 'separate groups' which means that each group has and can see and work in only its own forum instance. If you set the forum to 'visible groups' each group will have and work in its own instance but will also be able to see (read only) instances of the other groups. Since you already set the course to visible groups you can simply force ('Yes') that course setting and your forums (and all other activities for that matter) will be by default 'visible groups' regardless of their particular groups setting. hth

ResponsesInList.Title: Media Forum
ResponsesInList.Text: I am the moodle admin at a design school and the need arose for a forum that could integrate in some manner with the VoiceThread tool. I decided to make an even more flexible forum that could display any piece of content and integrate it with a forum for discussion about that piece of content. I've created a "patch" to the standard 1.9 forum that adds the ability to show a full-screen piece of content at the top of each thread. How it works: I've added 2 fields to the forum tables: media to table forum medialink to table forum_posts When you create or edit a forum, there is a new field available called Media. When set to yes, it will allow the use of the "medialink" field on new thread posts. The medialink field is ONLY available on top level thread posts. Instead of the medialink field an attachment can also be uploaded. The medialink field contains the URL of the piece of content being discussed in the forum. When the forum is viewed, an full-screen iframe (auto-sized with javascript ) displays the URL provided in the medialink field to the user. Scrolling down below the iframe will show the normal threaded discussion. If no link is provided in the medialink field on a new post and no attachment is uploaded, the iframe will not be displayed and the forum will look like a regular old forum. If anyone is interested in this enhancement you are free to download it from by clicking here .

ResponsesInList.Title: Using forum ratings to setup a simple booking system in Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: I wrote this for another purpose but others might be interested in a way to use Moodle forum ratings to setup a booking system allowing students to book into Wimba online classroom sessions. ----- /param>/param>/param> Above is a link to a short screen cast showing how to setup a booking system in a Moodle forum allowing student to book into chat sessions or vote on any issue. To do this we are going to use the ratings option at the bottom of a forum message. First we need to setup a scale Use Administration block > Grades > Choose and action ... > Grades > Add a new scale and add the following as options in the scale I will attend, I hope to attend, I would like to attend if there was another time, I won't attend Next add the scale to the forum Click the name of the forum > update forum > set Aggregate type to Count of ratings Click the name of the forum > update forum > set Grade the scale you created ealier Next modify the permissions so students can rate messages and see ratings Click the forum > update forum > local overrides > then for the student role enable ratings and view ratings and view any rating Then post a message to the forum advertising a session and clearly telling people how to indicate they will attend by entering their ratings then send all ratings. Below is a typical message I post advertsing a session and telling people that they must book in. Peter Evans http://eMarkingAssistant.com -------8< ----- cut here Wimba Orientation session: April 14 at 8pm There are three Wimba training sessions and most people will attend only the first session: If you are going to attend this session you must register using the RATE ... drop down menu below this message and then click SEND MY LATEST RATINGS (see below for a screen image). Can you then please check that you have successfully registered (and who else is attending) by clicking the link next to Count of ratings (see below). We suggest you encourage others in your course to attend the same orientation session as this means that you have a ready made study-group which can meet at any time using a Wimba drop in room. If you have any questions about starting to use Wimba or booking into teh session, please post them to the " Setup Wizard and starting to use Wimba questions and issues" forum. The sessions are limited to the first 20 people who book in using the RATE menu so it is CRITICAL that you check to see that your name is in the list (click the link next to COUNT OF RATINGS at the bottom of this message and you can can see if you have booked in). PLEASE DO NOT REPLAY TO THIS MESSAGE IF YOU ARE GOING TO ATTEND AND POST QUESTIONS TO THE "Setup Wizard and starting to use Wimba questions and issues" Forum. You should enter the Wimba Orientation room 15 minutes or so before the session starts and use the information on the screen to confirm that your audio is working. After you have done this you can put a tick next to your name and the facilitator will probably move you (politely) to a breakout room so you can talk to others who are already setup. Put a cross next to your name if there is a problem and someone will help you (I promise). We will have other sessions depending on the availability of the student volunteer DIGITAL LEARNING MENTORS. If you subscribe to this forum you will automatically receive a note of future sessions. Peter Evans for the Digital Learning Mentors

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Youtube in Forums
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Carmen if you want to use youtube in you Moodle site, the best way is to embeding them now, to let embed videos: 1) your Moodle site must allow embed Site Administration block ----> Security ---> Site policies ----> Allow EMBED and OBJECT tags

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Youtube in Forums
ResponsesInList.Text: Here is a screencast tutorial on how to use YouTube embed codes to embed YouTube videos in your Moodle courses: http://vimeo.com/channels/97810#10708002 You should be able to embed YouTube videos in resources (labels, web pages, topic/weekly summaries) even if your Moodle administrator has not turned on Allow EMBED and OBJECT tags (at least in the 1.9.x versions of Moodle that we have used). Since only instructors can create those resource items, they are safer than postings to forums, which students can also do. The Allow EMBED and OBJECT Tags settings extends use of embed code to activities and therefore student use, so some Moodle admins may not want to allow that setting. The default is to have that functionality turned off. If your Moodle admin doesn't want to allow EMBED tags, but is willing to turn on the YouTube multimedia filter (Moodle version 1.9.6 and later), that's a safer and actually easier alternative for displaying YouTube videos in your course activities. Here's a screencast on how to work with the YouTube multimedia filter: http://vimeo.com/channels/97810#10779054

We are a small university. I am more concerned about incoming security issues that may affect the whole site.  We have only been using Moodle for 8 months. thanks everyone

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Youtube in Forums
ResponsesInList.Text: We use the multi-movie filter . This way you do not need to allow embed privliges or give all users the teacher role. We posted a video tutorial on using it, and it works great. It is no more difficult for users than toggling source and pasting embed code. Rob

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Youtube in Forums
ResponsesInList.Text: I would second Rob's suggestion to use the multimedia filter to allow faculty and students to incorporate YouTube videos into their forum postings and other activity, rather than turning on the setting to allow embed codes to be used widely. We haven't seen any real security issues from the default setting where embed codes can only be used by faculty and only in resources. We have seen some instances where faculty have pasted in codes for various web widgets that have broken their course pages or led to situations where they couldn't get back to edit the html code to remove the widgets. When that has happened in label or web page resources, it's easy enough to delete the problem resource and return the course to its normal appearance. We've had a couple of instances where widget code was pasted into a weeky/topic summary which were more difficult to deal with since you can't just delete the summary for one of the course sections .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: limit access to content
ResponsesInList.Text: Have you considered/explored the use of Groupings ? This is a site setting that needs to be turned on via Administration > Miscellaneous > Experimental (even though it's not really 'experimental', it's been around for ages! Groupings allow you to restrict resources and activities to a set of users within a group that is associated to a grouping . We use this all the time where we have different users who do not need to see certain resources or activities. It also works very well to assign a set of groups to a forum if users are members of multiple groups - the grouping tell the forum which set of groups to use instead of all of them. Put the users who should have the extra access into a group. Create a grouping and add that group to it then change the resource(s) & activities groupings setting to that grouping - remembering to tick the box to say only those people can see this. That item will then be invisible to anyone NOT in the group that belongs to that grouping! I hope this makes sense & helps Cheers Teresa

ResponsesInList.Title: Sorting Posts
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a friend at PBS who has 2 questions. They are moving from D2L to Moodle (maybe) and she asks: Is there a setting in Moodle so that you can see which discussion (forum) posts you have read? Can you sort them by user names in order to grade them

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sorting Posts
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle profiles include a setting to track unread posts or not. I think it would be a no-brainer to have read tracking turned on, but individuals can choose whether or not to have Moodle keep track of posts they haven't read yet. The forums have a number of ways to sort posts (nested display, threads, chronological with oldest first, chronological with newest first), but not by author (at this time). You can turn on post ratings, however, which makes it easy to grade each individual post. You can then tell Moodle how to aggregate all the individual posts from each student (average them, take the highest grade, add them together, etc), and Moodle will then enter the aggregated grade for each student into the Moodle gradebook.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum E-mails Not Sending
ResponsesInList.Text: If you haven't figured it out yet, here's how: You have to configure your SMTP server to relay messages, and Exchange 2007 usually has this type of issue, here how to resolve: Here is step-by-step how to create anonymous recipient relay connector 1. Create a new Receive Connector with the Custom Usage Group 2. For Remote Network Settings default values are 0.0.0.0 -255.255.255.255, where you can add IP address range (for example if you have clients who are talking with exchange on port 25), or/and specific IP Address of the remote server that requires relaying permissions. 3. Once the new Custom Receive Connector is created, go into the properties of this connector 4. Go to the Permission Groups Tab > check Anonymous Users 1. To activate Anonymous users to use this connector for relaying, you must issue the following command using PowerShell : Get-ReceiveConnector "Receive connector name" | Add-ADPermission -User "NT AUTHORITY\ANONYMOUS LOGON" -ExtendedRights "ms-Exch-SMTP-Accept-Any-Recipient"

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Possible to have one forum for multiple courses?
ResponsesInList.Text: You can set up a meta-course, which all of the 'modules' are child courses of. Anyone enrolled in the child courses are automatically enrolled in the meta-course. You can put the forum into the meta-course, and it would be accessible by everyone in all of the child courses. If you're not using the meta-course for other overall activities or resources, you'd probably want to force subscriptions to the forum, so that everyone in all of the child courses get an email when new material is posted to the forum in the meta-course. keith

ResponsesInList.Title: 'Available for group members only'?
ResponsesInList.Text: There is a tick box that says:' Available for group members only' that i do not understand. I have set up a forum for separate groups, for one particular grouping . I assumed this means group members would see their own group discussion and no one else. So how does the above tick box modify who sees what? Thanks

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 'Available for group members only'?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Andrea, Please see the paragraph on assigning an activity to a grouping in Groupings for details of how to use 'Available for group members only'.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 'Available for group members only'?
ResponsesInList.Text: The separate groups mode includes a virtual 'all participants' group. The 'Available for group members only' refers to actual groups only. So, if you tick that option the activity won't be accessible to anyone who is not assigned to an actual group. In the scenario you describe above, that is, separate groups and a certain grouping, if the 'Available for group members only' is not ticked then anyone can enter the forum whether or not he/she is assigned to any group whether or not that group belongs to the grouping. Those who are not belong to any group, or who are not belong to a group in the grouping, will not be able to post anything or see anything except for what is posted by you in the virtual 'all participants' group. If the 'Available for group members only' is ticked , only those who are assigned to an actual group which belong to the grouping will see the forum, be able to access it, see only their own group and post there.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Embed video
ResponsesInList.Text: Embedded code is essentially untrusted content, and could include malicious content. My experience is that Moodle (1.9.7) allows embedded object code in resources (web pages, labels, topic summaries) because instructors are the only ones who can edit those and presumably instructors aren't going to deliberately put malicious code into their courses. Forums and other activities allow students to add content, and so embedded object code is stripped out by default. There are two options in the site administration block (Administration -> Security -> Site policies) that may apply: "Allow EMBED and OBJECT tags" and "Enable Trusted Content". The default on both of these options is No. If you don't have site administration permissions on your Moodle system, you can check with your system administrator to see if it's possible to set these options to Yes. Be warned though that it would open up security risks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: moodle doesnt support word??
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Syach, To expand a little on what Mary has already said. MS Word is designed to give instructions to a printer to print words on paper. A html text field (like the one we use to write messages in on Moodle) is designed to create pages of code that can be interpreted by navigators (Internet Explorer, Firefox ...) so that we can read text and see images, etc. on our computers when we surf the web. The two technologies are quite different and only partially compatible. You can usually copy simple text from Word to a text field, but complex formatting, tables, images, etc. don't transfer well. The solutions are : type your text directly in the text field on Moodle, and format it there, upload your Word file as a document to Moodle, copy your Word text into a a text editor (Notepad on Windows), which will remove the Word code and formatting, and then copy it from there into the text field on Moodle. It's not just Moodle that works like this, all text fields that create web pages work in the same way.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: moodle doesnt support word??
ResponsesInList.Text: There are lost of ways to avoid your problem beyond those mentioned, Syach, but the one that is most obvious is to quit using MS Word! While "word processors" certainly may have gotten their start as agents for printers, that is arguably historical as I think it fair to say that most of todays word processors store information in xml , but that discussion may be far afield and way too esoteric vis-a-vis your present needs. The point is that I have always found OpenOffice to be very cooperative with Moodle and have had no issues copying and pasting from OpenOffice to Moodle. That is to say that problem may be not generically with word processors, but with MS Word.... But the problem that Mary was trying to grapple with was just how you were trying to use MS Word with Moodle. For example, are you just looking for somewhere to draft before transferring to Moodle or do you have material composed in moodle that you wish to add to moodle. If the latter, there are quite a few ways to address that. If the former, try using a simple ASCII text editor. Of course, most word processors today allow you to save docs as ascii text. One of the exercises I often put my students through is creating a doc on google docs and then publishing it and referencing or embedding in Moodle. This would also allow you to draft in any supported word processor, upload to google docs and still incorporate in Moodle. And of course Google docs does allow you to export to pdf (of course any "everything but the kitchen sink"comprehensive word processor should arguably include that feature as openoffice does, though I think you will that your copy of Word doesn't....) Answers to complex questions often turn on what you might think are ancillary matters; you just want to know how to slice an onion, but that will be dependent on what kind of onion, how old the onion is, and what you want to do with the onion..... And the recipe may call for leaks ;=}

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: moodle doesnt support word??
ResponsesInList.Text: export to pdf (of course any "everything but the kitchen sink"comprehensive word processor should arguably include that feature as openoffice does, though I think you will find that your copy of Word doesn't....) And, no matter the context , virtually every instance save where some external authority for some ungodly reason mandates that Microsoft software be employed, a non-Microsoft solution typically renders the user issues moot, whether the user is student, teacher, administrator, silliputian or troll. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: 1 and out forum use
ResponsesInList.Text: For forums that do not have a required or graded posting metric, what encourages use is lots of people and topics that are interesting, and a "seed" writer to keep things going. The structure and grouping in general will not improve participation. Coming back to the forum isn't the only way that a student will see the posts. They may also be getting the emails and seeing all the posts. So it is very difficult to measure if they read the forum. Although you could detect if they are subscribed, you can't tell if they open their email. If you consider forum participation important, you have to tie it to their grade. There are a few options to do so. See Grading forums in the docs.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Editing forum capabilites
ResponsesInList.Text: Site administration > Users > Permissions > Define Roles I would always recommend leaving the standard roles alone and either creating a new "empty" role or (more likely) copying the closest existing one and modifying that. Then it's just a matter of going to "Assign roles" in your course's administration block and adding your victims to the new role (and possibly removing them from the old one). There are other, more exciting, ways to do the same thing but the above is probably easiest to understand. You can also override the capabilities for individual forum instances. When you update the forum, look for the "Override permissions" tab. This is only available to admins by default.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to get greater participation in our forum
ResponsesInList.Text: If they need help, and if the forums can help and if there is no easier way to get that help they will post. If they don't post, it is very likely that at least one of these conditions is not met.

ResponsesInList.Text: Make it an assessed activity!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to get greater participation in our forum
