ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Daily digests aren't going out daily
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Nicole, I don't know how much mileage this will get you, but this is what we were experiencing on our servers. It seems that the forum digest cron takes a bit of time to complete. If you
can check your phpinfo.php from the Admin page, you can look for the: max_execution_time = parameter. If it is at the default 30 seconds, you might be getting a timeout on the sending of the digests. One way to make sure is to get the output of every cron execution on
the installation. This will depend on how you can set the crontab and
will require a bit of research on how to get your hosting service to
send you the output of each cron execution. If you have the cron set for every 15 minutes, you will get about 96 messages per day!. However, it will be worth having a day or two of logs to check. A successful script will have this message: 
```text
<snip>


Processing email digest for user 217... success.


Email digests successfully sent to 68 users.


done.




<snip>
```
 I use a filtering on the email client (Thunderbird) to let me know when a script has sent a digest and if it was not successful. If you see that it is timing out before all messages are sent, then you can do or one or both of two things: 1. Try to set the: max_execution_time = to a higher number. This, you might get your hosting provider to do it in php.ini or try to do this in the .htaccess file. 2. Set the digest sending time to an obscure time (2:00am?) when you anticipate that the server is not as busy. As you are sharing your installation with other users on the same
server, it would be more of a hit or miss on getting the timing right. Monitoring the cron output  will give you a better idea. HTH , Bill

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: "Sorry, but you can't post in this discussion" error
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Amanda, Maybe you have set the forums to "groups-visible" mode, which means that learners within one group can see the posts of other groups but can not post messages there. To post to their own forum, the students have to select their own group from the drop-down list above the forum. If you want all your learners to participate in the forums regardless of the group they are in, make sure you set them to "no groups" mode on the forum settings screen (you can only set different group settings on different course activities if the "force groups" option in the course settings screen has been set to "no"). If you need more help don't hesitate to post here again, Tim.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: "Sorry, but you can't post in this discussion" error
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks!  That helped.  I had the course settings on "Separate Groups" and Force on "Yes".  I switched Force to "No" and it fixed the problem. I don't really understand the "force" part, but oh well... THANK YOU!! ~Amanda

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: "Sorry, but you can't post in this discussion" error
ResponsesInList.Text: Amanda, The "Force" option simply means that the groups setting for a particular course is applied to all activities in a course. If "Force" is set to no, this means that you can have different groups settings for different activities within a particular course (some can have no groups, some separate groups, some visible groups). I'm glad you solved  your problem. Tim.

ResponsesInList.Title: Two suggestions for improving forum browsing
ResponsesInList.Text: For class discussions I use the nested view. But when messages start to pile up it becomes harder and harder to get a sense of the discussion, for two main reasons: 1) since the view is exploded one has to do a lot of scrolling back and forth when exploring the discussion; 2) most people don't bother to put meaningful subjects and thus one frequently has to re-view more than a message's subject to recall what is it about. Two suggestions: 1) Allow expand/Collapse of messages' bodies both for individual messages and for all message at once. The former could be done by clicking the message subject and the latter by clicking two added buttons 'Expand All' and 'Collapse All'. The default nested view should open in collapsed mode and show only the messages' subjects. To the best of my knowledge it could be easily done with simple standard javascript and html and should not raise any outstanding multi-browsers compatibility issues. (I've tried that locally) 2) Remove the default 'Re: xxxxxx' subject and use instead the opening of the message body. The subject text field in the message edit window should be empty by default and not forced. If the message is posted with no subject, use the first, say, 60 characters and add '...' to indicate that there is more. What do we get? When I open the forum I can refresh my memory of previous discussion by reviewing the messages' titles. Note that now the titles view gives a better sense of the ongoing dialog since the titles are the openings of the messages rather than a repetitive 'Re: xxxxxx'. Since the forum is collapsed (or at least can be collapsed) many message titles fit into the window frame so I need to do less scrolling. If I want to read a certain message I simply open its body so I can see the message but also the other messages' titles. Since I'm in the same view I can scroll to nearby messages and open them too if I want to compare their content. The above approach is perhaps not so important in professional 'I have a problem' kind of forums but is crucial for online discussions in Arts faculty courses. A comment about the 'Re: xxxxxxx' feature. This is probably a remnant of email based discussion groups. But it should be obsolete by now in LMS environment. If I use the nested view, I can see for each message to which message it is a reply. If I use the flat view then all messages are replies to the topic. So I don't need the subject to repeat that.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Two suggestions for improving forum browsing
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, Itamar. Your suggestions are very significant in order to well manage web forums. You may be interested in knowing that Forum Plus , a third-party extension of the standard Forum module, already includes these features. Maybe that at least these two enhancements could be eventually included in the standard Forum module, in the future?

ResponsesInList.Title: Yes, I know about forum plus. It is an important project. But ...
ResponsesInList.Text: as you probably know, Antonio, large institutions are not too thrilled about applying even the most minor of customizations let alone major extensions, so they could keep maintenance cost low. And since I'm just a lowly user I won't have these features unless I get a research grant and have my own machine to experiment on or get the features added to the standard module. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: User email addresses not always displayed in forum emails
ResponsesInList.Text: It's not a bug, it's a feature The "email display" setting in the User's Profile controls the visibility of the address to others, allowing you to show or hide your email address. There are three options: you can set it so that all users (including guests) could see your email address, or so that only other participants in the course can see the email address, or so that no one could see your email address at all. If a user has set the "email display" setting in their profile to be hidden, then the noreply address will be used as the sender's email address. If not, then their own email address will be used. This is an individual setting - it's the user's choice.

The grading rubric rewards new ideas, starting discussion, answering questions, etc. Shorter responses like "me too" provide support to the person writing the post they were responding to but a similar thing could be accomplished by allowing student ratings. Then they could see that someone liked their idea without adding more to the forum. In other words, I am OK with a few "me too" posts especially if the student has already positively contributed to the conversation. I usually am not able to comment on each forum post; however, I do grade it and want to encourage quality posts over quantity.  I think with a little tweaking of the code, we could provide each teacher the control to grade the posts any number of ways and thus even within a single course use forums in a variety of ways.

ResponsesInList.Title: Forum as a Photo Gallery
ResponsesInList.Text: I was trying to come up with a good, integrated photo gallery solution for Moodle, when it came to me (actually it came to me in my sleep - I do a lot of designing while sleeping - I need help), we already have a solution. The forum module! It has everything we need: the ability to define who can post and view, a way to upload the image, the ability to title (subject) and describe (post) the image, the ability for others to comment on the post, the ability for the post to be rated. The only thing that needs to be done is to turn around the interface so that the image gets priority rather than the post. This isn't too difficult - just use a new forum type ('gallery'), and act on that. As an experiment, I copied the forum module to a new module called 'gallery', left the database the same, used the existing forum library as necessary and replaced the functions I needed, and came up with a working prototype (see attached for an example view). What I did was make each discussion an image post. I reworked the display to show each discussion as a thumbnail with title and other info (attached). Clicking on the post would display the full-sized image with description and any other replies (if allowed) plus ratings (if set). What do you think? If this works, it could also be used for a document library / repository. Using the same techniques, change the display to suit file uploads.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum as a Photo Gallery
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Mike, I will comment from a user's perspective. In fact, from a particular usage scenario. I teach in Medicine School. What morphologists seem to need here is a way to present collections of images to the students. For instance, microscope slide collections from  epithelial tissue, muscle tissue etc. These may be considered almost "Resources", not a great space for user interaction inside. The requirements would be: Uploadable in bulk (the whole collection as a zip file or so) Hierarchical categories Metadata for each image (like author, name, procedence etc): only written by teacher/curator Categories and metadata searchable Space for users comment and annotations (personal or shareable). Here there is space for a forum-like mini-thread of comments Rating for comments/annotations Linking the gallery to quizzes/ lesson for testing The whole thing is much, much more similar to a Glossary than to a forum. Actually, I have been doing it with glossaries. Glossaries do have other characteristic you mentioned in the OP : rating system, user permission control system etc. I would see it as a better start point. For casual use, "just look my holiday's photos", plain forums or the PhotoPhrame just are "good enough". just an opinion, - Enrique -

ResponsesInList.Title: Problems after cpanel restore.
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi, I have a client who has moodle installed on her account (i run a small hosting company). The hard drive recently died, so it was necessary to restore her account from a cpanel backup. However, when restoring the account, i get a lot of sql errors about creating tables  please see url here: http://susansivertson.com/ This is obviously because the table exists because i have restored the mysql db as well, however, only around 40 tables exist, as opposed to 133 that moodle normally has (is that right?).  Can you tell me if some configurations of moodle run with only 40 tables as i find it hard to believe that cpanel missed some in the backup? There is also a moodle backup, but when its restored, it does not restore any of the course data etc.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problems after cpanel restore.
ResponsesInList.Text: Elliot, The standard Moodle 1.5 install does have 133 tables...there could be more if there were additional blocks/mods installed. A 1.6 install has about 158 tables. It does sound like your cpanel restore isn't restoring all the tables. I seriously doubt if there are any Moodle installs running with only 40 tables. There are basically two places where Moodle stores data...the database and the moodle_data directory. Your moodle backup probably is restoring some data that is in the moodle_data directory (uploaded files, images, etc.) however, without a full restore of the database that doesn't do much good. If you have root access to your server , you may want to download the database backup from there and try restoring it. Steve

ResponsesInList.Text: We had the same problem on our system. I could not find any way of deleting the forums using the Moodle interface. So here's how to do it directly in MySQL . NOTE: Our forums were brand new and had no subscriptions, discussions, posts, etc. So I didn't have to worry about all the forum related tables. Of course if you there were related records they will have to cleaned up first. my sql > show tables like 'mdl_forum_%'; +-------------------------------+ | Tables_in_moodle (mdl_forum_%) | +-------------------------------+ | mdl_forum_discussions         | | mdl_forum_posts               | | mdl_forum_queue               | | mdl_forum_ratings             | | mdl_forum_read                | | mdl_forum_subscriptions       | | mdl_forum_track_prefs         | +-------------------------------+ 7 rows in set (0.01 sec) Get a list of all forums of type 'general' for a particular course. mysql> SELECT id, course, type, name FROM mdl_forum WHERE course = 218 AND type = 'general'; +-----+--------+---------+--------------------------------------+ | id  | course | type    | name                                 | +-----+--------+---------+--------------------------------------+ | 719 |    218 | general | Introductions                        | | 720 |    218 | general | Worksheet statements                 | | 768 |    218 | general | Discussion: Introductions            | | 769 |    218 | general | Discussion: Good management practice | +-----+--------+---------+--------------------------------------+ 4 rows in set (0.01 sec) Delete a couple of forums. mysql> DELETE FROM mdl_forum WHERE id = 719; Query OK, 1 row affected (0.00 sec) mysql> DELETE FROM mdl_forum WHERE id = 720; Query OK, 1 row affected (0.01 sec) List the general forums again. mysql> SELECT id, course, type, name FROM mdl_forum WHERE course = 218 AND type = 'general'; +-----+--------+---------+--------------------------------------+ | id  | course | type    | name                                 | +-----+--------+---------+--------------------------------------+ | 768 |    218 | general | Discussion: Introductions            | | 769 |    218 | general | Discussion: Good management practice | +-----+--------+---------+--------------------------------------+ 2 rows in set (0.01 sec)

I find myself wanting clear the unread messages (and the orange highlight), and it inspires me to read the messages. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: phantom/orphan forums that are only partially functional
ResponsesInList.Text: We're pretty new to moodle, but we experienced something similar and maybe I can give you some ideas for where to look. In our case, problems with phantom forums were caused by incorrect data in several key tables that govern moodle's activity modules and forums. It's a tricky data schema... honestly, I'm not thrilled with it, but I can see why they implemented it this way.  On my short list is finding (or writing) a utility to check our moodle database for referential integrity... there's just too much that can go wrong if small corruption in a db like this snowballs. Look through the tables mdl_course_modules, mdl_course_sections, and mdl_forum, and (with some time) see if you can figure out the data structure.   Chances are, there's a problem with the sequence column of the mdl_course_sections table (for the course that's showing problems.) -Garret Gengler University of Illinois Graduate School of Library and Info Science

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Nesting problem
ResponsesInList.Text: I had the same problem, but it got fixed They relate to the behaviour of the "me()" function in weblib.php For some reason (probably webserver related), $_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'] returns a FAULTY url with multiple "/" instead of one / you can try out if this is the case at your setup by including echo $_SERVER['REQUEST_URI']; somewhere. We got a fix by changing the following in the "me()" function in weblib.php $darn = $_SERVER['REQUEST_URI']; $test = str_replace ("//", "/", $darn); return $test; instead of return $_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'];

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle forums aren't bad, but they are limited
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle forums aren't bad, but they are limited and still far from competitive IMO . It does not include many of the community forum management features that other applications commonly provide. So, here's my current list of forum tool annoyances and wishes. Ability to auto-quote the post that you are responding to. This is very common in online community apps. Without it, automated email notifications often make little or no sense. Ability for a teacher to permanently stick/highlight a thread at the top of a forum threads list. This is commonly found in online forums apps. The Ability to split multiple posts within a thread into a new multi-post thread. This is another common community/forums application feature. Right now it only supports splitting individual posts into a new thread. A simple non-graded polling and surveying tool is commonly found integrated within online forum apps. A lightweight version for Moodle would be great for facilitating discussions. Again, another very common feature of forum apps. Display view counter and reply counter in threads index. Again, commonly found. A forum moderator role without the user being in a teacher role would be nice. How about a 'mark all as read' option for forums with unread tracking enabled? I'll post more feedback as I am able.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle forums aren't bad, but they are limited
ResponsesInList.Text: I think that you may find that more than one or all of the above have been posted to the bug tracker which is the place for feature requests. If you do an advanced search for the forum related feature requests and make a list of them here, then perhaps people may vote for them.

I know it isn't directly in the forum page, but that's such a small difference. (You can use the "choice block" to make it appear in a sidebar.) "mark all as read" - that already exists - click on the tick-mark icon at the top of the list. I think the option for "sticky threads" (as you mention) is one which would be easy to implement and would be very useful. It's stored as bug 1997 - sign up to the bugtracker and vote for it!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle forums aren't bad, but they are limited
ResponsesInList.Text: Many of these request come up quite a lot. I suspect eventually they will all get implemented, just because they get asked for again and again. I would however like to point out that many of the features you are talking about are common only to Bulletin Board or Forum software, that is I mean software that only does forums has has no other features. This means they need to put all their community building tools into forum posts. For example: Bulletin Board feature -> Moodle features sticky posts -> resources, wikis and the intro text for a forum poll posts -> choices, surveys, questionnaire, feedback module, quiz Then there is the fact that most of these forum tools are unthreaded. This design choice means that many things are done differently because multiple conversations are intertwined, not linked in the database but only because people quote a post further up the discussion: auto-quoting -> reply to a specific post split multiple posts -> split a thread at its root and all child posts follow Some other things in your list are good ideas, they're just clearly influenced by a different way of doing things e.g. if you want a busy forum with lots of moderators that aren't necessarily trusted teachers then why not make a social format course, which is seperate from all the actual teaching courses? 'Teachers' in that course have no extra rights in other parts of the Moodle unless explicitly given them. (I think Moodle 1.7 is implementing a feature like this anyway, but more generally so you can have different 'teachers' responsible for different course sections and activity etc.) As I said I think these ideas will eventually be implemented anyway. It's very difficult to defend intentionally not implementing a feature. I think that's part of why most software gets bloated and more difficult to use over time (e.g. Microsoft Office) unless you have someone with an iron will ensuring that it doesn't happen and things remain coherent and focused (e.g. see Apple software/hardware or the Mozilla- Firefox transition).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A big beef about subscribing.. Please respond
ResponsesInList.Text: Steve-When I was 11 years old, my teacher gave our class a surprise "test." The test consisted of a series of items, all of which told us to do very ridiculous things like flapping our arms like birds, making strange sounds etc. Well, a classroom full of thirty 11 year olds followed every item exactly, flapping our arms, making strange sounds, feeling like idiots but still following the instructions exactly so as to pass the test. Or so we thought. Because the last item on the test said "Do not do any of the above and stay seated quietly at your desk." None of us had bothered to read what it said at the top of the test: "Read the entire test first before starting." And we all failed that test but I learned a valuable lesson I have never forgotten and I consider it one of the best-taught lessons I have ever received from a teacher. Yes,  I too have accidentally subscribed myself to Moodle forums before when I didn't want to be subscribed, but I have absolutely no one to blame but myself because the choice was there, I just chose to not read it. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Posts + Cron=BAD BAD BAD
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Mary, I don't know if this will help, but we had some of the same problems with our servers. It
seems that the sending of the digest email portion of Moodle is timing
out. This means that it is not getting the permission to finish the job
before the server decides that it is taking too long to do it. The
server will terminate the job before it is finished, leaving the
digests unsent to some members. This will happen if there are a number of jobs running at the same time, each requiring server resources and slowing down the whole process. What we did on our servers is to
run the cron jobs sequentially for each Moodle installation. That
ensures that only one Moodle installation at a time is running a cron job and
finishes it before the next installation starts. This technique might delay a bit
the periodic sending of digest emails. However, it relieved the
bottleneck of having different installations of Moodle fighting for
server resources at the same time and all the digests are now being
sent out in full to everyone. If you are using a hosting
service, it might be a difficult to get the admin to use this technique
as it requires some script programming that they may not want to do. You also might try using a .htaccess setting to change the timeout settings for PHP as a temporary measure. However, it will untimately depend on whether the hosting service is willing to let you make these settings to your installation. Hope this helps, Bill

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Moodle Email Digest ? ?
ResponsesInList.Text: On the more general question of "do we or don't we send a email for EVERY post to EVERY forum?" I believe it is too easy to overlook potential uses for forums that may make email copies impractical for the student. What is wrong (as an alternative, mind you) with considering that some forum uses SHOULD be viewed JUST WITHIN THE FORUM and not extended to the email box of every student in the course every time someone posts to the forum? Some forums are topical discussions and it is easy to see why a complete mailing would be suggested. Other forums may be chatter that people (students, users, teachers?) should go look at within the Moodle site, because it is: - possibly irrelevant unless logged in at the time - restricted to use only when the student is within the classroom (which, incidently, is one way I use Moodle as a learning aid; within the classroom itself and not extended past our walls.) The "must email everyone" concept violates that method of use. - when the students are using a forum as a team tool as a group. They are working in the SAME ROOM at the SAME TIME. They do not need emailed copies of the postings. They have the forum itself in context and can print, save or email a copy of the whole set of postings to themselves if desired. As to this forum, itself, I am sorry but I have to disagree with the "you are either in or out" opinion. Getting dozens of emails about technical discussions about esoteric issues of modules that I don't use doesn't enrich me, just clutters up my email, making me less likely to attempt to find messages that actually are relevant to my needs or interests. Yes, I can filter, but with the volume experienced, the pile gets too big to sort through over the course of a week and I end up deleting most wholesale without reading any of them. Again, it might be different if I spent the day in front of my own computer at home, but I don't. I spend the day using a lab computer. I am forced to manage my email through a web mail interface that can be ponderous when forced to deal with high volumes of mail. Many of my students are stuck with a similar web-based interface to their mail. I usually wait until I am home to consider email, except rare exceptions. And the pile gets large fast. Honestly, at this point, I think the volume of mail coming through has caused my ISP to flag it as spam and I don't think messages are getting through from moodle.org. But maybe I was unsubscribed because of inactivity. I guess I'll know tomorrow! I am not sure why (at least in my situation) giving the teacher or admin a choice to limit emailed copies to the forums that need them violates any principles of the moodle project. To me it seems like A) people are using forums in diverse or atypical ways and B) just a matter of housekeeping. Personally, I see no "slippery slope" in this topic. The default could be "on." but I could really use an OFF checkbox or menu choice as well. I'll leave the arguement about whether a user-based control of this option is wise. In my case, it is not relevant.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Not receiving e-mails when posting to forum
ResponsesInList.Text: Have you remembered to set up a cron job? I hadn't! Do a search for "cron" in the forums--basically you have to automatically open the page your.site/admin/cron.php for the system to do all the little jobs it's supposed to on a regular basis, like posting out digests etc. You can either have a machine you own do it (if it's on all the time), or get someone else's host to do it for you... A word of warning: most of your users will probably be subscribed to the forums without having set their email option to recieve digests. If there's been a fair bit of activity in the meantime, they may receive many emails suddenly all at once when you switch on cron. A well worded apology and explanation in the News forum should placate them!

ResponsesInList.Text: Mike If you set the groups to visible groups instead of seperate groups then the troublesome one should be able to see everyone else's on the other forum, though not be able to post to it, yet still post onto the one you have set for him. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: A forum taking over News Forum functions?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi rafal, A simple solution would be to add a hidden forum as an archive for winter semester news and move all the discussions into it. An alternative solution, if you have phpMyAdmin , would be to create a new forum for summer semester news, hide the winter semester news forum, then edit the forum types in the database table mdl_forum. Further solutions are possible using backup and restore.

ResponsesInList.Title: Publishing a forum post on a web page outside of Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Does anyone know where the data from a given XYZ forum in a given ABC course is stored in a Moodle database ? I need to know this so that I can find that data and publish it on a webpage outside Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Publishing a forum post on a web page outside of Moodle
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Curtis, There are 8 tables related to forums in the Moodle database: forum, forum_discussions, forum_posts, forum_queue, forum_ratings, forum_read, forum_subscriptions and forum_track_prefs. If this can help, here's an example of a mysql query to retrieve data from a given forum.id 999 in a given course.shortname ABC. SELECT ## course details course.shortname, ## user details u.lastname, u.firstname, ## forum discussion details fo.id, fo.name, fd.name,

ResponsesInList.Title: Brainstorm Module - New Forum Format or complete new module?
ResponsesInList.Text: Preamble I've been thinking about what follows for a while, so thought I'd post it here to see what people's reaction is. Having used the NCSL 's Talk2Learn tools for a number of years (which originally used Oracle 's Think.com) I've been wondering about a Brainstorm module for Moodle. Now, I'm not sure if this would be a new forum format or a complete module. It's one of the most useful tools I ever used in Think.com and I for one would love to see in Moodle. This was originally a reply to a thread in the Open Social Forum, but I'll reproduce it here to see if there's any mileage in it... Well, if you need an "ideas storm"... then something for Moodle similar to Think.com's original Brainstorm tool would be great. This module was (to my mind) a fantastic tool and one that I could see being used massively... It's something like a forum, except... It starts off with a blank page with a 'grid' of 'blank' Post-it -like notes on it. You choose one, click on it, and enter your comment or idea. to start with, it looks like this: What extra features would we like to see in Moodle? Enter your ideas here, however silly... [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] ...so, the user clicks on an add idea link and get to enter their (brief) idea. when you've added it (simple, just text), you are returned to the brainstorm and your idea is there, but anonymous... What extra features would we like to see in Moodle? Enter your ideas here, however silly... [ add idea ] how about a brainstorm module? [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] something to make tea for busy teachers [ add idea ] a small avatar of Martin D on each site to keep things in order [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] [ add idea ] The thing is this - most recent ideas are coloured differently (divided, say, into five colours equally divided across the time from the first idea to the last) according to how recently they were posted - giving some idea of the evolution of the ideas... Key to ideas: newer older When the three rows are nearly full (for example when there's less than one row's worth of empty cells - in this case five), the grid gets another row of [ add idea ] cells added to the bottom, thus providing space for the brainstorm to grow. A few things: the teacher would be able set things so that contributions would be completely anonymous authors of contributions could be seen by the teacher everyone could see who said what or maybe they could be attributed once the time limit for the brainstorm had closed? I'm not sure if this would be a completely new module, or a different type of forum. I don't think ratings are involved, but that could be an option... It's not a mind map, more of "a collection of random thoughts" tool. I've seen it used v effectively on the NCSL's Talk2Learn community, I'd love to have it in Moodle... What do you think? A stupid idea, or something with mileage?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Brainstorm Module - New Forum Format or complete new module?
ResponsesInList.Text: ...and, should anyone read this, I'm aware that there's an activity module in CVS called 'brainstorm', but from my reading it takes a slightly different approach with a lot more teacher intervention (though I may be mis-reading it though). Also, later versions seem to have an output of a concept map (aka mindmap?) as an outcome. Maybe that's why I figured that what I've outlined above might be a forum type rather than a new module. Also, there's nothing on the thread in question for about nine months or so... anyone know of any progress?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Brainstorm Module - New Forum Format or complete new module?
ResponsesInList.Text: The glossary module can already do most of these things: You can have students add entries to the glossary. You can sort them according to creation date The glossary module also allows: moderation by a teacher before ideas get displayed commenting grading by students / teachers using the secondary / main glossary feature to gather useful ideas into a separate glossary. I guess it should be possible to write a gloosary format to support the grid layout and the colour scheme. Writing a glossary format is certainly easier than writing a complete module or a forum type. Another option would be to wait for the Data module in Moodle 1.6. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bug? update 1.5+ 2005-06-18 fails!!!
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Bertold/Martin/All, We have the same problem on postgres 7.4.8. The problem is not the database but a wrong query. I might have the solution for your problem, when looking closely you see the SQL generated is wrong : (i turned on adodb debug to see this) SELECT p.id, p.subject, p.modified, p.discussion, p.userid, d.name as myname, d.timemodified, d.usermodified, d.groupid, u.firstname, u.lastname, u.email, u.picture , um.firstname AS umfirstname, um.lastname AS umlastname FROM , moodle_forum_discussions d, moodle_forum_posts p, moodle_user u LEFT JOIN moodle_user um on (d.usermodified = um.id) WHERE d.forum = '1' AND p.discussion = d.id AND p.parent = 0 AND p.userid = u.id ORDER BY d.timemodified DESC The Bit .... moodle_user u LEFT JOIN moodle_user um on (d.usermodified = um.id) .... makes no sense at all. The join link field should allways be in one of the two tables joined: ( SELECT a.x, b.y, c.z FROM a, b LEFT JOIN c (b.some_id = c.some_id) The solution is : (Moodle people please watch this) Exchange the moodle_forum_discussions d and the moodle_user u in the from clause in the file mod/forum/lib.php The new working SQL command generated is SELECT p.id, p.subject, p.modified, p.discussion, p.userid, d.name as myname, d.timemodified, d.usermodified, d.groupid, u.firstname, u.lastname, u.email, u.picture , um.firstname AS umfirstname, um.lastname AS umlastname FROM moodle_user u, moodle_forum_posts p moodle_forum_discussions d LEFT JOIN moodle_user um on (d.usermodified = um.id) WHERE d.forum = '1' AND p.discussion = d.id AND p.parent = 0 AND p.userid = u.id ORDER BY d.timemodified DESC BTW: As a database expert i strongly dissagree with using fieldnames like "name" and "id" BTW2: In setup.php you turn off all error reporting prior to database connection routines. I think this is not good practice, problems like the above will not be noticed this way. Kind Regards, Pim Koeman, Database Expert Wittenborg University, The Netherlands

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bug? update 1.5+ 2005-06-18 fails!!!
ResponsesInList.Text: >> BTW: As a database expert i strongly dissagree with using fieldnames like "name" >> and "id" >I'm interesting in hearing your reasoning behind this statement. Hi Penny, Thanks for your action, i will explain my point; When designing a table i allways try to stick to a standard naming convention for example: - allways use a prefix or a schema (if supported) - a table's name is always the plural of the entity - the primary key fieldname always contains the name of the entity followed by _id - never use reserved words for any of the databases you want to use - try to avoid shorting names as much as possible (if you do document them !(like apples_no (for number of apples etc.)) - use '_' between all name parts (birth_date, payed_amount, student_number) Using a naming convention is harder (more typing, being consistent) but serves two purposes : - Making your database more readable and maintainable for other people - Helps you staying out of trouble in all dialects of SQL (the bug reported is an example of this) - Saves time in the end, since you can "guess" most of the key/fieldnames without looking them up So when i would design a table to store student information for my "adm" system a table look like this adm_students student_id first_name last_name birth_date Without a naming convention it could look like this studentlist ID Name lastName BirthDate FAQ ? So why not call the key field just "ID" and the name field just "Name" ? Because these fieldnames are reserved words in postgres SQL examples : the adm_student.name means the "name" of the table in PostgreSQL not the name of the student Using ID as a fieldname can also be very hard to identify in large SQL statements with a lot of JOINS ? Why use all lowercase separated by "_" ? Allthough Mysql and Postgres support case in table- and fieldnames is not recommended, if you would ever migrate to Oracle or DB2 you'll be running into problems. (these DBMS's only support caseless names (mostly displayed as uppercase) to use the undersquore is just personal preference, dash is also fine, but less common. http://phplens.com/lens/adodb/tips_portable_sql.htm is a good read on how to make valid sql for all kinds of databases, the excellent Adodb library is used for moodle, so no problem using for moodle code.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Bug? update 1.5+ 2005-06-18 fails!!!
ResponsesInList.Text:
I'm using Moode v1.5.3+. Forums were working fine, then today my IT department upgraded MySQL to v5.0.18 and my forums discussions disappeard as described above. I put Moodle into Debug mode and got the following information: Unknown column 'd.usermodified' in 'on clause' SELECT
p.id,p.subject,p.modified,p.discussion,p.userid, d.name,
d.timemodified, d.usermodified, d.groupid, u.firstname, u.lastname,
u.email, u.picture , um.firstname AS umfirstname, um.lastname AS
umlastname FROM forum_discussions d, forum_posts p, user u LEFT JOIN
user um on (d.usermodified = um.id) WHERE d.forum = '3' AND
p.discussion = d.id AND p.parent = 0 AND p.userid = u.id ORDER BY
d.timemodified DESC There is a thread in the MySQL bug discussion list that discusses the syntax of this type of query: http://bugs.mysql.com/bug.php?id=13832 Queries of the form: SELECT * FROM t1, t2 LEFT JOIN t3 on (t1.a = t3.c) Are expected to give Error 1054: Unknown column 't1.a' in 'on clause' Because the LEFT JOIN clause has a higher order of precedence than the comma. The way to fix this syntax error is to add parentheses as follows: SELECT * FROM (t1, t2) LEFT JOIN t3 on (t1.a = t3.c) Hence the earlier query becomes: SELECT p.id,p.subject,p.modified,p.discussion,p.userid, d.name, d.timemodified, d.usermodified, d.groupid, u.firstname, u.lastname, u.email, u.picture , um.firstname AS umfirstname, um.lastname AS umlastname FROM (forum_discussions d, forum_posts p, user u) LEFT JOIN user um on (d.usermodified = um.id) WHERE d.forum = '3' AND p.discussion = d.id AND p.parent = 0 AND p.userid = u.id ORDER BY d.timemodified DESC To fix this in the source code you need to modify the file: /moodle/mod/forum/lib.php starting at line 1296 to add in the parentheses in the query for MySQL. Hope this helps someone! Morgan

ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Sue, You have to modify the Moodle source code. Find and open the file: /moodle/mod/forum/lib.php On line 1294 you should see some code that looks like: 
```text
return get_records_sql("SELECT $postdata, d.name, d.timemodified, d.usermodified, d.groupid,


                                   u.firstname, u.lastname, u.email, u.picture $umfields


                              FROM {$CFG->prefix}forum_discussions d,


                                   {$CFG->prefix}forum_posts p,


                                   {$CFG->prefix}user u


                                   $umtable


                             WHERE d.forum = '$forum'


                               AND p.discussion = d.id


                               AND p.parent = 0


                               AND p.userid = u.id $groupselect $userselect 


                          ORDER BY $forumsort $limit");
```
 You need to add in parentheses as follows: 
```text
return get_records_sql("SELECT $postdata, d.name, d.timemodified, d.usermodified, d.groupid,


                                   u.firstname, u.lastname, u.email, u.picture $umfields


                              FROM 
(
{$CFG->prefix}forum_discussions d,


                                   {$CFG->prefix}forum_posts p,


                                   {$CFG->prefix}user u 
)


                                   $umtable


                             WHERE d.forum = '$forum'


                               AND p.discussion = d.id


                               AND p.parent = 0


                               AND p.userid = u.id $groupselect $userselect 


                          ORDER BY $forumsort $limit");
```
 Then save the file and upload it.  I hope this helps! Cheers, Morgan

ResponsesInList.Title: Looking at forums, vs. blogs, vs. journals, vs. assignments
ResponsesInList.Text: There has been some lengthy discussion about this, one very very long thread initiated by MD on blogs vs. forums. I wanted to throw out some ideas, that I think have not come out yet: After using moodle and a number of main activities (forums, assignments, journals (when available) ) I've come to see a lot of parallels. In comparing forums to assignments: Option of students writing text on the webpage; Forums yes Assignments one of 3 options Option of attachments by student assignments can be text but at expense of attachment, or vice versa. forums text WITH attachments optional (set by teacher) Option of being readable by peers forums yes assignments now Option of replies assignments yes (inline too!) forums yes Option of assigning grades assignments yes forums yes Quick grade/view/feedback options assignments yes forums no Threading assignments no... would it make sense? forums yes Forgive my sloppy notation- it's 1:44am and you know how that goes.. but it seems to me that in the spirit of the OO in moodle, what we have, especially as we add blogs to the mix, is one kind of object, that in fact just has a wide variety of settings: Create a new activity that is an ASSIGNMENT/FORUM/ BLOG - let's call it a DIALOGUE (if that's not already taken). Settings would go something like this: icon (assignment or discussion or journal or blog) public (for peers to see) graded (all typical grading options as in forum) allow inline feedback (for teachers) one per student or not(so each student sees THEIRS and THE REST, as in a blog, where the rest lists everyone) allowing replies subscribing (if public, but always for teachers, as with current homework) quick grading (I LOVE this add on to assignments) From a presentation standpoint, you could still have each of these named items, but they could functionally do the same thing, perhaps with different defaults- so a forum is a DIALOGUE that's public, with replies, optional grading, subscription options, etc.. A journal is DIALOGUE that's private, with optional grading, teacher subscription options, optional inline feedback, etc.. A blog id a DIALOGUE that's public, allowing replies, optional grading, subscription, etc... I suspect this whole conversation may be somewhat redundant with similar conversations- so forgive me for not being up to speed on all of them. It just started to grate on me when grading hundreds of assignments and forums how similar they are in functionality- yet how different the options and setup and interactions (from a teacher perspective) are. If anyone's interested in this angle, I'm eager for thoughts. d.i.

ResponsesInList.Text: Myo, When a person is subscribed to a forum it means that they will be sent email copies of every post in that forum (posts are sent about 15 minutes after the post was first written). ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Disabling mail copies of posts
ResponsesInList.Text: Mark, You have choices that will affect how much e-mail people get, and they also can make choices about how much they want to receive. First of all, within their profile, their e-mail can be turned on or off. If it is off, they will receive no e-mail from the site. Secondly, there is a News Forum in the top of every moodle to which everyone is automatically subscribed. This can be hidden if you don't want it, but it is useful for sending messages to the entire group for many things. Then, as editing teacher, when you add forums, you will set them either as "Everyone is subscribed" or "Everyone can choose to be subscribed". If you choose to subscribe everyone, then everyone will receive every e-mail. If you choose the latter, then they will choose to receive the forum messages that interest them. Hope this helps! Moodle on!

ResponsesInList.Title: Default setting
ResponsesInList.Text: Is there a way to set the default in a forum or for the whole course so all member do not receive e-mails for every forum post? I know each member can set that individually, but is there a way to do it for the whole course? Sorry for the simple question - thanks, Lauren

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Default setting
ResponsesInList.Text: Lauren, Like you pointed out, that is controlled by the setting each student has in their profile. At the forum level, you can force everyone to be subscribed, but you can't force everyone to be unsubscribed. By default, everyone's profile is set to subscribe them to any forum they post to...the Forum auto-subscribe setting. So, when a student posts to a forum they get subscribed and most don't realize it....even though there is a statement at the bottom of the posting screen, most don't even see it. I solved this problem on my sites by changing the Forum auto-subscribe value in the mdl_users table of the database from 1 to 0. This makes the default setting for Forum auto-subscribe in the user profile "No: Don't automatically subscribe me to forums". Changing this value won't impact any existing user profiles, but it will change the default value for any new accounts. Your existing users will need to change it for themselves, unless you are comfortable doing a query on the database to change all of them. Steve

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Separate forums for different groups inside a class
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Robert, In your course settings, set your group mode to separate groups. If your course settings are set to force the group mode (force = yes), then all activities in the course will automatically be separate. If you set the course settings group mode to force = no, you will have to set the group mode in the forum settings to separate. Then, the group members will only see each other's posts in that forum.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Editing a forum post after the 30 minutes deadline
ResponsesInList.Text: Well, I've got the same problem - I need to allow teachers to edit posts even after 30 minutes. So, I've got your idea and here's the solution that allows teachers to edit posts inside their courses: 3 files are affected: /config.php /mod/forum/lib.php /mod/forum/post.php Changes are shown with bold blue text; normal code in blue. In /config.php you need to add one line (I suggest after $CFG->adminedit): $CFG->teachereditalways = true; -by this we show that we allow teachers to edit forum posts inside their courses. In /mod/forum/lib.php : Goto line 1555 , add new variable $teachersuperedit in the end of the line so that it should look like: static $stredit, $strdelete, $strreply, $strparent, $strprune, $strpruneheading, $threadedmode, $isteacher, $adminedit, $teachersuperedit ; Goto line 1568 , it should be $adminedit = (isadmin() and !empty($CFG->admineditalways)); Insert a line after it: $teachersuperedit = (isteacher($courseid) and !empty($CFG->teachereditalways)); Goto line 1698 , add conditions in lines 1698, 1699 as below: if ($ownpost or $adminedit or $teachersuperedit ) { if (($age < $CFG->maxeditingtime) or $adminedit or $teachersuperedit ) { In /mod/forum/post.php Goto line 286 , it should be $adminedit = (isadmin() and !empty($CFG->admineditalways)); Insert a line after it: $teachersuperedit = (isteacher($courseid) and !empty($CFG->teachereditalways)); Goto line 291 , add condition as below: if ( (($post->userid <> $USER->id) and !$adminedit) or (($post->userid <> $USER->id) and !teachersuperedit)) { Goto line 294 , add condition as below: if ( (((time() - $post->created) > $CFG->maxeditingtime) and !$adminedit) or (((time() - $post->created) > $CFG->maxeditingtime) and !$teachersuperedit)) { That's all. Now teachers can always edit all posts in their courses. P.S. Admin user will have possibilities to edit posts only if $CFG->admineditalways is set. If only $CFG->teachereditalways is set, they will get an error "you can't edit other peoples' posts" , although admin can always delete the post. Hope that helps

ResponsesInList.Title: Document contains no data error message
ResponsesInList.Text: I had a 500kb limit on file attachments in one of my forums, and wanted to raise it to 6MB, which is the limit I set in Moodle.  The problem is, the setting does not seem to be "taking" and if I attempt an upload of any file larger than 500kb I get a "Document contains no data" error message.  The upload doesn't work and the system is mistakenly seeing an empty file when it is in fact valid.  Can anyone advise me how to fix this?  Thanks. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Document contains no data error message
ResponsesInList.Text: After worrying a bit that this was the wrong forum to post my problem, I did some checking in the General Problems forum.  Denis Cahalane made a post yesterday in response to a thread called "File Upload Issue."  He noted that the "Document contains no data" error message is related to an Apache configuration setting called "LimitRequestBody"  My LimitRequestBody setting was 524288 and in his post in the General Problems Forum Denis suggested increasing it to 10485760 (i.e. 20 times larger).  Both he and the person to whom he was directing his post found that increasing this setting eliminated the problem. Since they were both dealing with Apache 2 on Red Hat (same situation for me), the LimitRequestBody directive is in the following file: /etc/httpd/conf.d/php.conf.  I made the change to this file, restarted Apache and was able to upload a couple of 3-4MB files with no problem. Rick Danielson

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum icon is little green guy?
ResponsesInList.Text: custom icon located in your theme at : moodle/theme/"your_theme"/pix/mod/forum/icon.gif

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Forum icon is little green guy?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Each Moodle theme can either use the standard icon set located in moodle/pix directory & subdirectories OR its own icon set located in
moodle/theme/"your_theme"/pix/ directory & subdirectories. The choice is made in your theme's config.php file, line: $THEME->custompix = true; Erin, to know which is which you have to find out which theme your institution is using, whether it is a unique theme site-wide or teachers are allowed to choose their preferred theme for their own courses. Hope that helps, Joseph PS If the little green guy icon looks like the one below, then it means your institution have chosen the use the NUVOLA ICON THEME set. See this discussion about it.

ResponsesInList.Title: I want to add a forum for teacher access only.
ResponsesInList.Text: I want to add a forum that only my teachers can access and contribute to.  But I can't figure out what I need to do to succeed with this.  I know this must be simple, but......

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: I want to add a forum for teacher access only.
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Bill, You have two options (as I see it) 1. If the forum is for a particular course, this feature already
exists.  Under the course "administration" section there is a link
"Teacher forum." 2. If you want a forum for teachers but not course specific, try
setting up a course for "staff" and use and enrolment key to keep out
the students. Hope this helps. Jeff

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: I want to add a forum for teacher access only.
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Jeff, Option #2 seems like the more likely prospect for me.  I just set them up and assigned the teacher "students".  Fairly simple and straightforward.  Looks like this should do it.  Thanks again for the help. bill

Since there is a forum type 'teacher' I wonder whether it is a deficiency of GUI that does not allow to set up such a forum on a site-basis or this type is really restricted to be inside a single course (pretty much useless for us since courses have only 1 or 2 teachers here).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: I want to add a forum for teacher access only.
ResponsesInList.Text: You can make a minor change in enrol/enrol.class.php so as to make suggestion #2 easier to implement. Change the line: if ($course->password == "") { // no password, so enrol to if (($course->password == "") || (($course->password == 'isteacherinanycourse') && isteacherinanycourse($USER->id))) { Then create a staff course and set the enrolment key to: isteacherinanycourse Then anybody who is an assigned teacher in any course on your site will be able to enter the staff course without typing any enrolment key. [Security note: a student who guesses that you have set the enrolment key to 'isteacherinanycourse' will also be able to enter the course. If you are worried about that, replace 'isteacherinanycourse' by something else.]

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: I want to add a forum for teacher access only.
ResponsesInList.Text: I set to implement the #2 suggestion but then realized that I would really prefer to have the teacher forum on the homepage rather than as part of staff-only course. To test my earlier idea, I created a forum directly on the homepage. Then, I manually changed its type in the database from 'general' to 'teacher'. And... it works -- when trying to enter when logged in as a student, I get an error message that this forum is for teachers only I wonder why the popup menu for setting up new forums is so restricted. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: I want to add a forum for teacher access only.
ResponsesInList.Text: Upon further testing, I found that changing forum type in db was not enogh. I did not realize that Moodle homepage is also a course, so effectively I created a forum for teachers of that course only. However, the following changes seem to allow this functioning as intended (not fully tested yet, though) /moodle/forum/discuss.php /moodle/forum/view.php changed if ($forum->type == "teacher") { if (!isteacher($course->id)) { error("You must be a $course->teacher to view this forum"); } } to if ($forum->type == "teacher") { if ($course->id == 1) { if (!isteacherinanycourse()) { error("You must be a $course->teacher to view this forum"); } } else if (!isteacher($course->id)) { error("You must be a $course->teacher to view this forum"); } } Note that the error msg is hardcoded in English with only $course->teacher shown in current language. I have already entered this into the bug database.

ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rob, regarding "teacher logins"... the problem with creating a site-wide teacher forum is that strictly speaking there's no such thing as a Teacher Login on Moodle - teacher status is assigned on a course-by-course basis rather than being associated with the login itself. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: private discussion threads for teaching purposes
ResponsesInList.Text: A few options come to mind: Make everyone a member of their own group and use the invisible groups setting (depends how big your class is!). Online assignment with email alerts and resubmission on. Allows for private dialogue between student and teacher and has a grading facility (if required). Can't make public later and would require the use of some conventions to track changes over time e.g. you progressively copy and paste edited code down the page, use of colur coding etc. Wiki set for students and no groups gives individual wikis with clear edit and revert path. But no email alerts or grading facility. The old Dialogue module may useful, but the content boxes didn't have the HTML editor. Someone else may have better ideas. Moodle 1.6 will have a Q&A forum which requires a student to submit a reply to a discussion before they see anyone else's reply. But that only gives a 1-off restiction, not a continuous private thread.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: private discussion threads for teaching purposes

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Please explain advantages of Moodle forums vs Discussion Boards
ResponsesInList.Text: For several years I used forums and wanted more functionality directly related to education and I found that in Moodle. Moodle gives you forums and other educational related tools such as quizes, journals, and the lesson modules which gives you the delivery of content that depends on the answers given to previous questions. I suspect that the best forum software may be more featurful than the Moodle forum system, but the moodle system is specifically designed around education and is thus general preferable in teaching. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Please explain advantages of Moodle forums vs Discussion Boards
ResponsesInList.Text: Erin, You are right, Moodle forums do have far fewer controls than you have with vbulletin. If I were choosing between Moodle and vbulletin based ONLY on the discussion board features there would be no contest...vbulletin wins hands-down...as does phpBB...BUT, you have to remember...vbulletin and phpBB are only discussion boards...that's all they do (other than maybe a calendar and some other "bell and whistle" add ons)...they are not LMSs. The discussion board is only one feature of Moodle. The reason I use the Moodle discussion forums is because I like the Moodle LMS package...overall, it's a very nice LMS...the best open source one available, in my opinion. Bottom line for me is that I'm willing to "live with" the limited capabilities of the Moodle discussion boards for the advantage of doing all my class activities in one system. It's a pain to use Moodle for part of your class activities and another program like vbulletin for discussions...I've tried it and it was more work for me and more confusion for my students. Now...if you don't want or need an LMS and you only need a discussion board, then, in my view, I would go with phpBB since it's open source and is just as good as vbulletin. Steve

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sometimes "read" posts come back as "unread"
ResponsesInList.Text: I hit the same problem and here is my findings. There are 2 incidents that read records will be deleted: 1. ResponsesInList.Title: Function to initially hide others' posts
ResponsesInList.Text: While it is generally useful for all participants to view and respond to forum messages as they are posted, there are times when the first posting or two on a discussion topic covers most of what you, as the instructor, expect to be said on the topic. This leaves the other participants with little to add except to say "I agree". I have found in my own online teaching, that there are often a few bright and enthusiastic students who often jump in first with their postings. Or, if the participants span multiple time zones, those in an earlier timezone always have the opportunity to view new forums first and thus have the opportunity to respond first. I therefore see a need for "delayed release" postings, where students are requested to post their initial thoughts on the topic by a specific time and date, and until that date the only thing they can see in the forum is their own contribution and a message stating the deadline for initial posts and the current number of completed submissions. Also, since the publication of the post is delayed, students can be permitted to edit their submission up until the release date rather than the normal 30 minute (or whatever) editing deadline. How this could be accomplished. 1) This function could be a simple additional choice when setting up a new forum: (_) Do not allow other participants to see postings until 2) To accommodate this new function, a new field would have to be added to the _forum table: release_date

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Function to initially hide others' posts
ResponsesInList.Text:
Well, I've done it. It actually wasn't too difficult and the logic is fairly straightforward. Here is the explanation that I've placed in a help file: In some classes there may be a few students who always take the first opportunity to post their comments. Sometimes these comments are so comprehensive that other students no longer need to think deeply about the
question because the thinking has already been done for them. This feature hides the postings until a specified date, which means that students cannot rely on others to do their thinking for them. Once the release date has arrived, all postings become available and hopefully a more
fruitful discussion can ensue discussing the relative merits of everyone's comments. In some cases, if all submissions were sent out by e-mail once the release date has arrived, the students might be inundated with too many messages. Only check "Send out posts when they are released for viewing." if you feel
that the students should receive all messages via e-mail. This function allows all posts in a particular forum to be temporarily hidden from view of the other participants. Here is what the addition to the forum settings panel looks like: This is what a forum looks like when this function is invoked: It works like this: There are two new fields in the mdl_forum table, "hideuntil" and "sendhiddenposts". The value of "hideuntil" is usually 0, but for forums that are hidden, the value is set to the release date. "sendhiddenposts" is 0 by default but 1 if the teacher wishes all postings to be mailed out once the release date and time has arrived. All postings, except those of the current user, are hidden from view. A message at the top of the forum states: "There are now (number) posts in this forum. You may not view the postings of other students until (date/time) . The forum search function has also been modified so that non-teachers cannot search postings in forums that are currently hidden. The postings are marked as "mailed" even though they have not been send so that CRON will ignore them. Since these postings are not sent out until the release date, students are permitted to edit them until that time arrives. Each time the CRON function in mod/forum/lib.php is invoked the "hideuntil" date is tested for all forums, and if any are found where the release date as passed, the "hideuntil" value is reset to 0, which therefore permits anyone to view the postings in the usual manner. Furthermore, if "sendhiddenposts" has been set to "1", then all posts in that forum have their "mailed" value set to "0" so that they will be mailed out with this invocation of CRON. The attached zip file includes the above information with further details on which files and functions have been augmented. Please let me know if you have any problems with it or wishes for further functionality.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Function to initially hide others' posts-Database additions
ResponsesInList.Text: Sorry, I forgot to supply information on how to modify the database "forum" table. If your prefix is "mdl_" you can just run these two lines with your mySQL administrative application, otherwise, if you are using a different prefix or different database, please modify it accordingly. ALTER TABLE `mdl_forum` ADD `hideuntil ` INT(10) UNSIGNED NOT NULL default '0' ALTER TABLE `mdl_forum` ADD `sendhiddenposts` tinyint(3) UNSIGNED NOT NULL default '0'

My idea of a deadline, however, was to help keep the course "on schedule" since it would encourage people to post before the deadline and would establish a definite time when the students should go to the forum to read over, analyze and respond to the entire set of postings. Simply preventing those who haven't posted yet from seeing the postings might pose another problem: The postings would have to be mailed out only to those who have already posted, and it would be very difficult to make it so that everyone eventually received all of the postings as e-mail. With the current design, the postings can be sent out to the entire class (if they have all been force-subscribed) merely by resetting the "mailed" field to "0" when the dealine has been reached. I've talked about this with a few faculty members, and they are enthusiastic about this approach -- although one person did make the same suggestion as Martin as another alternative. This really ISN'T COMPLEX. The programming and logic are very simple.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: More ratings on moodle.org?
ResponsesInList.Text: I expect the problem with adding these kinds of ratings is that the scale is supposed to be unidimensional so that it will make reasonable sense for the gradebook to average all the ratings and give the result.  For example, it makes sense to say that "fairly helpful" is between "good information" and "not very helpful", but "I agree" isn't between "Excellent idea" and "You're welcome." To put it another way, ratings are presumed to be along some sort of scale, but it also makes sense to allow ratings that are not necessarily positions along a scale.  Perhaps another type of ratings needs to be defined ("Unscaled"), and for gradebook output it would send the number of posts submitted to that forum for each user rather than an average (I can't see what else would make sense). Jim.

ResponsesInList.Title: Problem with ratings code
ResponsesInList.Text: I just ran into a conflict between the ratings code and my annotation extension for the discussion forums. The problem is that there is a button inside each forum post which a user clicks on to create an annotation. When ratings are in use, clicking on that button submits the ratings and brings up the "Rating saved" page - even though the user didn't click on the ratings. The button in question is not a submit button, just a regular button with an onclick handler. Looking at the code, I see a form wrapping the all the posts, and this form actually performs the ratings. Why it's picking up my button click I don't know. It would probably also have problems with any other buttons within a message. I realize ratings are part of the standard distribution and annotation is not, and I could probably hack the two to work together (either by rewriting how ratings work, or (possibly) by ensuring that none of my button clicks propagate). But I don't want to muck with the larger design of Moodle. It seems to me that this implementation is wrong - there should not be a form wrapping all posts on a page, or even all of a single post, for two reasons: Semantically, a list of posts is not a form. This restricts the potential to add forms within posts in the future. Who should I talk to about this?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Problem with ratings code
ResponsesInList.Text: I have modified annotation to solve the conflict with ratings. However, in the process I had some thoughts about how to improve the ratings and eliminate the form around most of the page. I suggest eliminating the "Send in my latest ratings" button at the bottom. Instead, submit ratings silently whenever the user changes one of the drop-down ratings controls. This is easy to do with XMLHttp; the only reason against (at least that I can think of) it is the lack of support in older browsers (support is in IE 5, Firefox 1, Opera 7.6, and Safari 1.2).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Is there a way to keep forum posts from reordering
ResponsesInList.Text: I agree James...in my opinion, the way the discussion forums function, and the way you can manage and configure them, is one area where Blackboard does have an advantage over Moodle. It's very inefficient, (in my opinion and from my experience), to create a separate single topic forum for each discussion question. It makes a lot more sense, and is a lot more manageble, to create one discussion forum (where the teacher is the only one who can start new threads) for a particular module, topic, week, etc. and place all discussion threads in that one forum. Then, have those threads stay put throughout the discussion. Also, it would really help to be able to mass delete posts to the threads. That would allow us to build a course with starter threads and then once a course is over, restore it for the next class and delete all the student responses while keeping the starter threads. Currently, that is a very tedious process and it's simpler to just post the starter threads in the new course. Again, just my opinion....I don't agree that it is generally accepted that newer posts should always be first. That may be the case in discussions like here on Moodle.org, but when conducting an online course, with students who may not be "technology wizards", having the threads shift order can be confusing and not necessarily desirable. Below is a screenshot of one of my past modules at the end of a two week period. It would have been nice to have DQ1 through DQ4 stay in that order and have Task #1 at the end for the entire period...setting-up separate single topic forums to achieve this is just too inefficient, so I put up with the shifting threads for the efficiency. On an end note...even though it may sound like it, this is not a complaint, just an opinion . Overall, I think Moodle is far superior to other LMS's that I've used and I very much appreciate the ability to use this great piece of open source software.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Block email autoresponders from forum participants
ResponsesInList.Text: Hmm, an interesting case from point of view of logic. I doubt that anything can be really done to prevent it. User's turning on autoresponder negates her privacy setting otherwise.Properly configured autoresponders should ignore forum and mailing list posts but many vacation-responders have no such an option and even fewer users know how to configure that if they even know they should do it. Have you checked the original mail headers if they were included in the autoresponse? I think that while the receipient has blocked her email from displaying in Moodle, you did not, so the mail was sent with your email address as sender, and probably also as reply-to, and that is what the autoresponder used. Possibly setting reply-to to noreply@yourmoodledomain could swart such a response from reaching you but a novice email user may also try to reply to it and wonder that you never got it. Plus, some mailers may use the from address anyway (some have a switch whether use from or reply-to by default).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Block email autoresponders from forum participants

My post was sent to her email address, and then the autoresponder came to me from her mail server and her address. Obviously if I had my email address hidden, then the autoresponder would have gone to noreply@moodle.org. Moodle is setup so that the forum posts come from the poster's email if their email address is visible and from noreply if they are hidden. What's the logic behind this?

You have received this email because you are a member of the Virtual Learning Centre at www.baillie.org.uk
'. get_string('unsubscribe', 'forum').'
'; } $posthtml .= ''; return $posthtml; } There's probably a much better way than hard-coding it, but I hope this helps until someone else chips into the discussion!

Some things I tried anyway: One thing to do is to only get the users for the course that have logged on since the $dateafter and leave the posts as unread for those who we haven't seen in a while. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Sticky Forums... Useful?
ResponsesInList.Text: I like the sticky concept - but I think there is a better solution to this problem. I like to create a forum for a class - or for a topic. In that forum - what I would like to do - is to raise a set of questions, each to be given its own topic, so that students/participants go answer that question - as if I were in a live class and asked it. They will be in a context in which others too will be talking - but only in regards to that question. I also like to ask a set of questions - in a particular order. So I get the students reflecting on one point - then move on to another, related, point. And they can build from there. This is what I do in a "live" classroom. In a forum - I can try and replicate this - if I can have some control over the ordering of questions. As it is now - any topic that is new is added on top of all previous topics. Thus the second question I ask - comes first - rather than the other way around. Furthermore - if a student starts a new topic - it now comes on top - and the questions could be all the way at the bottom. The solution I think is simple. Like with phpBB - you can have the forum administrator (the teacher or designer) create different categories. Each category having different rules. THe first category - could be used, in my example, for my questions. Under that cateogory - only the questions I pose (as topics underneath the category) will appear. The second category - could be used for new questions raised by students. And they could add them one by one - and have them listed chronologically (the newest at the top). At the same time - I would want to be able to EDIT the forums - as the administrator/teacher. To be able to edit in two ways, at least: 1) to edit the order of posts - so in my example of the first category - I could go in and reorder the topics in the order that I want the students to read them and participate; 2) to be able to edit content - for inappropriate materials. This function should only be granted to the teacher/administrator. The stickies concept could be added too - for the kind of "rolling" forum used in the second category - whereby some topic is of such importance, that it can be designated to remain at the top of the list.

ResponsesInList.Title: Slow forum read tracking
ResponsesInList.Text: Even in a quite small Moodle installation the forum read tracking in Moodle 1.5 slows down the display of the course page dramatically. I just tested it in a course with 100 users and a forum with about 60 discussions and 300 posts. It takes roughly 1.8 seconds just to process this one forum. Because the course has other forums as well  the display of the course page has become very slow. And each time the page is reloaded it takes the same time!  Why? Couldn't more of the processing be done at the time when users use the forum rather than at the time when the course page is loaded? Luckily it was easy to turn the read tracking off, but only after I figured out that this was the cause of the slowdown. I think Moodle 1.5 should either switch forum read tracking off by default or warn upgraders that if they experience a slowdown that the read tracking might be the reason.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Slow forum read tracking
ResponsesInList.Text: Exactly what I feared with the approach of storing "read posts" rather than "unread posts". Mike says he did comparative tests and the difference wasn't much, but I haven't tested it myself yet on a heavily loaded site (it's been OK on a light site like partners.moodle.com) More testing/improvement of this would be very welcome. We can look at optimising this further by caching some of the results in the session, or storing some of the calculations in the database in an intermediate form. Can database gurus please examine the indexes, too? If we can't improve it before release of 1.5 I will definitely make it default to being off. I'll leave it on for now to get more testing feedback.

In such way you can keep the whole thread open in a window and the answer in other in a "natural" way, without having to right click, etc. I understand that threading usually means branching and see the risk of fragmentation that Feldstein points out. But I think he is talking about "casual" or "general purpose" forum conversations. Where all contribute to all. But in some parts of education we do need branching, and been able to review arguments in the thread, why branching occurs etc. Moodle offers a "flat" format, but I use most the "nested", since I do see al posts (with scrolling) AND the tree. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: What's wrong with the Sakai UI (and Moodle's as well)
ResponsesInList.Text: Enrique, agreed this is a complex issue. However, I think Feldsteins suggestion of making branch or "tangent" posts new discussions is a good idea. A flat view of the original post, along with a view showing tangents allows for the creative flow that often emerges in real conversation, yet maintains the integrity of the original discussion. The threaded model can and very often does lead to a disintegration of the original subject when ambiguity and neediness creeps in. It can be difficult to keep on track with the original thread when branches that may not be relevent to the topic are all displayed with those that are. This isn't very intuitive.  At the same time relevant information often comes from tangent branches, so it might be nice to somehow merge just that kernel of relevence from tangent branches into the original discusssion. As an example, a bug tracker would allow for tagging of a discussion as a whole - where the problem is, what type it is - and then tagging of posts - additional information, potential fix. A question and answer forum might want posts to be tagged as question, further info, response. Getting this information hooked into the posts properly, along with linking the relationships, will allow us to start designing the informational display and the user interface. I could see a forum format the collapses the posts like gmail, and allows me to quickly open and close them while I'm editing. It would be great to have a personal scrapbook, that allows me to collect bits of information as I move through forums and other activities . These scraps would have appropriate informational ties back to their sources and would allow me to drop them into posts or other activities. Anyway, lots of thinking still to do...
